title: RFC 3977 NNTP section 8: OVER / LIST OVERVIEW.FMT / HDR / LIST HEADERS and :bytes :lines metadata
summary: Full text read from this verbatim mirror because WebFetch truncates the rfc-editor copy at section 6.2.4. OVER returns TAB-separated fields: article number ('0' for the OVER <msgid> form), Subject, From, Date, Message-ID, References, :bytes, :lines, then any extra fields LIST OVERVIEW.FMT advertises. Extra header fields appear as 'Name:full' meaning the whole 'Name: value' is in the field; metadata appears as ':name value'. HDR returns '<n> <value>' for any header or metadata item; a LIST HEADERS reply of a single ':' means the server allows HDR on any header.
metadata_fields: value transform: unfold CRLF, TAB->single space, NUL/CR/LF->space
LIST OVERVIEW.FMT lines: Subject: From: Date: Message-ID: References: :bytes(|Bytes:) :lines(|Lines:) Xref:full <Header>:full
HDR <field> accepts header name w/o colon or :metadata w/ colon; first occurrence only
GROUP -> 211 count low high group; ARTICLE -> 220 n <msgid>
CAPABILITIES labels: VERSION READER IHAVE POST NEWNEWS HDR OVER[ MSGID] LIST<variants> MODE-READER IMPLEMENTATION
techniques: :bytes per RFC may disagree with real article size (CRLF counted as 1, dot-stuffing/terminator included, or a different copy counted) - Atlas should treat XOVER bytes as approximate, not an identity key

Xref:full is present on nearly all servers as an overview extra; its crosspost group list is constant across one upload so it is a free grouping key, and per-group article numbers let you dedup the same article seen in multiple groups
HDR :lines vs HDR Lines distinguishes server-computed line count from the poster's (often faked) Lines header - a faked Lines header is itself a poster/tool fingerprint
new_for_atlas: Atlas keeps XOVER bytes but should request LIST OVERVIEW.FMT per server and pull every advertised extra field (Xref:full especially) rather than assuming the 8 standard fields; and treat HDR :bytes/:lines (computed) vs Bytes:/Lines: (claimed) as two different signals.

title: RFC 2980 Common NNTP Extensions: XOVER/XHDR/XPAT/XROVER/XPATH and LIST ACTIVE.TIMES / DISTRIB.PATS
summary: The pre-RFC3977 extensions most providers still implement. XOVER returns subject, author (From), date, message-id, references, byte count, line count, then optional fields per LIST OVERVIEW.FMT. XHDR/XPAT fetch one header across a range (XPAT with wildmat matching). XROVER returns just References. XPATH returns storage filenames. LIST ACTIVE.TIMES gives group creation time + creator email; LIST DISTRIB.PATS gives weight:wildmat:distribution.
metadata_fields: XPAT header range|<msgid> pat [pat...] -> 221 (wildmat on header value)
LIST ACTIVE.TIMES: group, create-time (unix secs), creator-email
LIST NEWSGROUPS: group + UTF-8 description; DATE -> 111 YYYYMMDDhhmmss
techniques: XPAT lets the server filter a header by wildmat server-side - usable to find all articles whose Subject matches an obfuscation pattern without pulling every overview row
XROVER/References chaining reconstructs reply threads even when subjects are randomized
LIST NEWSGROUPS descriptions and ACTIVE.TIMES creator emails are metadata about the group, not the article - useful for scoring which groups a release family lives in
new_for_atlas: Atlas groups via subject regex; XPAT-style server-side header matching and XHDR sweeps over arbitrary headers (not just the overview set) are a cheaper way to gather correlation keys like References across a whole group.

title: RFC 6048 NNTP LIST additions: COUNTS, MODERATORS, MOTD, SUBSCRIPTIONS, status flags
summary: Adds LIST COUNTS (name, high, low, est-count, status), LIST DISTRIBUTIONS, LIST MODERATORS (wildmat:submission-template), LIST MOTD, LIST SUBSCRIPTIONS. Defines the LIST ACTIVE status values: y (posting ok), n (no posting), m (moderated), x (no posting, no peer articles), j (peer articles not filed), =group (aliased to another group).
metadata_fields: LIST COUNTS: group high low count status (e.g. 'misc.test 3002322 3000234 1234 y')
ACTIVE status: y n m x j =othergroup
capability sub-labels: LIST COUNTS DISTRIBUTIONS MODERATORS MOTD SUBSCRIPTIONS
techniques: Group status 'm' (moderated) and '=group' (alias) explain why an article's Approved header or Xref group set looks unusual - alias groups collapse multiple names to one physical group, affecting crosspost-based grouping
LIST COUNTS gives article counts cheaply for deciding which groups to scan for a release
new_for_atlas: The '=group' alias and 'm' moderated status are edge cases Atlas's Xref-based grouping should normalize (treat aliased groups as one) and the Approved header as expected on moderated groups rather than anomalous.

title: RFC 8054 NNTP COMPRESS DEFLATE and the proprietary XZVER/XZHDR/XFEATURE predecessors
summary: Standardizes COMPRESS DEFLATE (raw DEFLATE RFC 1951, windowBits -8..-15, i.e. no zlib header). Responses 206 active, 403 cannot, 502 already active. Layer order MUST be COMPRESS then SASL then TLS. Explicitly names the earlier non-standard mechanisms XZVER, XZHDR, XFEATURE COMPRESS, MODE COMPRESS and criticizes them for compressing only server responses. Suggests level 0 for already-compressed blocks like yEnc.
metadata_fields: raw DEFLATE, negative windowBits (no zlib/gzip header)
names XZVER, XZHDR, XFEATURE COMPRESS, MODE COMPRESS as unstandardized prior art
techniques: Compression is a transport concern, but recognizing which mechanism a provider offers (COMPRESS vs XZVER vs XFEATURE) is needed to even read overview data from Highwinds-family servers that do not advertise COMPRESS
new_for_atlas: If Atlas speaks only plain OVER/XOVER it gets no compression on Highwinds/eweka (which offer only XZVER/XZHDR/XFEATURE); implementing those is the only bandwidth win there - see the Spottarr ADR finding for the wire details.

title: RFC 4643 NNTP AUTHINFO USER/PASS and SASL, plus the posting audit-trail recommendation
summary: Defines AUTHINFO USER/PASS (281/381/481/482/502) and AUTHINFO SASL (281/283/383/481/482). Section 5 recommends (by default) that the authenticated identity be recorded in an audit trail linking the identity to POSTed articles, done either by inserting headers into the article or via server logs - this is the origin of posting-account/logging-data trace data.
metadata_fields: audit trail: authorization identity linked to POST articles, via inserted headers or server logging
techniques: The spec's audit-trail recommendation is exactly what populates Injection-Info posting-account/logging-data and provider X- trace headers; those fields tie together all articles from one authenticated account even across random poster names
new_for_atlas: Confirms that posting-account (and provider trace headers) are per-account stable identifiers; Atlas can cluster obfuscated posts with random From/Subject by a shared posting-account or logging-data value from one ARTICLE fetch per candidate.

title: RFC 5536 Netnews Article Format: Injection-Info parameters, Path ABNF, Xref, obsolete headers
summary: The current article-format spec. Injection-Info parameters are posting-host, posting-account, logging-data, mail-complaints-to (each at most once; private params begin x-). Path uses path-identity with diagnostics and a tail-entry that may be 'not-for-mail'. Xref is 'server-name newsgroup:article-locator ...'. Message-ID max 250 octets. Obsolete headers: Lines, NNTP-Posting-Date (->Injection-Date), NNTP-Posting-Host (->Injection-Info posting-host), X-Trace/X-Complaints-To (->Injection-Info), plus RFC 850 Posting-Version/Relay-Version/Date-Received and son-of-1036 Also-Control/Article-Names/Article-Updates/See-Also.
metadata_fields: Injection-Info: path-identity; posting-host=, posting-account=, logging-data=, mail-complaints-to=
Path tail-entry often 'not-for-mail'; path diagnostics !! and !.keyword
mandatory: Date From Message-ID Newsgroups Path Subject
techniques: posting-host (poster IP/FQDN), posting-account (opaque per-account token) and logging-data (session id) are the three strongest cross-article identity keys for deobfuscating random-named posts from one uploader
mail-complaints-to and the Path path-identity reveal the injecting server/provider, a coarse grouping key
A faked/absent Lines header vs computed :lines, and presence of obsolete trace headers, fingerprint the posting software
new_for_atlas: Atlas keeps Injection-Info/Date but should parse out posting-host/posting-account/logging-data/mail-complaints-to individually as correlation keys, and record the full Path path-identity (injecting server) - these cluster obfuscated uploads that share no visible subject/filename.

title: RFC 5537 Netnews Architecture: Path diagnostic keywords and injecting/relaying agent header duties
summary: Defines Path diagnostics: !.POSTED (injection point, optionally with source FQDN/IP), !! (verified added identity), !.MISMATCH. (expected identity/IP recorded when it did not match), !.SEEN. (identity not checked). Injecting agents add Message-ID/Date/Injection-Info/Injection-Date and update Path; they reject proto-articles already carrying Injection-Info/Xref or POSTED in Path. Relaying/serving agents may delete/replace Xref. Duplicate detection is by Message-ID with an Injection-Date (or Date) cutoff of >= 7 days.
metadata_fields: injecting agent adds: Message-ID, Date, Injection-Info (SHOULD), Injection-Date (if MID+Date absent)
dup detection key = Message-ID; history cutoff by Injection-Date/Date (>=7d Usenet convention)
techniques: The Path .POSTED token marks the exact injection host and carries the poster's FQDN/IP - a trace identifier parallel to Injection-Info posting-host

Standard inter-server dedup is Message-ID only; Atlas 'twins' (byte-identical reposts) have DIFFERENT Message-IDs by design, so MID-dedup never catches them - that is why PAR2-MD5/yEnc-CRC twin matching is necessary
new_for_atlas: Parsing Path for .POSTED/.MISMATCH/.SEEN gives a second injection-host + poster-IP source independent of Injection-Info, and explains why reposts evade native dedup (new Message-IDs), validating Atlas's content-hash twin strategy.

title: IANA Message Header Field Registry: the 43 netnews-protocol headers
summary: Authoritative list of every header whose protocol is netnews: 38 permanent + 5 provisional. Includes the standard set plus Cancel-Key/Cancel-Lock (RFC 8315), Archived-At/X-Archived-At (RFC 5064), Original-Sender (RFC 5537), and provisional Face, Jabber-ID, X-Face, X-PGP-Sig. Marks obsoleted (NNTP-Posting-Host/Date, Also-Control, Article-Names/Updates, See-Also, Date-Received, Posting-Version, Relay-Version) and deprecated (Lines).
metadata_fields: standard: Approved Archive Archived-At Cancel-Key Cancel-Lock Comments Control Date Distribution Expires Followup-To From Injection-Date Injection-Info Keywords Message-ID Newsgroups Organization Original-Sender Path References Reply-To Sender Subject Summary Supersedes User-Agent Xref
obsoleted: Also-Control Article-Names Article-Updates Date-Received NNTP-Posting-Date NNTP-Posting-Host Posting-Version Relay-Version See-Also
provisional: Face Jabber-ID X-Archived-At X-Face X-PGP-Sig
techniques: A complete allow-list of standard header names lets Atlas separate 'known' headers from provider/tool X- headers (the latter are higher-value fingerprints precisely because they are nonstandard)
Cancel-Lock/Cancel-Key presence and scheme is a poster-software fingerprint; X-PGP-Sig/X-Face/Face are rarer still and strongly identify specific agents
new_for_atlas: Atlas keeps a handful of headers from one ARTICLE; this registry is the full target list, and flags which are obsolete (so their presence dates the posting software) and which standard ones Atlas is not yet collecting (Cancel-Lock, Archive, Archived-At, Original-Sender, Supersedes, Control, Distribution, Followup-To).

title: yEnc 1.3 draft: =ybegin / =ypart / =yend fields, escaping, multipart and subject conventions
summary: Read from the sabctools mirror (yenc.org and archive.org both blocked). Encoding is O=(I+42)%256; critical chars NUL/LF/CR/'=' are escaped as '='+(c+64)%256 (TAB dropped as critical in 1.2; leading/trailing TAB/SPACE and leading '.' may be escaped). Keyword lines start '=y'. =ybegin has line=, size=, name= (name MUST be last) plus part=/total= for multipart; =ypart has begin=/end= (1-based byte offsets into the original file); =yend has size=, part=, pcrc32= (this part), crc32= (whole file, on last part). Subject conventions give the filename-in-quotes + '(part/total)' + size form.
metadata_fields: name may hold non-ASCII/control chars, up to ~256; decoders strip quotes and leading/trailing spaces
max line= 998 (997 practical for NNTP); part size derivable from begin/end
techniques: pcrc32 per part and crc32 of the whole decoded file are exact content hashes: identical crc32 across two uploads = byte-identical twin even with different Message-IDs/subjects/filenames
begin/end give each part's byte range, so you can detect floating (variable) part sizes and reassemble out of order; a part whose yend size != (end-begin+1) is corrupt
name= in yEnc survives subject obfuscation: when the subject is random, the real filename is often still in the yEnc header of the first part
new_for_atlas: Atlas already parses these fields; the spec confirms crc32 (whole-file) is the strongest twin key, name= is an obfuscation-resistant filename source, and part begin/end supports reassembly of floating-size multiparts - worth storing per-part pcrc32 for partial-twin detection.

title: yEnc experiences / V2 proposals (yEnc-Notes3): =ybegin2, compression, floating sizes, =ydata
summary: Helbing's companion notes. Confirms there is no deployed yEnc V2; future keyword would be '=ybegin2' or '=y2begin' (scan for '=ybegin ' with trailing space to avoid version clashes). Proposed-but-never-shipped V2 features: variable offset/escape (offset=/escape=/escoff=), compression (comp=zip/bzip), Unicode filenames. Decoders must skip stray '=y***' lines (abandoned =ydata database lines). Multipart parts may have floating sizes; last part end= equals size=.
metadata_fields: detection: scan '=ybegin ' (trailing space); '=ybegin2'/'=y2begin' reserved for V2
never-shipped V2 params: offset= escape= escoff= comp=zip/bzip, unicode name
floating multipart sizes legal; recommended fixed source-bytes per part
techniques: Robust yEnc scanning must look for '=ybegin ' with a space and tolerate stray =y lines, or obfuscation tools that pad/mangle around the keyword line can break naive parsers
Knowing V2 was never deployed means any real-world '=ybegin2'/odd offset= is almost certainly a custom/obfuscation tool fingerprint, not standard yEnc
new_for_atlas: Hardening Atlas's yEnc scanner to the '=ybegin '-with-space rule and stray-=y-line skipping protects against malformed/obfuscated posts; and offset=/escape= if ever seen flags a nonstandard encoder worth fingerprinting.

title: NZB 1.1 format spec (newzbin DTD) with head/meta types
summary: The NZB 1.1 spec mirrored from newzbin. DOCTYPE '-//newzBin//DTD NZB 1.1//EN', xmlns http://www.newzbin.com/DTD/2003/nzb. <head> holds <meta type=...> with defined types title, tag, category, password (case-sensitive; private types prefixed X-; multiple tags/passwords allowed by repeating the element). <file poster date subject> where poster=From, date=unix time the server saw the article (unreliable), subject has the segment counter replaced with (1/yy). <segments><segment bytes number>MessageID-without-brackets</segment>.
metadata_fields: head/meta types: title, tag(multi), category, password(multi), X-<private>
techniques: meta password / title / category / tag carry indexer- and poster-supplied release metadata directly - password meta names the archive password needed to deobfuscate encrypted RARs
Reconstructing the full subject from <file subject> + segment @number lets you re-derive the (n/m) counter and group segments into files even when the NZB was built from obfuscated subjects
segment @bytes summed per file and across files gives a size signature for twin/alt matching
new_for_atlas: Atlas should harvest NZB <meta> password/title/category/tag (password meta is the archive-decrypt key for encrypted-twin detection) and use per-file/total byte sums from segments as a size fingerprint alongside PAR2/yEnc CRCs.

title: SABnzbd nzbparser.py: NZB meta ingestion, md5-of-message-ids, duplicate-part detection
summary: Production NZB parser. Collects every <meta type> into a multi-valued dict; computes nzo.md5sum = MD5 over all article-ids (an NZB fingerprint / dedup key); computes avg_date/avg_stamp from segment dates. Rejects segments with size<=0 or >=2**23 (8MB) as 'strange'. Detects duplicate part numbers with different ids and counts them as bad_articles. category meta maps to a category via cat_convert; first password meta becomes the job password.
metadata_fields: md5sum = MD5(concatenated article-ids) - NZB-level dedup fingerprint
duplicate part detection by partnum with differing ids
techniques: MD5 over the sorted article-id set is a cheap NZB-identity/dedup key: two NZBs with the same segments are the same post regardless of meta
Average segment date is a more stable post timestamp than any single article date (resists a few spoofed dates)
Per-file ordering sorts segments by part number to rebuild files from scrambled NZBs
new_for_atlas: A content hash over article-ids gives Atlas an NZB-level dedup key; average-date is a robust release timestamp; and the 8MB/part sanity bound plus duplicate-part detection are practical ingestion guards.

title: SABnzbd deobfuscate_filenames.py: is_probably_obfuscated heuristics and par2-driven rename
summary: The canonical obfuscated-filename classifier. is_probably_obfuscated() returns True for: exactly 32 hex chars; 40+ lowercase hex/dot chars; 30+ hex plus >=2 [bracketed] groups; starts 'abc.xyz'. Returns False (clean) for: >=2 upper + >=2 lower + >=1 space/dot/underscore; >=3 space-dots; >=4 letters + >=4 digits + space-dot; capitalized with upper/lower<=0.25. Default is obfuscated. recover_par2_names() parses par2 and renames by matching each file's MD5-of-first-16k to the par2 FileDesc hash16k; get_biggest_file() picks the main file only if >3x the next.
metadata_fields: clean signals: upper>=2&lower>=2&spacedots>=1 ; spacedots>=3 ; letters>=4&digits>=4&spacedots>=1 ; Capitalized&upper/lower<=0.25
rename key: md5(first 16384 bytes) == par2 FileDesc hash16k
techniques: Ready-to-port character-class heuristic for deciding whether a filename is obfuscated (hex-blob, bracket-noise, abc.xyz vs human-readable)
par2 hash16k rename: md5 of the first 16KB of a file matched against the par2 FileDesc 16k hash recovers the true filename when subjects/names are random - works even on a file with a garbage name
Biggest-file-by-3x rule identifies the payload file among samples/txt/nfo so only the main file is renamed
new_for_atlas: Atlas reads PAR2 Main/FileDesc/UniFileN but can add this exact obfuscation classifier and the md5-of-first-16k -> par2 hash16k rename to deobfuscate random inner names; the heuristic thresholds and excluded-extension list are directly reusable.

title: SABnzbd par2file.py: PAR2 packet parsing and CRC32 reconstruction from IFSC slices
summary: Parses PAR2 by scanning for 'PAR2\x00PKT' headers (8B magic, 8B length, 16B packet-MD5, 16B recovery-set-id, 16B type). Handles Main ('PAR 2.0\0Main\0\0\0\0': slice_size u64, nr_files u32), FileDesc ('...FileDesc': fileid=data[32:48], md5=48:64, hash16k=64:80, filesize=80:88, name=88:), Creator ('...Creator\0'), IFSC ('...IFSC\0\0\0\0': per-slice 16B md5 + 4B crc32). It reconstructs each file's whole-file CRC32 from the per-slice CRC32s using crc32_multiply/combine/zero_unpad with coeff=crc32_xpow8n(slice_size) - yielding filehash without downloading the file.
metadata_fields: packet header: PAR2\x00PKT | len u64 | md5 16 | setid 16 | type 16
FileDesc: fileid 16, md5 16, hash16k 16, filesize u64, name(rest)
IFSC: fileid 16, then {md5 16, crc32 u32} per slice
reconstructed filehash = GF-combined per-slice crc32 over filesize/slice_size slices + tail via crc32_zero_unpad
techniques: Combining IFSC per-slice CRC32s into a whole-file CRC32 lets you compute a file's content hash from par2 alone, then match it against the on-the-fly yEnc CRC of downloaded articles - identity without the full file
FileDesc md5 (whole file) and hash16k (first 16KB) are two exact twin keys; hash16k alone deobfuscates names (first 16KB rarely collides)
Creator packet text fingerprints the par2 tool (QuickPar/par2cmdline/MultiPar) - a release-tool signal
md5-of-16k collisions are tracked and such files excluded from rename to avoid false matches
new_for_atlas: Atlas reads Main/FileDesc/UniFileN; adding IFSC parsing enables per-slice CRC32 -> whole-file CRC32 reconstruction (match against yEnc CRCs for identity), the Creator packet gives a par2-tool fingerprint, and the 16k-collision guard prevents false renames.

title: SABnzbd verify_nzf_filename + quick_check_set: 16k-hash rename and CRC32 content verification
summary: During download SABnzbd computes md5of16k = md5(first 16384 decoded bytes) per file and builds nzo.md5of16k {hash:name} from par2 FileDesc. verify_nzf_filename renames a file when its 16k-hash matches a par2 entry; otherwise falls back to the yEnc name only if it is not obfuscated. quick_check_set (in newsunpack.py) verifies each par2 file by on-the-fly yEnc crc32 == par2 filehash AND exact filesize, and will rename an obfuscated file onto the par2 name when its crc32+size match a par2 entry even though the filename differs.
metadata_fields: rename priority: par2 16k-hash match > non-obfuscated yEnc name
quick-check match = (yenc crc32 == par2 filehash) AND exact size
par_hashes / crc donor tables keyed by hash and crc32
techniques: Live crc32 (from the yEnc trailer) compared to the par2-reconstructed filehash plus an exact-size check both verifies integrity AND assigns the correct filename to an obfuscated file in one step
First-16KB MD5 is the primary name-recovery key; the yEnc name is a fallback only when it passes the obfuscation test - preventing random names from overwriting good ones
new_for_atlas: This is the concrete pipeline Atlas's 'alts' (same inner file wrapped differently) and deobfuscation should follow: match yEnc CRC + size to par2 filehash to both confirm identity and recover the real inner filename, with 16k-MD5 as the rename key.

title: NZBGet RarReader.cpp: RAR3 and RAR5 block/flag constants for header-only parsing
summary: Self-contained RAR volume reader (no unrar lib). RAR3 signature 52 61 72 21 1A 07 00; RAR5 adds 01 00. RAR3 blocks: main 0x73 (flags VOLUME 0x0001, NEWNUMBERING 0x0010, PASSWORD 0x0080), file 0x74 (SPLIT_BEFORE 0x0001, SPLIT_AFTER 0x0002), endarc 0x7b (NEXTVOL/DATACRC/VOLNUMBER). RAR5 blocks: 1 main,2 file,4 encryption,5 endarc; file flags DIRECTORY/TIME/CRC; main ISVOL 0x01/VOLNR 0x02; vint encoding. Tracks m_encrypted, m_multiVolume, m_volumeNo, splitBefore/After and reads encryption salt (RAR3 8B, RAR5 16B + kdfCount).
metadata_fields: RAR3: main 0x73, file 0x74, endarc 0x7b; MHD_NEWNUMBERING 0x10, MHD_PASSWORD 0x80; LHD_SPLIT_BEFORE/AFTER 0x01/0x02
RAR5: types 1/2/4/5; MAIN_ISVOL 0x01, MAIN_VOLNR 0x02; FILE flags TIME 0x02 CRC 0x04
encryption: RAR3 salt 8B; RAR5 kdfCount + salt 16B => m_encrypted
per inner file: name, size, splitBefore/After, CRC
techniques: Parsing split-before/split-after flags across volumes reconstructs which inner file spans which .rNN/.partNN volume - needed to map an inner payload to all its article segments
Password/encryption flags detect encrypted archives (Atlas's encrypted-twin case) from headers alone, before any decrypt attempt
Volume number + new-numbering flag orders volumes even when filenames are obfuscated
new_for_atlas: Atlas lists RAR inner names/sizes; adding split-before/after and volume-number parsing lets it stitch inner files across volumes, and the encryption/password flags flag encrypted releases for the 'wrapped differently' alt case without needing the password.

title: NZBGet DirectRenamer.cpp: first-article content analysis, par2 set-id and hash16k from one article
summary: Renames obfuscated files mid-download by analyzing only the FIRST article of each file: a RenameContentAnalyzer computes hash16k (md5 of first 16KB) and, if the article is a par2, sniffs the PAR2 packet header to extract the par set-id, so par2 files are identified even when cloaked. When all first articles are in, it maps each file's hash16k to the par2 FileDesc Hash16k and renames. Only files whose first article is >=16KB (or single-article) get a hash16k.
metadata_fields: per-file hash16k = md5(first 16384 bytes) from first article only
par2 detection by sniffing PACKET_HEADER signature in-stream
par set-id extracted to group par2 volumes of one set
condition: article size >= 16KB or file has 1 article
techniques: You only need the first article of each file (first 16KB) to compute the rename key and to detect+group par2 sets - no full download required for deobfuscation
Sniffing the par2 packet signature in the article body identifies cloaked par2 files (renamed to look like data) by content, not extension
new_for_atlas: Atlas keeps headers from one ARTICLE per release; this shows the same first-article can yield hash16k (name-recovery key) and par2 set-id (grouping key) for streaming deobfuscation, and that cloaked par2 must be detected by signature not filename.

title: RAR 5.0 archive format (rarlab technote): blocks, flags, extra records incl. encryption, metadata, redirection
summary: Official RAR5 format. Signature 52 61 72 21 1A 07 01 00. Generic block: HeadCRC32, vint HeadSize/Type/Flags, optional ExtraSize/DataSize. Types 1 main,2 file,3 service,4 encryption,5 endarc. File extra records: 0x01 encryption (version AES-256, flags 0x01 check-data/0x02 tweaked-checksums, kdfCount=log2 PBKDF2 iters, salt 16, IV 16, check 12), 0x02 file hash (BLAKE2sp), 0x03 file time (m/c/a, unix or FILETIME, ns), 0x04 version, 0x05 redirection (symlink/junction/hardlink/filecopy), 0x06 Unix owner, 0x07 service data. Main extra 0x01 Locator, 0x02 Metadata (original archive name + creation time). Service names CMT/QO/ACL/STM/RR. Tweaked-checksum flag makes CRC32/BLAKE2sp key-dependent so they cannot fingerprint encrypted contents.
metadata_fields: block flags: 0x0001 extra,0x0002 data,0x0004 skip-if-unknown,0x0008 split-prev,0x0010 split-next
file time extra 0x03: mtime/ctime/atime, unix-vs-FILETIME flag, ns
redirection 0x05: 1 unix symlink,2 win symlink,3 junction,4 hardlink,5 filecopy
archive encryption header: ver(AES-256), flags(0x01 check), kdfCount, salt16, check12
main Metadata record 0x02: original archive name (UTF-8) + creation time
service header names: CMT QO ACL STM RR
techniques: RAR5 BLAKE2sp file hash (extra 0x02) is an exact inner-file content hash stronger than CRC32 - a cross-wrapper 'same inner file' (alt) key when present
The Metadata record's original archive name + creation time survive renaming of the .rar volumes and fingerprint the creating session
Tweaked-checksum flag (0x02) warns that CRC/hash on encrypted files are key-dependent, so they must NOT be used as twin keys for encrypted archives
new_for_atlas: Atlas lists RAR5 inner names/sizes; it should also read the BLAKE2sp file-hash extra (exact alt key), the Metadata original-name/creation-time (survives volume renaming), redirection records, and must skip CRC/hash twin-matching when the tweaked-checksum encryption flag is set.

title: unrar headers.hpp: full RAR 1.5-4.x (and RAR5) flag/type constant table
summary: Canonical constant source where codedread's RAR doc is mostly TBD. RAR3 MHD flags: VOLUME 0x01, COMMENT 0x02, LOCK 0x04, SOLID 0x08, PACK_COMMENT/NEWNUMBERING 0x10, AV 0x20, PROTECT 0x40, PASSWORD 0x80, FIRSTVOLUME 0x100. LHD flags: SPLIT_BEFORE 0x01, SPLIT_AFTER 0x02, PASSWORD 0x04, COMMENT 0x08, SOLID 0x10, WINDOWMASK 0xE0 (64K..4096K, 0xE0=DIRECTORY), LARGE 0x100, UNICODE 0x200, SALT 0x400, VERSION 0x800, EXTTIME 0x1000. Block types 0x72-0x7b. EARC flags NEXT_VOLUME/DATACRC/REVSPACE/VOLNUMBER. HOST_OS 0 MSDOS..5 BEOS. Subheads CMT/QO/ACL/STM/UOW/AV/RR/EA2. VER_UNPACK 29 (RAR4), 50 (RAR5), 70 (RAR7).
metadata_fields: MHD 0x73 flags listed above incl FIRSTVOLUME 0x100
LHD 0x74 flags incl UNICODE 0x200, SALT 0x400, EXTTIME 0x1000, dict bits 0xE0
block types: MARK 0x72, MAIN 0x73, FILE 0x74, COMMENT 0x75, AV 0x76, OLDSERVICE 0x77, PROTECT 0x78, SIGN 0x79, NEWSUB/SERVICE 0x7a, ENDARC 0x7b
EARC 0x7b flags: NEXT_VOLUME 0x01, DATACRC 0x02, REVSPACE 0x04, VOLNUMBER 0x08
techniques: LHD_UNICODE 0x200 means the file header carries a Unicode filename alongside the OEM name - needed to read non-ASCII inner names
LHD_SALT 0x400 + MHD_PASSWORD flag detect encryption; FIRSTVOLUME/NEWNUMBERING + volume number order multi-volume sets
UnpVer byte (29/50/70) dates the RAR version used to create the archive - a packaging-tool fingerprint
new_for_atlas: Gives Atlas the exact bitflags to detect encryption/solid/split/unicode and to order volumes for RAR 1.5-4.x (which RarReader-style code and the RAR5 technote don't fully cover), plus the UnpVer-based RAR-version fingerprint.

title: 7-Zip 7zFormat.txt + Methods.txt: property IDs, signature header, codec/AES IDs
summary: Official 7z format. Signature '7z' BC AF 27 1C, version major 0 minor 4, StartHeaderCRC, then NextHeaderOffset/Size/CRC (header lives at end). Property NIDs: kHeader 0x01, kMainStreamsInfo 0x04, kFilesInfo 0x05, kPackInfo 0x06, kUnpackInfo 0x07, kSubStreamsInfo 0x08, kSize 0x09, kCRC 0x0A, kFolder 0x0B, kCodersUnpackSize 0x0C, kEmptyStream 0x0E, kEmptyFile 0x0F, kName 0x11, kCTime 0x12, kATime 0x13, kMTime 0x14, kWinAttributes 0x15, kEncodedHeader 0x17. Methods.txt: 00 Copy, 03 Delta, 21 LZMA2, 030101 LZMA, 03030103 BCJ, 040108 Deflate, 040202 BZip2, 04F71101 7zAES(AES-256+SHA-256), 06F10101 ZipCrypto, 06F10303 Rar29AES.
metadata_fields: signature 7z BC AF 27 1C; end-of-file header via NextHeaderOffset/Size/CRC
NIDs: kName 0x11, kCTime/kATime/kMTime 0x12/13/14, kWinAttributes 0x15, kCRC 0x0A, kEncodedHeader 0x17
per-file: name(UTF-16LE), times, attributes, CRC32 (in SubStreamsInfo)
codec IDs: LZMA 030101, LZMA2 21, Deflate 040108, BZip2 040202, PPMd 030401
crypto IDs: 7zAES 06F10701 (listed 04F71101 region), AES F0 ciphers, ZipCrypto 06F10101
techniques: kEncodedHeader (0x17) means the 7z metadata (names, CRCs, sizes) is itself compressed/encrypted - header must be decoded before inner names are visible; an encrypted header hides even the file list
Per-file CRC32 in SubStreamsInfo is an exact inner-file key for alt/twin matching across differently-named 7z wrappers
Presence of 7zAES coder marks encryption; the coder chain (LZMA2+BCJ etc.) fingerprints the packing tool/settings
new_for_atlas: Atlas lists 7z inner names/sizes; it should also capture per-file CRC32 (alt key), detect kEncodedHeader (encrypted/compressed header hides the file list), and record the coder chain + 7zAES flag as packaging fingerprints.

title: PKWARE ZIP APPNOTE 6.3.10: headers, GP bit flags, split naming, and the full extra-field ID list
summary: The ZIP spec. Local header 0x04034b50, central dir 0x02014b50, EOCD 0x06054b50, Zip64 EOCD 0x06064b50 + locator 0x07064b50, data descriptor / spanning 0x08074b50. 'Version made by' upper byte = host OS (0 FAT, 3 UNIX, 10 NTFS, 19 OSX). GP bit flags: 0 encrypted, 3 data-descriptor (sizes/CRC in trailer), 6 strong encryption, 11 UTF-8 (EFS) names, 13 encrypted central dir. Extensive extra-field Header ID list: 0x0001 Zip64, 0x000a NTFS times, 0x000d UNIX, 0x0017 strong encryption, 0x5455 extended timestamp, 0x7855/0x7875 Info-ZIP UNIX uid/gid, 0x7075 Unicode path, 0x6375 Unicode comment, 0x9901 AE-x (WinZip AES), 0xcafe Java, plus many third-party IDs.
metadata_fields: signatures: LFH 04034b50, CDH 02014b50, EOCD 06054b50, Zip64 06064b50 / loc 07064b50, DD/span 08074b50
GP bits: 0 enc, 3 data-desc, 6 strong-enc, 11 UTF-8, 13 enc-CD
version-made-by host OS byte: 0 FAT,3 UNIX,10 NTFS,19 OSX
extra IDs: 0x0001 Zip64, 0x000a NTFS, 0x000d UNIX, 0x0017 strong-enc, 0x5455 ext-timestamp, 0x7875 unix uid/gid, 0x7075 unicode-path, 0x6375 unicode-comment, 0x9901 AE-x, 0xcafe Java
per-entry: name, CRC-32, comp/uncomp size, method, mod time/date, internal/external attrs, disk-start, offset
techniques: Per-entry CRC-32 + uncompressed size is an exact inner-file key; the UTF-8 (bit 11) and Unicode-path (0x7075) fields recover true non-ASCII inner names
GP bit 0 / 0x9901 (AE-x) / bit 13 detect encryption; the version-made-by host OS and extra-field mix fingerprint the zip tool/platform
Extended-timestamp (0x5455) and NTFS (0x000a) extra fields carry create/modify/access times that survive renaming - a session fingerprint
new_for_atlas: Atlas lists zip inner names/sizes; adding per-entry CRC-32 (alt key), Unicode-path/EFS name recovery, encryption-flag detection (incl. AE-x 0x9901), and the host-OS/extra-field fingerprint rounds out zip handling parallel to its RAR support.

title: WinZip AES extra field (0x9901): AE-1 vs AE-2 and the CRC-zeroing anti-fingerprint
summary: Defines the 0x9901 extra field: data size 7, vendor version 0x0001 (AE-1) / 0x0002 (AE-2), vendor ID 'AE', AES strength 1/2/3 (128/192/256), then the actual compression method (the LFH method is 99 to flag AES). AE-1 keeps the real CRC-32; AE-2 forces CRC-32 to 0 specifically so a CRC on a tiny file cannot leak its plaintext. Salt 8/12/16 bytes for 128/192/256; a 2-byte password-verification value is stored unencrypted (1-in-65536 false positive).
metadata_fields: 0x9901: size 7, version AE-1 0x0001/AE-2 0x0002, 'AE', strength 1/2/3, real method
AE-2 => CRC-32 field is 0 (deliberately); AE-1 keeps CRC
techniques: Method==99 + 0x9901 unambiguously flags a WinZip-AES encrypted entry; AE version tells you whether the CRC is usable (AE-1) or zeroed (AE-2)
Under AE-2 the CRC is intentionally 0 - Atlas must not treat a 0 CRC as a content key for encrypted zips; fall back to size + 2-byte verifier
The AES strength + salt size + AE version fingerprint the encrypting tool/settings
new_for_atlas: Directly relevant to Atlas's encrypted-archive case: detect 0x9901/method-99, read AE version to know if CRC is real or zeroed (AE-2), and avoid false twin/alt matches on deliberately-zeroed CRCs.

title: Parity Volume Set Specification 2.0 (parchive.github.io): every packet type and body layout
summary: Full PAR2 spec. 64-byte packet header: magic PAR2\0PKT, length u64, packet-MD5 (covers setid..body), Recovery Set ID (16, = MD5 of Main body), type (16). Core: Main (slicesize u64, nr-files u32, sorted recovery-set File IDs then non-recovery File IDs); FileDesc (File ID, whole-file MD5, MD5-16k, length u64, ASCII name); IFSC (File ID, then {MD5 16, CRC32 4} per slice); RecvSlic (exponent, data); Creator (client text). Optional: UniFileN (File ID, UTF-16 name), CommUni/CommASCI comments, FileSlic, RFSC, PkdMain, PkdRecvS. File ID = MD5(MD5-16k || length || name). Names use '/' for subdirs, zero-padded to 4-byte alignment.
metadata_fields: header: PAR2\0PKT, len u64, md5 16, setid 16, type 16
Main: slicesize u64, nr-files u32, File IDs (recovery then non-recovery, sorted)
FileDesc: File ID 16, full-MD5 16, MD5-16k 16, length u64, name
IFSC: File ID 16, {MD5 16, CRC32 4} per slice
UniFileN: File ID 16, UTF-16 name; Creator: client text
File ID = MD5(MD5-16k || length || name); Recovery Set ID = MD5(Main body)
techniques: Recovery Set ID (MD5 of Main body) is a single 16-byte key that groups all par2 volumes of one set AND, because it derives from slice size + the sorted File IDs, it is effectively a release fingerprint
FileDesc whole-file MD5 is the canonical byte-identical-twin key; MD5-16k deobfuscates names; IFSC per-slice MD5+CRC32 enables partial-file/twin matching and whole-file CRC reconstruction
File ID = MD5(16k-hash,length,name) means a rename changes the File ID but not the 16k-hash - match on 16k-hash, not File ID, to survive renames
new_for_atlas: Atlas reads Main/FileDesc/UniFileN; this confirms Recovery Set ID as a release-grouping key, IFSC as the slice-level key it is missing (for partial twins and CRC reconstruction), and that matching should be on MD5-16k/whole-MD5 rather than File ID (which renames break).

title: Parity Volume Set Specification 3.0 draft (PAR3): BLAKE3/CRC-64, chunk dedup, File/Directory/Root packets
summary: PAR3 draft. Header: magic PAR3\0PKT, 16-byte fingerprint (lower 16B of BLAKE3), length u64, InputSetID u64, type (ASCII 'PAR XXX\0'). Two hashes: rolling = CRC-64-ISO (locate shifted blocks), fingerprint = 16B BLAKE3 (identity). Packets: Start (PAR STA, block size + GF + parent InputSetID for incremental), Creator (PAR CRE), Comment (PAR COM), Data (PAR DAT), External Data (PAR EXT: {CRC-64, BLAKE3-16} per block), matrix Cauchy/Sparse/Explicit (PAR CAU/SPA/EXP), Recovery (PAR REC), File (PAR FIL: name, 8-byte rolling hash of first 16KB, option checksums, chunk descriptions), Directory (PAR DIR), Root (PAR ROO), UNIX/FAT perms (PAR UNX/FAT), Link (PAR LNK). InputSetID = first 8 bytes of BLAKE3 of the Start packet body. Chunk descriptions enable content-defined dedup with inline tails (<40B) and shared chunks across files.
metadata_fields: header: PAR3\0PKT, BLAKE3-16 fingerprint, len u64, InputSetID u64, 'PAR XXX\0' type
File packet: name-len, name, 8B rolling-hash of first 16KB, option checksums, chunk descriptions
chunk desc: length u64, BLAKE3-16 of chunk (or 0), first-input-block index, tail rolling+fingerprint+block+offset
External Data: {CRC-64, BLAKE3-16} per input block
techniques: Content-defined chunking with per-chunk BLAKE3 enables cross-file and cross-release dedup: two releases sharing chunks (e.g. a re-mux reusing streams) are detectable at sub-file granularity, far beyond whole-file twins
Rolling CRC-64 over a block-size window locates a known block even when data shifted (inserts/deletes) - robust against repackaging, then BLAKE3 confirms
File packet's rolling hash of first 16KB is PAR3's name-recovery hint, analogous to PAR2 MD5-16k; InputSetID groups packets of one set across files
new_for_atlas: PAR3 (when it appears) gives Atlas BLAKE3 content hashes and content-defined chunk hashes that move 'alt' detection below the whole-file level - two differently-wrapped or partially-edited releases sharing chunks become matchable; worth planning parsers for PAR FIL/EXT/ROO now.

title: RFC 9559 Matroska: Info/Track/Segment-linking element IDs for media correlation
summary: Matroska element IDs. Info: SegmentUUID 0x73A4 (random 128-bit, UUIDv4-like), SegmentFilename 0x7384, PrevUUID 0x3CB923 / NextUUID 0x3EB923 (linked segments), SegmentFamily 0x4444 (shared across a linked set), TimestampScale 0x2AD7B1, Duration 0x4489, DateUTC 0x4461 (epoch 2001-01-01), Title 0x7BA9, MuxingApp 0x4D80, WritingApp 0x5741. Tracks: TrackUID 0x73C5, CodecID 0x86, CodecPrivate 0x63A2, Name 0x536E, Language 0x22B59C / LanguageBCP47 0x22B59D, flags FlagDefault 0x88/Forced 0x55AA/HearingImpaired 0x55AB/VisualImpaired 0x55AC/Original 0x55AE/Commentary 0x55AF.
metadata_fields: DateUTC 0x4461 (epoch 2001-01-01, per RFC 8794 date type), MuxingApp 0x4D80, WritingApp 0x5741, Title 0x7BA9
techniques: SegmentUUID is a random 128-bit id set at mux time: two files with the same SegmentUUID came from the same mux run (a strong same-source key); PrevUUID/NextUUID/SegmentFamily link multi-file sets
MuxingApp + WritingApp + DateUTC fingerprint the exact muxing tool/version and time - a packaging-session signal that groups a release group's output

CodecPrivate (e.g. the exact SPS/PPS for H.264) is a near-unique per-encode blob: matching CodecPrivate across files is strong evidence of the same video encode (an alt key stronger than track layout)
new_for_atlas: Atlas parses MKV tracks/chapters/HDR; it should also capture SegmentUUID (same-mux key), MuxingApp/WritingApp/DateUTC (tool+time fingerprint), SegmentFamily/Prev/Next (multi-file linking) and hash CodecPrivate per track (same-encode key) - these push MKV matching past 'same film' toward 'same encode/same mux'.

title: Matroska tagging spec: TargetTypeValue levels and official tag names incl. IMDB/TMDB/TVDB IDs
summary: Defines TargetTypeValue 70 COLLECTION, 60 SEASON/SEQUEL, 50 MOVIE/EPISODE/ALBUM, 40 PART, 30 CHAPTER/TRACK, 20 SCENE, 10 SHOT, and the full official tag-name set. External Identifiers: ISRC, MCDI, ISBN, BARCODE, CATALOG_NUMBER, LABEL_CODE, LCCN, IMDB (tt+>=7 digits), TMDB ('movie/' or 'tv/' prefix), TVDB, TVDB2 ('series/'/'episodes/'/'movies/' prefix). Plus Temporal (DATE_RELEASED/RECORDED/ENCODED/TAGGED), Technical (ENCODER, ENCODER_SETTINGS, BPS, FPS, REPLAYGAIN_*), and many Entity tags.
metadata_fields: external IDs: IMDB(tt#######), TMDB(movie/|tv/ #), TVDB, TVDB2, ISRC, BARCODE, CATALOG_NUMBER
technical: ENCODER, ENCODER_SETTINGS, BPS, FPS; TITLE, CONTENT_TYPE, KEYWORDS, SUMMARY
techniques: An embedded IMDB/TMDB/TVDB tag links a media file directly to a canonical title id - the strongest possible content-identity key, turning 'same film' into 'same titled work' and enabling cross-release grouping by title id
ENCODER / ENCODER_SETTINGS tags record the exact x264/x265 command line - a per-encode fingerprint that distinguishes two encodes of the same source (alt discrimination)
new_for_atlas: Atlas's frame/audio matches only say 'same film'; reading Matroska IMDB/TMDB/TVDB tags gives an authoritative title id, and ENCODER_SETTINGS gives an encode-level fingerprint - both directly upgrade Atlas's media correlation beyond 'same film'.

title: mkvmerge statistics tags and identity-suppression options
summary: mkvmerge writes per-track statistics tags BPS, DURATION, NUMBER_OF_BYTES, NUMBER_OF_FRAMES by default (disable with --disable-track-statistics-tags). --no-date omits DateUTC; --deterministic <seed> produces byte-identical files (and omits the date). --segment-uid sets SegmentUUID (random if not given); --link / --link-to-previous set Prev/Next UUID; --title sets Title.
metadata_fields: stat tags: BPS, DURATION, NUMBER_OF_BYTES, NUMBER_OF_FRAMES (per track)
--no-date suppresses DateUTC; --deterministic omits date + fixes UIDs
techniques: NUMBER_OF_BYTES / NUMBER_OF_FRAMES / DURATION per track are exact numeric fingerprints of each track's content - matching them across files is a cheap same-track test without hashing frames
Absence of DateUTC or of statistics tags itself signals --deterministic/--no-date muxing (a scene-tooling fingerprint), while a present SegmentUUID that repeats across files proves shared origin
new_for_atlas: Atlas can read the per-track NUMBER_OF_BYTES/FRAMES/DURATION statistics tags as exact track fingerprints (sharper than 'same film'), and treat missing-date/missing-stats as a deterministic-mux signal.

title: ExifTool QuickTime.pm: MP4/MOV udta, ilst (iTunes) and Keys atom IDs incl. Apple store ids
summary: The most complete MP4/MOV atom map. UserData ©-atoms: ©nam Title, ©ART Artist, ©day Date, ©too Encoder, ©enc EncoderID, ©cmt Comment, ©xyz GPS, ©mak/©mod Make/Model, chpl Nero chapters. iTunes ilst: ©too Encoder, desc/ldes Description, tvsh TVShow, tven TVEpisodeID, tvsn/tves season/episode, stik MediaType, purd PurchaseDate, cnID AppleStoreCatalogID, atID, plID, geID, sfID iTunesStoreCountry, apID AppleStoreAccount (email), ownr Owner, xid ISRC, covr CoverArt, egid EpisodeGlobalUniqueID. Keys (mdta): com.apple.quicktime.creationdate, make, model, software, location.ISO6709, content.identifier, android.* make/model/version/capture.fps.
metadata_fields: ilst: cnID atID plID geID sfID apID(email) ownr purd xid(ISRC) stik tvsh tven tvsn tves egid covr
Keys mdta: com.apple.quicktime.creationdate / make / model / software / location.ISO6709 / content.identifier; com.android.{make,model,version,capture.fps}
techniques: apID (Apple Store account email), ownr (owner name) and purd (purchase date) in iTunes-sourced MP4 directly identify the purchasing account - a hard identity leak that links all files from one buyer

content.identifier / com.apple.quicktime.content.identifier pairs a video with its matching Live Photo / original-capture id; cnID/geID/egid are store/episode ids that act like Matroska's TMDB/IMDB tags
©too/©enc/software/android.* fingerprint the exact encoding app/device; location.ISO6709 + creationdate geotag and time-stamp the capture
new_for_atlas: Atlas parses MP4 tracks; it should also read udta/ilst/Keys metadata - especially apID/ownr/purd (account identity), store ids cnID/geID (title identity), and software/©too/android.* (device/tool fingerprint) - to correlate media beyond track layout.

title: ExifTool RIFF.pm reference: AVI INFO (LIST) chunks and avih/strh header fields
summary: AVI/RIFF metadata map. INFO chunk tags: IARL, IART, ICMS, ICMT, ICOP, ICRD (date), IENG, IGNR, IKEY, IMED, INAM (title), IPRD, ISBJ, ISFT (software), ISRC, ITCH, plus ICNM, IEDT, IPRO, IWRI, ISTR (starring), and many media-oriented ones (IMUS, ICDS, IDST, ISTD). AVI main header avih holds FrameRate, MaxDataRate, FrameCount, StreamCount, ImageWidth, ImageHeight; stream header strh holds StreamType, codec, StreamSampleRate, StreamSampleCount, Quality, SampleSize; strn = StreamName; dmlh = OpenDML TotalFrameCount; IDIT = DateTimeOriginal.
metadata_fields: INFO: INAM ISFT ICRD ISRC IART ICMT ICOP IGNR IKEY ISBJ IENG IPRD ITCH; ISTD(ProductionStudio) IDST(DistributedBy)
avih: FrameRate, FrameCount, StreamCount, ImageWidth, ImageHeight, MaxDataRate
strh: StreamType(vids/auds), codec fourcc, SampleRate, SampleCount, Quality, SampleSize; strn StreamName
techniques: ISFT (software) in an AVI names the muxing/ripping tool (e.g. VirtualDub/mencoder) - a packaging fingerprint; ICRD/IDIT give a creation timestamp
avih FrameCount/dimensions + strh codec fourcc + SampleCount form a compact technical signature of the video that distinguishes encodes of the same title
INFO INAM/ISBJ/IGNR carry human title/subject/genre embedded by the ripper
new_for_atlas: For older AVI releases Atlas should read RIFF INFO (ISFT tool, INAM title, ICRD date) and avih/strh technical fields as encode fingerprints and tool signals - the AVI analogue to its MKV/MP4 metadata parsing.

title: willglynn/nntp: concrete XZVER (yEnc+DEFLATE) and XFEATURE COMPRESS GZIP ([COMPRESS=GZIP]) framing
summary: Working Go client showing the two proprietary overview-compression wire formats. XZVER (Astraweb): the 224 response is a yEnc stream wrapping a DEFLATE stream wrapping the normal overview text, terminated by a '.' line after the yEnc/flate ends. XFEATURE COMPRESS GZIP (Giganews): enabled with 'XFEATURE COMPRESS GZIP' (reply 290); subsequent OVER/XOVER/LIST replies whose status line contains the magic substring '[COMPRESS=GZIP]' are followed by a zlib 'dot-response' (zlib-compressed, dot-terminated). Falls back OVER->XOVER on 500.
metadata_fields: XFEATURE COMPRESS GZIP -> 290; status line marker '[COMPRESS=GZIP]' -> zlib-compressed dot-terminated body
techniques: Decode path for XZVER: strip yEnc, inflate raw DEFLATE, then parse normal TAB overview rows - lets Atlas read overview from Astraweb-style servers
For XFEATURE, the only reliable signal is the '[COMPRESS=GZIP]' substring in the status line, after which the body is a zlib stream with the dot-terminator inside the compressed data
new_for_atlas: Gives Atlas the exact byte framing to implement XZVER and XFEATURE COMPRESS GZIP so it can pull compressed overview from providers that lack RFC 8054 COMPRESS - the dominant indexer traffic.

title: Spottarr ADR-0006: empirical XZVER/XZHDR wire behavior on Highwinds/eweka (magic-byte codec sniffing)
summary: Decision record from empirical probing of news.eweka.nl. Highwinds (eweka + resellers) advertises XZVER, XZHDR, XFEATURE-COMPRESS GZIP TERMINATOR but NOT COMPRESS. Despite the '[COMPRESS=GZIP]' label the payload is actually zlib (starts 78 01), not gzip - so trust the first byte, not the label: 0x78->zlib, 0x1f->gzip, else raw DEFLATE. The decompressed output is byte-identical to XOVER including the terminating '.' line (the dot lives inside the compressed stream). XZVER and XFEATURE+XOVER produce identical bytes; ratio ~3.88x. GZipStream can hang on a persistent socket because it probes for concatenated members; zlib/deflate give clean EOF.
metadata_fields: eweka CAPABILITIES: XZVER XZHDR XFEATURE-COMPRESS GZIP TERMINATOR (no COMPRESS)
label '[COMPRESS=GZIP]' is unreliable; sniff first byte 0x78 zlib / 0x1f gzip / else raw DEFLATE
dot-terminator is inside the compressed stream; XZVER==XFEATURE bytes; ~3.88x ratio
techniques: Choose the decompressor by sniffing the data block's first magic byte rather than trusting the advertised name - the label says GZIP but eweka sends zlib
Because the '.' terminator is inside the inflated stream, the existing line framer and dot-detection work unchanged on the decompressed bytes; no separate wire terminator to hunt
Prefer zlib/deflate decoders (clean EOF) over a gzip decoder that can block waiting for concatenated members on a kept-alive connection
new_for_atlas: For Atlas (Rust), implement XZVER/XZHDR as explicit siblings of XOVER/XHDR, pick the inflater by magic byte (0x78/0x1f/raw), and rely on the in-stream dot terminator - this is the only compression Highwinds-family providers offer and the label cannot be trusted.

title: INN innd.c known-header table and nnrpd post.c Injection-Info/Cancel-Lock construction
summary: INN's ARTheaders[] is a canonical enumeration of ~70 recognized headers with status HTreq/HTstd/HTobs/HTsav, including provider/tool headers Atlas may see: X-Trace, X-Complaints-To, X-Newsreader, X-Mailer, X-Newsposter, X-Usenet-Provider, X-Originating-IP, X-Original-NNTP-Posting-Host, X-Auth, X-User-ID, X-PGP-Sig, NNTP-Posting-Path, Cancel-Key, Cancel-Lock, Face, X-Face. nnrpd/post.c shows exactly how Injection-Info is built: path-identity; posting-account=PERMuser; posting-host="host:ip"; logging-data="<pid>"; mail-complaints-to=..., and how .POSTED is prepended to Path and Cancel-Lock/Cancel-Key added per authenticated user.
metadata_fields: INN header statuses HTreq/HTstd/HTobs/HTsav across ~70 names incl X-Usenet-Provider, X-Originating-IP, X-Original-NNTP-Posting-Host, NNTP-Posting-Path, X-Auth, X-User-ID
Injection-Info built as: <path-identity>; posting-account="<user>"; posting-host="<host:ip>"; logging-data="<pid>"; mail-complaints-to="<addr>"
Path gets '.POSTED[.client.host]!' prepended at injection; Cancel-Lock/Cancel-Key added keyed by username or ip
techniques: logging-data is literally the server PID in INN - combined with posting-host it narrows a post to one server process/session; posting-account is the authenticated username
X-Originating-IP / X-Original-NNTP-Posting-Host / NNTP-Posting-Path preserve the real poster IP even after Injection-Info masking - extra identity sources to collect
The header status table tells Atlas which headers are obsolete (dating the software) vs standard, and surfaces real-world provider X- headers to parse
new_for_atlas: Confirms the concrete construction of Injection-Info (so Atlas can reverse-engineer posting-account/logging-data/posting-host), surfaces additional real provider identity headers (X-Originating-IP, X-Original-NNTP-Posting-Host, X-Usenet-Provider, X-User-ID) beyond the ones Atlas keeps, and shows how .POSTED enters Path.

title: newznab-tmux NameFixingService: multi-source release renaming (NFO/Files/SRR/CRC32/UID/PAR2-16k/PreDB)
summary: The reference indexer name-fixing pipeline Atlas is porting. Distinct ordered sources each with a proc_ flag: NFO, Files, SRR (.srr/.srs), CRC32 (release_files.crc32), UID (media_infos.unique_id from MediaInfo), PAR2 hash_16K (par_hashes.hash), plus PreDB filename match. Each source finds 'donor' releases that already have a predb_id (or anidbid, or trusted fromname) sharing the same key, then applies the donor's searchname within a size tolerance (CRC 5%, UID 10%, hash 5%). It attaches the donor's predb_id when the key matches.
metadata_fields: sources/flags: proc_nfo, proc_files, proc_srr, proc_crc32, proc_uid, proc_hash16k, proc_par2
keys: release_files.crc32, media_infos.unique_id (MediaInfo UID), par_hashes.hash (PAR2 16k), SRR stored name
donor must have predb_id>0 OR anidbid>0 OR trusted fromname; size tolerance CRC 5% / UID 10% / hash 5%
techniques: Transfer a known release name onto an obfuscated release by matching a shared content key (CRC32, MediaInfo Unique_ID, PAR2 16k-hash) to a 'donor' release already tied to a PreDB entry - this is the core deobfuscation-by-correlation method
Require the donor to be PreDB/AniDB-backed and within a size tolerance so random collisions don't propagate a wrong name
MediaInfo Unique_ID (video container UID) is treated as a first-class cross-release key alongside archive CRC and PAR2 hash
new_for_atlas: This is the exact correlation graph Atlas should build: obfuscated release -> shared key (yEnc CRC / PAR2 16k-md5 / MediaInfo UID / SRR name) -> PreDB-backed donor -> inherited name+predb_id, gated by size tolerance; it names the specific keys and thresholds to use.

title: srrDB API + ReScene SRR/SRS format (zeebinz/rarinfo srrinfo.php): archive-crc, OSO hash, stored RAR metadata
summary: SRR (ReScene) stores a release's RAR volume headers WITHOUT the packed data, plus stored files (.nfo/.sfv), enabling exact reconstruction and name lookup. Block types: SRR header 0x69 (app-name flag 0x0001), SRR Stored File 0x6a, SRR OSO Hash 0x6b (file_size + 16-hex OpenSubtitles hash + name), SRR RAR File 0x71. The srrDB API (api.srrdb.com/v1) searches by keywords including r (release), archive-crc, archive-size, isdbhash, rarhash, store-real-filename, store-real-crc, imdb, nfo, srs; /details returns files[] and archived-files[] each with name/size/crc, where the real media CRC+size is under archived-files.
metadata_fields: SRR blocks: header 0x69, stored-file 0x6a, OSO-hash 0x6b, rar-file 0x71; app_name string in header
srrDB search keys: r, archive-crc, archive-size, isdbhash, rarhash, store-real-filename, store-real-crc, imdb, nfo, srs, confirmed, category
/details fields: files[]{name,size,crc}, archived-files[]{name,size,crc}; nfo/ endpoint; imdb/ endpoint
OSO hash = OpenSubtitles hash (filesize + checksum of first/last 64KB)
techniques: Query srrDB by archive-crc (the stored RAR volume CRC) or by archived-files CRC+size to resolve an obfuscated release to its scene name - but a valid match MUST be against archived-files (inner media), not the outer files[] (volumes/nfo/sfv), or you get false negatives
OSO hash (OpenSubtitles moviehash, which Atlas already computes) is stored in SRR and searchable - a direct bridge from Atlas's existing moviehash to a scene release name
The SRR app_name (reconstruction tool) and stored NFO/SFV give release-group and CRC metadata even when the post is obfuscated
new_for_atlas: Atlas already computes the OpenSubtitles moviehash; srrDB's isdbhash/OSO-hash search turns that into a scene-name lookup, and archive-crc/archived-files matching is a ready deobfuscation path - with the explicit caveat (from newznab issue 481) to match archived-files inner CRC+exact size, never the outer files list.

title: Nyuu uploader config + article.js: header/subject/Message-ID templates and obfuscation tokens
summary: A dominant posting tool whose output Atlas ingests. Default Message-ID is '${rand(24)}-{timestamp}@nyuu'; From defaults to user@hostname; User-Agent 'Nyuu/<ver>'. Subject/Message-ID/yenc-name accept tokens: {filenum}{0filenum}{files}{filename}{fnamebase}{part}{parts}{size}{filesize}{timestamp} and ${rand(N)}. Default subject '[{0filenum}/{files}] - "{filename}" yEnc ({part}/{parts}) {filesize}'. groupFiles groups similar filenames into sub-collections (mimicking indexers). --date can override Date/Message-ID timestamp/NZB time to obfuscate. article.js writes the yEnc header as 'total= line= size= name=' with pcrc32 per part and crc32 on the final part.
metadata_fields: default Message-ID ${rand(24)}-{timestamp}@nyuu; keepMessageId reuses it (same length required)
yEnc header order: total= line= size= name= ; =yend pcrc32 (+crc32 last part)
techniques: The Message-ID shape '<24 random chars>-<unix ms>@<signature>' is a Nyuu fingerprint: the trailing @signature and the embedded timestamp are parseable - and the timestamp ties parts of one upload together
yEnc name= is the real filename even when the Subject is fully randomized (Nyuu lets subject be obfuscated independently) - so the yEnc header is the obfuscation-resistant filename source
Recognizing tool-default subject/User-Agent templates classifies the posting tool and version, a grouping/attribution signal
new_for_atlas: Nyuu's Message-ID '@<signature>' + embedded timestamp and User-Agent are concrete tool fingerprints; the yEnc name= survives subject obfuscation (so Atlas should always prefer yEnc name over subject for filenames); the timestamp component groups an upload's articles.

title: ngPost obfuscation internals: random From, UUID Message-IDs, subject==Message-ID when obfuscated
summary: A widely used poster with a built-in obfuscation mode. In obfuscate mode each article's Message-ID is a per-article QUuid (Id128 format, 32 hex) with '@<idSignature>' (default 'ngPost', '.com' domain); the Subject is set equal to the Message-ID (so subject carries no filename); From is randomStdFrom() = 13 random alphanumerics + '@' + signature + '.com'. yEnc header is 'part= total= line=128 size= name=<real filename>' with pcrc32 per part. Non-obfuscated mode uses subject '"name" (part/total)'.
metadata_fields: obfuscated Message-ID: QUuid Id128 (32 hex) @<signature>.com (default signature 'ngPost')
obfuscated Subject == Message-ID (no filename in subject)
yEnc still carries real name= and pcrc32/crc32
techniques: ngPost obfuscation leaves the real filename and CRCs in the yEnc header while randomizing From/Subject/Message-ID - so content-hash (crc32) and yEnc name= remain the only cross-article links; this is exactly the case Atlas's twin (CRC) matching is built for
The '@<signature>.com' Message-ID/From domain (default ngPost.com) and the subject==msgid pattern are strong ngPost fingerprints, and the shared idSignature across one post's articles groups them
Random-From with a shared signature domain means From is useless as identity but the signature domain still groups a poster's output
new_for_atlas: Confirms the obfuscation adversary model: random From/Subject/Message-ID but intact yEnc name=/CRC and PAR2 - so Atlas should (a) group an upload by shared Message-ID @signature domain + close timestamps, (b) fingerprint ngPost by the subject==msgid + UUID pattern, (c) rely on yEnc crc32 for twins exactly as it does.

title: RFC 5322 Internet Message Format: msg-id and date-time (incl. obsolete 2-digit years, UT/GMT/military zones)
summary: Base syntax for the mail-derived headers Usenet reuses. Lists 3.6 header fields (orig-date, from, sender, reply-to, to, cc, bcc, message-id, in-reply-to, references, subject, comments, keywords, resent-*, trace return-path/received, optional-field). Message-ID is <id-left@id-right>, globally unique, recommended as timestamp+unique-value @ originating domain. date-time allows obsolete forms: 2-digit years 00-49 => 2000-2049, 50-99 => 1900+; obs-zone UT/GMT = +0000, US zones fixed, military/unknown alpha zones => -0000. Lines <=998 (78 recommended).
metadata_fields: msg-id: [CFWS] '<' id-left '@' id-right '>' ; id-right may be no-fold-literal '[...]'
date-time obsolete: 2-digit year 00-49->2000s, 50-99->1900s; UT/GMT/EST.. and military letters -> -0000
headers: Date From (mandatory), Sender if multi-From; References/In-Reply-To for replies
techniques: Robust Date parsing must handle 2-digit years and obsolete zone names (common in old/obfuscated Usenet posts); mapping military/unknown zones to -0000 avoids bogus timestamps that would scatter an upload's parts across time
The RFC's recommended Message-ID shape (timestamp + unique @ domain) is why embedded timestamps are so common in generated IDs - parse them as a grouping signal
In-Reply-To/References reconstruct reply/thread structure independent of Subject
new_for_atlas: Atlas must tolerate 5322 obsolete date forms when normalizing article dates (so an upload's segments cluster in time), and can mine the timestamp embedded in many Message-IDs as an upload-grouping key.

title: RFC 2046 message/partial + RFC 2045/2047 MIME: split-message reassembly, CTE, encoded-words
summary: message/partial (RFC 2046 5.2.2) splits a large message with Content-Type params id (world-unique match key), number (1-based fragment), total (required on last). Reassembly copies the outer headers except Content-* / Subject / Message-ID / Encrypted / MIME-Version, which come from the enclosed message. RFC 2045 defines CTE values 7bit/8bit/binary/quoted-printable/base64/x-token and base64's 76-char lines; Content-ID uses msg-id syntax. RFC 2047 encoded-words =?charset?B|Q?text?= (<=75 chars, whitespace between adjacent ones ignored) appear in Subject/Comments/phrases, never in msg-id/addr-spec/quoted-string.
metadata_fields: message/partial params: id (match key), number (1-based), total (on last)
CTE: 7bit 8bit binary quoted-printable base64 x-token; base64 76-col
encoded-word: =?charset?B|Q?text?= <=75 chars; allowed in Subject/Comments/phrase only
techniques: message/partial id/number/total is the MIME-native multipart scheme (parallel to yEnc (n/m)); the shared id groups fragments even with no subject correlation
Subjects are frequently RFC 2047 encoded-words - Atlas must decode =?utf-8?B?...?= before applying subject/filename regexes or obfuscation detection, or it will mis-read non-ASCII release names
CTE tells you whether a body is base64/yEnc/uuencoded before parsing
new_for_atlas: Atlas's subject/collection regexes should decode RFC 2047 encoded-words first (many real subjects are B/Q-encoded), and message/partial id/number/total is an additional multipart-grouping key alongside yEnc part/total for non-yEnc posts.

title: RFC 1036 + son-of-1036 (RFC 1849): control messages, See-Also split postings, Xref/Path/Lines
summary: Historic Usenet format still echoed by legacy posts. Control messages: cancel <msgid>, ihave/sendme, newgroup/rmgroup (need Approved), sendsys, version, checkgroups. Xref 'host group:number ...' is local-only. Message-ID must never be reused (>=2 years). son-of-1036 (RFC 1849) adds: Subject 'Re:' and 'new topic (was: old)' conventions; for large binaries it recommends MIME message/partial and a See-Also header listing the message-IDs of prior parts (deemed more correct than References for this); ~60000-octet article guidance; obsolete Also-Control/Article-Names/Article-Updates/See-Also.
metadata_fields: control: cancel, ihave/sendme, newgroup/rmgroup(+Approved), sendsys, version, checkgroups
Xref: host group:number ...; Lines: body line count; Path host!host!...
son-of-1036: See-Also = msg-ids of prior parts; Subject '... (was: ...)'; ~60000 octet guidance
techniques: See-Also (son-of-1036) and References chain multi-part binary postings by message-id - a grouping key for old posts predating NZB/yEnc multipart conventions
Control-message detection (cancel/supersede) tells Atlas when an article withdraws/replaces another - relevant to not indexing cancelled posts
The 'Subject ... (was: old)' convention explains topic drift in thread subjects
new_for_atlas: For legacy or archive.org-sourced posts Atlas may encounter See-Also-based multipart linking and control messages (cancel/Supersedes) that modify or withdraw articles - both affect correct grouping and should be recognized.

title: RFC 8315 Cancel-Lock/Cancel-Key: poster-identity-linked HMAC locks
summary: Defines Cancel-Lock and Cancel-Key headers (scheme:value lists; sha256 mandatory, sha512 defined, sha1 deprecated). Key K = HMAC(secret, uid+mid) where uid is an optional user id and mid the Message-ID; the lock = Base64(hash(Base64(K))). Injecting agents MAY add their own Cancel-Lock (server secret) for an authenticated poster. Multiple locks (poster + server) can appear.
metadata_fields: Cancel-Lock: <scheme>:<base64> [more]; schemes sha256(mandatory) sha512, sha1 deprecated
Cancel-Key: same scheme prefix + base64 key (revealed to cancel/supersede)
techniques: A server-added Cancel-Lock is computed from the server secret + the poster's uid+mid; while designed to prevent user tracking, a constant server secret means the scheme/format and any server-injected lock are a provider/software fingerprint
Presence and scheme (sha1 vs sha256) of Cancel-Lock dates and identifies the posting agent/server software
new_for_atlas: Cancel-Lock is one of the standard headers Atlas does not yet collect; its scheme and whether it is poster- vs server-injected is a software/provider fingerprint, and a matching Cancel-Key in a later article signals a cancel/supersede of an earlier one.

title: RFC 8143 + RFC 4642: NNTP over TLS (STARTTLS vs implicit 563, SNI, re-CAPABILITIES)
summary: TLS for NNTP. RFC 4642 STARTTLS: command STARTTLS -> 382 proceed / 580 cannot / 502 already-active; capability STARTTLS must not be advertised after TLS; after handshake NNTP state resets to just-after-greeting and the client SHOULD re-issue CAPABILITIES; 483 means a secure connection is required; MODE READER must not be issued while TLS active. RFC 8143 updates it: prefer implicit TLS (port 563) over STARTTLS (119), mandate SNI in clients, disable TLS compression, forbid RC4, follow BCP 195, verify server identity per RFC 6125.
metadata_fields: STARTTLS -> 382/580/502; 483 'encryption required'; capability STARTTLS (hidden after TLS)
after TLS: state resets, re-issue CAPABILITIES; MODE-READER not advertised after TLS
implicit TLS port 563 preferred vs STARTTLS 119; SNI mandatory; TLS compression disabled; no RC4
techniques: After STARTTLS the capability list can change - Atlas must re-issue CAPABILITIES post-TLS to learn whether XZVER/COMPRESS/OVER are available on the secured session
Prefer implicit TLS on 563 (SSL-strip resistant) and send SNI so multi-homed providers present the right cert
new_for_atlas: Operational for Atlas's NNTP client: use implicit TLS/563 with SNI, re-run CAPABILITIES after any STARTTLS, and don't cache pre-TLS capabilities - otherwise it may miss the compressed-overview commands a provider only advertises post-TLS.

title: SABnzbd par2file.py: PAR2 packet parser, hash16k map and whole-file CRC32 from IFSC
summary: SABnzbd scans up to 10 MiB of each par2 file for 'PAR2\0PKT' packets, checks each packet's MD5 and length, and reads Main, FileDesc, IFSC and Creator packets (it only counts RecvSlic). It builds a hash16k->filename map for renaming obfuscated files, and computes each file's whole-file CRC32 from the IFSC per-slice CRCs.
metadata_fields: packet magic 'PAR2\0PKT'; length must be a multiple of 4 and >= 64; packet MD5 validated
data = packet after magic/length/MD5: recovery set id data[:16], packet type data[16:32]
FileDesc: fileid [32:48], hash16k [64:80], file size <Q [80:88], name [88:] with NULs stripped
IFSC: per-slice CRC32 at [i+16:i+20], stepping 20 bytes from offset 48 (16-byte MD5 + 4-byte CRC per slice)
techniques: Whole-file CRC32 from IFSC slice CRCs: crc = crc32_multiply(crc, crc32_xpow8n(slice_size)) ^ slice_crc for each full slice; the last zero-padded slice is fixed with crc32_zero_unpad and crc32_combine
A hash16k value that maps to two different names is dropped, because it cannot rename safely
PROBABLY_PAR2_RE (.*)\.vol(\d*)[+\-](\d*)\.par2 groups par2 volumes by base name
The packet MD5 check rejects corrupt or fake par2 data before any name is trusted
new_for_atlas: Atlas reads Main/FileDesc/UniFileN but not IFSC or Creator. IFSC gives a whole-file CRC32 for every protected file from the small index .par2 alone. That CRC can be joined to yEnc =yend crc32, combined pcrc32, SFV lines and RAR file-header CRCs across releases (twins and alts) without downloading the payload. Atlas should also store the Creator string and drop ambiguous hash16k values.

title: SABnzbd deobfuscate_filenames.py: is_probably_obfuscated classifier and biggest-file renamer
summary: This post-processing step decides whether a filename is obfuscated. If it is, SABnzbd renames the biggest file (and files with the same base name) to the job name. It first tries to recover names from PAR2 md5-16k on the unpacked files, and adds missing extensions by sniffing content.
metadata_fields: file basename character-class counts (upper, lower, digits, spaces, dots, underscores)
sizes of all files in the job
md5 of the first 16384 bytes of unpacked files (recover_par2_names)
NZB content markers '!doctype nzb public' and '<nzb xmlns='
techniques: Obfuscated if the name matches ^[a-f0-9]{32}$ or ^[a-f0-9.]{40,}$, or has [a-f0-9]{30} plus at least two \[\w+\] groups, or starts with abc\.xyz

Not obfuscated if: upper>=2, lower>=2 and at least one space/dot/underscore; or spaces+dots>=3; or letters>=4, digits>=4 and a separator; or a leading capital with lower>2 and upper/lower<=0.25. Anything else defaults to obfuscated
Rename only when the biggest file is more than 3x the second biggest; skip jobs with DVD/Bluray folder structures
Also rename lookalike files with the same base name, and prefix .srt files with the biggest file's base name
Add a missing extension by content sniffing (puremagic, NZB detection, txt fallback)
new_for_atlas: Atlas has no per-file obfuscation verdict. Porting this classifier (and NZBGet's stricter one) lets Atlas decide when a subject or yEnc name can be a grouping key. When it cannot, Atlas falls back to hash16k/CRC/set-id evidence. The 3x biggest-file rule is a simple way to pick the payload file that alt matching should key on.

title: SABnzbd nzb/object.py + decoder.py: first-article md5-16k, filename priority and dupe keys
summary: SABnzbd queues the first article of every file first, and the decoder takes the md5 of the first 16384 decoded bytes (md5of16k) of the lowest part number. verify_nzf_filename then picks each file's name in priority order. Duplicate detection uses a guessit 'smart' key or an md5 over all segment message-ids.
metadata_fields: md5of16k = md5(first 16384 decoded bytes of lowest_partnum)
filename parsed from the NZB subject
guessit title, season, episode, year, month, day, proper (sorting.BasicAnalyzer)
techniques: Fetch each file's first article before the others, so the yEnc name and md5-16k are known early
Name priority: PAR2 hash16k map, then the yEnc name (only if is_probably_obfuscated is false and the NZB name is not .par2), then the NZB subject name
handle_par2 falls back to the PAR2 set_id when set names collide, and renames obfuscated par2 files to <setname>.par2
Smart dupe key: 'title/season/episode', 'title/year/month/day' or the movie title, plus 'proper'
Exact dupe: md5sum over the concatenated segment message-ids
new_for_atlas: Atlas fetches one ARTICLE per release, for headers only. If it decodes the first segment of each file and stores md5(first 16 KiB), it can join obfuscated files to any PAR2 FileDesc hash16k it has seen in any release. That names the files and links alts. A hash of the message-id set is a cheap exact-NZB-duplicate key.

title: SABnzbd newsunpack.py quick_check_set: rename by combined article CRC32 vs PAR2 hash
summary: QuickCheck verifies files without a par2 repair, and renames obfuscated ones, by comparing each file's CRC32 and size with the PAR2-derived hash. The file's CRC32 is built by combining the per-article yEnc CRCs. This file also holds the SFV parser and archive signatures.
metadata_fields: nzf.crc32: crc32_combine over article CRCs in decodetable order (finalize_crc32, run in postproc)
SFV lines (parse_sfv uses rsplit(maxsplit=1), so names may contain spaces)
techniques: Rename an obfuscated file to the PAR2 name when nzf.crc32 == par2info.filehash and the sizes match. This works even with no md5-16k match
Combine per-article CRC32s in part order with crc32_combine to get the whole-file CRC32
new_for_atlas: This gives Atlas a second content key besides hash16k. The whole-file CRC32 can come from PAR2 IFSC, from the last article's crc32= when the poster writes it, or from combined pcrc32 values. Matching it against RAR/SFV/PAR2 CRCs from other releases confirms twins and names obfuscated files.

title: SABnzbd postproc.py rar_renamer: order obfuscated RAR volumes from header volume numbers
summary: rar_renamer renames randomly named RAR volumes. It reads each volume's header (via utils/rarvolinfo.py) to get the volume number and inner file list. It handles several interleaved RAR sets in one job.
metadata_fields: RAR3/4 MAIN_VOLUME flag and ENDARC volume number
inner file list per volume (an empty list means fully encrypted)
techniques: RAR5: volume = main_volume_number + 1, named part%03d.rar
RAR3/4: volume from ENDARC endarc_volnr + 1; NEWNUMBERING gives part%02d.rar, otherwise .rar / .r%02d
Bail out if a set is fully encrypted; a single set is renamed directly

Several sets: a staircase check (per-volume set counts never increase), then chaining where the last inner file of volume n equals the first inner file of volume n+1. Sets are named 'A--<job>', 'B--<job>' and so on
.cbr files are protected from renaming
new_for_atlas: Atlas lists inner names and sizes. It should also store the volume number, split flags and first/last inner file for each RAR article it reads. With those it can order obfuscated volumes, count missing ones, and chain volumes of one set across random file names. That shows two posts carry the same RAR set even when every name differs.

title: SABnzbd assembler.py is_cloaked: RAR-in-RAR and password-named inner files
summary: While a job downloads, SABnzbd lists the first RAR volume and flags 'cloaked' content: an inner RAR named almost like the outer one, or inner files with 'password' in the name. It also tries the known passwords and flags unwanted extensions.
metadata_fields: encryption status and password test result
techniques: Cloaked if an inner .rar's name is a prefix of the outer name (length difference < 8), there are fewer than 3 inner names, and they are not subtitles
Cloaked if an inner name contains 'password' and its extension is not in SAFE_EXTS
Password trial: a RarCRCError containing 'cannot find volume' counts as the correct password
Flag unwanted extensions in the inner listing
new_for_atlas: Atlas can compute these flags from the RAR listings it already makes. Nested RARs and password-hint files are fake/spam signals, and they should keep a release out of twin/alt groups with real releases.

title: SABnzbd nzbparser.py + misc.py + urlgrabber.py: NZB meta, segment sanity checks, subject filename regexes, x-dnzb headers
summary: SABnzbd's NZB parser collects every <meta> type plus each file's subject, date, groups and segments, with sanity checks. misc.py extracts filenames from subjects and finds password notations. urlgrabber reads the newznab x-dnzb-* HTTP headers that indexers send with NZBs.
metadata_fields: file subject, date, groups; segment bytes, number, message-id
x-dnzb-category (or category_id), x-dnzb-moreinfo, x-dnzb-name, x-dnzb-propername, x-dnzb-episodename, x-dnzb-year, x-dnzb-failure, x-dnzb-details, x-dnzb-password
techniques: Skip segments with size <= 0 or >= 2**23; count duplicate part numbers that have different message-ids
avg_date across files; md5 of the message-ids as a dupe key
Try RE_SUBJECT_FILENAME_QUOTES "([^"]*)" first, then RE_SUBJECT_BASIC_FILENAME \b([\w\-+()' .,]+(?:\[[\w\-/+()' .,]*][\w\-+()' .,]*)*\.[A-Za-z0-9]{2,4})\b
scan_password notations: 'name / pw', 'name/pw', 'password=', '{{pw}}'
Accept gzip- and bz2-compressed NZBs
new_for_atlas: Atlas could add the x-dnzb-* headers to its own NZB API, and read <meta> password/tag/category from imported third-party NZBs. The segment-size and duplicate-part checks are cheap signals for corrupt or spliced posts.

title: sabctools yenc.cc: SABnzbd's C++ yEnc header parser and CRC32 math exports
summary: sabctools decodes NNTP responses directly. It parses =ybegin/=ypart/=yend with strict caps and fallbacks, and exports the CRC32 math (combine, multiply, zero-unpad, xpown, xpow8n) that SABnzbd uses for PAR2 and article CRCs.
metadata_fields: =ybegin part= (if absent, data starts on the next line: single-part)
=ybegin name= (last field; trailing whitespace and NUL stripped)
=ypart begin=/end= (1-based converted to 0-based; invalid values become 0)
=yend pcrc32= (preferred) else crc32=; =yend size= kept as end_size
decoder attributes crc_expected, bytes_decoded, baddata, lines, format
techniques: Use pcrc32 in preference to crc32 as the article CRC; keep end_size to check against begin/end
Size caps reject absurd headers from malformed or hostile posts
Exported CRC32 helpers: crc32_combine, crc32_multiply, crc32_zero_unpad, crc32_xpown, crc32_xpow8n
new_for_atlas: Atlas already parses these keywords. What is new: the size caps, the rule that a missing part= means single-part, and a CRC-math layer. That layer is needed to combine article CRCs and to unpad PAR2 slice CRCs for the IFSC and quick-check matching.

title: NZBGet Deobfuscation.cpp: subject filename extraction, IsExcessivelyObfuscated thresholds, hashed-release regexes
summary: NZBGet's deobfuscation module pulls a filename from a subject, including the [PRiVATE] newzNZB form. It scores filenames for excessive obfuscation with fixed character-statistic thresholds and an 11-regex hashed-release list. QueueCoordinator uses the score to decide whether to trust the yEnc article name.
metadata_fields: subject: first quoted string; without quotes, the word before ' yEnc', or the 'Re: ...(' form
filename token statistics: alphanumeric runs, capitals, vowels, digits, letter/digit alternations, case transitions
techniques: Thresholds: MIN_MIXED_ALNUM 10, MIN_ALNUM 12, MIN_CAPS 8, VOWELLESS 8, LOW_VOWEL 24 with vowels*5 < length, NUMERIC 16, alternations >= 6, case transitions >= 3, MAX_TITLE_LEN 32 for joined adjacent mixed tokens

Exemptions: part\d+.(rar|par2), vol\d+\+\d+.par2, and a single rar/7z/par name with an alphanumeric run of 16-256. Whitelisted: CamelCase titles, and all-caps tokens of at most 15 chars with >= 20% vowels
QueueCoordinator.cpp (around line 780): with FileNaming=auto, the yEnc article name is used only if it is not excessively obfuscated and ManyDupeFiles is off
new_for_atlas: A second, finer-grained obfuscation score with explicit numbers that can be ported to Rust, plus a parser for newzNZB [PRiVATE] subjects. Both decide when Atlas may use subject or yEnc names for grouping.

title: NZBGet NzbFile.cpp + DupeCoordinator.cpp + DupeMatcher.cpp: content hashes and largest-inner-file dupe matching
summary: When NZBGet loads an NZB it computes full and filtered content hashes over message-ids, fixes subjects that would all parse to the same filename, and reads passwords and names from the NZB filename and meta. DupeMatcher compares two downloads by the largest file inside their RARs and whether it is stored or compressed.
metadata_fields: subject and parsed filename per file
password from {{...}} in the NZB filename
meta password, category, name, title (name falls back to title)
'unrar lt' Name, Size and Compression lines
techniques: HasDuplicateFilenames: more than 2 files with the same parsed name but different subjects (or 2 if the NZB has only 2 files) triggers a reparse without quotes; otherwise subjects are used as names

CalcHashes: Util::HashBJ96 over message-ids, with files sorted by filename descending. FullContentHash, plus FilteredContentHash that skips ParIgnoreExt files (dropped if built from fewer than half the files)
DupeCoordinator: an equal full or filtered hash means duplicate content
