DupeMatcher: largest Name/Size from 'unrar lt *.rar'; compressed = a ' Compression:' line without ' -m0'. A match needs an equal largest size and the same compressed flag
SizeDiffOK(size, expected, 20): sizes within 20%
new_for_atlas: The filtered hash (ignoring extra par2/nfo/sfv) catches NZBs that differ only by extra files. 'Largest inner file size + stored vs compressed' is an alt key Atlas can compute from its existing RAR listings: the same largest inner size with -m0 strongly suggests the same payload, rewrapped.

title: NZBGet DirectRenamer.cpp: rename during download by first-16KiB MD5 vs PAR2 Hash16k
summary: During download, DirectRenamer hashes the first 16 KiB of each file's first article and spots PAR2 files by their packet magic. It renames files whose hash matches a PAR2 FileDesc Hash16k, and renames obfuscated par2 files by set id.
metadata_fields: MD5 of the first 16 KiB of article data (RenameContentAnalyzer)
PAR2 packet_magic in the first article; set id from PACKET_HEADER
techniques: Find par2 content behind obfuscated names by packet magic, without trusting the extension
BuildNewParName: keep an existing .volXX+YY.par2 suffix, otherwise name the file '<setid>.vol%03d+01.PAR2'
NeedRenamePars is true if any par2 lacks the .par2 extension, or one set id appears with different base names
new_for_atlas: With one first-article decode per file, Atlas can find par2 files hidden behind random names (by packet magic) and group them by set id. The same set id in two posts marks them as twins even when subjects and names are fully random.

title: NZBGet RarReader.cpp + RarRenamer.cpp: RAR3/RAR5 header reader with encrypted-header support and set rebuilding
summary: RarReader parses RAR3 and RAR5 headers, and can decrypt encrypted headers when the password is known. RarRenamer uses the volume numbers and split flags to rebuild RAR sets and rename obfuscated volumes.
metadata_fields: RAR3 main flags MAIN_VOLUME 0x0001, NEWNUMBERING 0x0010, PASSWORD 0x0080
RAR3 FILE SPLITBEFORE/SPLITAFTER, ADDSIZE; ENDARC NEXTVOL/DATACRC/VOLNUMBER
RAR5 block types MAIN 1, FILE 2, ENCRYPTION 4 (kdfCount, salt[16]), ENDARC 5
techniques: Header decryption: DecryptRar3Prepare(salt) with AES-128 for RAR3; DecryptRar5Prepare from kdfCount and salt for RAR5

MakeSets: a set starts at volNo 0 with a first file that is not split-before. The next volume must be multivolume with volNo = last + 1, and either its first file is split-before while the previous last file is split-after with the same filename, or both are unsplit
new_for_atlas: With an NZB/meta password, Atlas could read inner names from header-encrypted RAR5 posts, which look opaque today. The MakeSets rule chains volumes into sets across random names, so twin/alt matching can work on whole sets, not single files.

title: NZBGet ParChecker.cpp + ArticleWriter.cpp: quick par verification by combining IFSC and article CRCs
summary: NZBGet's quick verification combines the IFSC per-block CRCs into a whole-file CRC and compares it with the CRC it built while writing articles. With segment CRCs it can also check partial files block by block, and it logs the PAR2 creator.
metadata_fields: IFSC FILEVERIFICATIONENTRY.crc per block; block size
download CRC built in ArticleWriter.cpp (around line 600): Crc32::Combine(crc, pa->GetCrc(), segSize)
PAR2 Creator string ('Recovery files created by: <creator>')
techniques: Crc32::Combine over IFSC CRCs by block size gives a whole-file CRC, compared with the combined article CRCs
Partial verification maps good segments to PAR2 blocks by CRC
ParParser parses .vol+/- block counts and groups the par files of one set (SameParCollection)
new_for_atlas: An independent second implementation of the IFSC-to-file-CRC32 approach Atlas should add. Also store the creator string per release.

title: Parity Volume Set Specification v2.0 (PAR2): full packet layouts and ID derivations
summary: The official PAR2 spec defines the packet header (magic, length, MD5, recovery set id, type) and every core and optional packet. It specifies how FileIDs and the Recovery Set ID are derived, how volume files are named, the non-recovery set, and an example application-specific packet.
metadata_fields: header: magic 'PAR2\0PKT', 8-byte length, 16-byte packet MD5, 16-byte recovery set id, 16-byte type
Main: slice size, number of recovery-set files, FileIDs of the recovery set and of the non-recovery set
File Description: FileID, MD5 of the whole file, MD5 of the first 16 KiB, length, ASCII name
IFSC: FileID plus an MD5 and CRC32 per slice
Recovery Slice (RecvSlic): exponent and recovery data
optional: UniFileN (Unicode filename), CommASCI, CommUni (comments), FileSlic, RFSC, PkdMain, PkdRecvS
techniques: FileID = MD5(MD5-16k, length, ASCII name): the same content and name give the same FileID, so it is a twin key
Recovery Set ID = MD5 of the Main packet body: the same slice size and file set give the same set id
Naming: the spec's .volXX-YY.par2 vs the volXX+count style par2cmdline uses
Non-recovery-set files are listed in Main without slice protection
The example application packet carries a newsgroup and a subject regex
new_for_atlas: Atlas stores the set id and file MD5/MD5-16k. It should also store FileID (content plus name) next to MD5 (content only): an equal FileID means twin, while an equal MD5 with a different FileID means a renamed alt. It should also parse CommASCI/CommUni comments and note non-recovery-set files.

title: ParPar help-full.txt + bin/parpar.js: creator string and slice/naming options that fingerprint posting pipelines
summary: ParPar's help documents its slice sizing, recovery distribution, naming and comment options. bin/parpar.js (around line 336) writes the Creator packet as 'ParPar v<version> <arch> [https://github.com/animetosho/parpar]'; the library default is 'ParPar (library) v...'.
metadata_fields: -s slice size (count, size in B/K/M, or relative suffixes l/s/w/o)
techniques: Slice size fingerprints the tool or preset: the help notes -s2000 matches the par2cmdline default and -s0.5w*10 the par2j default
Naming style: -n std gives vol12-22, par2cmdline style gives vol12+10
Recovery distribution -d equal/uniform/pow2 (default pow2) sets the pattern of vol file sizes
Other settings that show in the output: -p 65535, --slices-first-file, --noindex (no index .par2)
new_for_atlas: Store the Creator packet; ParPar's string even includes the CPU arch. Slice size, vol naming style and vol-size progression together form a 'par profile'. The profile stays the same for one uploader's pipeline, so it can group obfuscated uploads by the same poster.

title: par2cmdline creatorpacket.cpp + par2cmdline-turbo configure.ac: creator string format
summary: par2cmdline writes its Creator packet as 'Created by ' PACKAGE ' version ' VERSION '.', so the string names the package and exact version. par2cmdline-turbo's turbo branch sets AC_INIT([par2cmdline-turbo],[1.5.0]), while its master branch keeps upstream's AC_INIT([par2cmdline],[1.3.0]).
metadata_fields: Creator: 'Created by par2cmdline version X.Y.Z.' or 'Created by par2cmdline-turbo version X.Y.Z.'
techniques: Map creator strings to tool and version; together with slice size this tells par2cmdline, par2cmdline-turbo, ParPar and par2j apart
new_for_atlas: A creator-string to tool/version lookup table for poster fingerprinting.

title: MultiPar par2j create.c: par2j creator string and Unicode/comment packets
summary: MultiPar's par2j command-line engine writes Creator 'par2j v' PRODUCT_VERSION (1.3.3; FILE_VERSION 1.3.3.7). It also writes UniFileN, CommASCI and CommUni packets.
techniques: The par2j creator identifies Windows MultiPar posters, including ngPost in its optional MultiPar mode
UniFileN keeps the original non-ASCII name even when FileDesc holds an ASCII form
new_for_atlas: Atlas parses UniFileN but not Creator or the comment packets. Add both: the comment packets can carry uploader text.

title: node-yencode README: SIMD yEnc with CRC32 combine/zeroes/multiply/shift and incremental NNTP decoding
summary:
animetosho's yencode library (used by Nyuu and ParPar) documents CRC32 helpers for combining and shifting CRCs. It also has an incremental decoder that handles NNTP dot-unstuffing and stops at '
=y' or '
.
'. Its example shows the last part carrying both pcrc32= and crc32=, and the decoder returns parsed props and byte offsets.
metadata_fields: pcrc32= and crc32= on the last part
yencStart, dataStart, dataEnd, yencEnd byte offsets
techniques: crc32_combine(crc1, crc2, len2) builds whole-file CRCs from article CRCs
crc32_zeroes, crc32_multiply and crc32_shift handle padded slices and power-of-x math
decodeChunk with dot-unstuffing and end-state detection for raw NNTP streams
new_for_atlas: A reference for the CRC math Atlas needs. The byte offsets of the yEnc header and trailer also expose formatting differences (line length, trailer layout) that identify the posting tool.

title: yEnc draft 1.3 (yenc-draft.1.3.txt): keywords and Usenet subject conventions
summary: The yEnc 1.3 draft defines =ybegin (line, size, name, part, total; total was added in 1.2), =ypart (begin, end) and =yend (size, part, pcrc32, crc32). It also gives the recommended subject formats and decoder conventions.
techniques: Parse subjects with the spec grammar (quoted filename, yEnc token, (n/N), size)
Match '=ybegin ' with its trailing space; '=ybegin2' is reserved for a future version
Decoders mark damaged output names, e.g. (crc32-error)
new_for_atlas: Atlas can measure how far each subject strays from the spec grammar (missing quotes, no size, extra comment blocks). That pattern fingerprints the tool and uploader, which helps group obfuscated posts.

title: NZB file specification (SABnzbd wiki): meta types and element meanings
summary: The NZB spec defines <head><meta> types title, tag (repeatable), category, password (repeatable) and private X- types, plus file poster/date/subject, groups, and segments (bytes, number). It warns that date is the Unix time the server first saw the article (unreliable), and that the subject is munged so (xx/yy) becomes (1/yy).
metadata_fields: meta title, tag, category, password, X-*
techniques: Normalize (xx/yy) to (1/yy) when matching NZB subjects to article subjects
Treat the NZB date as approximate; prefer header dates or Message-ID timestamps
new_for_atlas: Atlas writes NZBs. It could also emit meta password/tag and X-atlas-* types (for example twin/alt group ids), and read meta from imported third-party NZBs as extra correlation keys.

title: Nyuu lib/article.js + config.js + help-full.txt: default Message-ID, headers, subject template and yEnc trailer
summary: Nyuu's defaults: a random Message-ID with a millisecond timestamp, a Nyuu User-Agent, a 'user <user@hostname>' From, a fixed subject template, 716800-byte articles with 128-byte lines, and a whole-file crc32= on the last part. Options let uploaders make the NZB subject, poster and yEnc name differ from the article headers.
metadata_fields: Message-ID: 24 random letters alternating upper/lower case, '-', 13-digit ms timestamp, '@nyuu'
=ybegin part= total= line= size= name=; the last part's =yend adds crc32= (whole file, via crc32_combine)
techniques: The Message-ID timestamp gives the upload time to the millisecond, independent of the Date header
The 24-letter alternating-case local part identifies Nyuu even with a custom domain (newzNZB uses @PRiVATE)
Obfuscating uploaders randomise subjects with the ${rand(N)} and {timestamp} tokens
Post methods POST, IHAVE, XREPLIC and TAKETHIS
NZB subject/poster can differ from the article, so comparing NZB to headers can expose rewritten metadata
new_for_atlas: Parse Message-ID local parts: Nyuu's form yields the tool plus a ms timestamp, which groups all files of one upload session even under random subjects. Fetching the last segment's =yend crc32= gives a whole-file CRC for one extra article.

title: ngPost NntpArticle.cpp + NntpFile.cpp + NgPost.h: UUID Message-IDs, obfuscation mode and yEnc formatting
summary: ngPost sends only From, Newsgroups, Subject and Message-ID (a 32-hex QUuid @ngPost). In obfuscation mode (-x) the Subject is the Message-ID's UUID and From is random, but =ybegin name= still holds the real filename. Its =yend writes pcrc32 with std::hex (no zero padding) and omits crc32.
metadata_fields: obfuscated Subject = Message-ID UUID; From = randomStdFrom() (13 random chars + '@' + signature + '.com')
NZB subject '[n/N] - "name" yEnc (1/N) size'; NZB date in seconds
=ybegin part= total= line=128 size= name=<real filename>
techniques: Detect ngPost obfuscation: the Subject equals the Message-ID local part and there is no User-Agent header
Deobfuscate from =ybegin name=, which ngPost leaves unobfuscated
A pcrc32 shorter than 8 hex digits (no zero padding) is an ngPost formatting tell
Random 17-char archive names and 13-char passwords come from ngPost's auto-generation
new_for_atlas: Atlas already parses the yEnc name. New are rules that classify a post as ngPost (subject == msgid UUID, minimal header set, unpadded pcrc32) and then treat the yEnc name as the trusted filename.

title: newsmangler postmangler.py + GoPostStuff article.go: legacy poster Message-ID, X-Newsposter and yEnc formats
summary: madcowfred's Python poster newsmangler and its Go successor GoPostStuff both put timestamps in Message-IDs and name themselves in X-Newsposter. They differ in subject padding, pcrc32 case and article size.
metadata_fields: newsmangler X-Newsposter 'newsmangler %s (%s) - https://github.com/madcowfred/newsmangler' with a trailing CRLF (extra blank line)
newsmangler subject '%s [%s/%d] - "%s" yEnc (%s/%d)' zero-padded; =yend 'size=%d part=%d pcrc32=%08x'
techniques: The Message-ID holds float epoch seconds plus the part number (newsmangler) or Unix nanoseconds (GoPostStuff): exact post time and part order
pcrc32 case (lower vs upper) and article size (768000 vs 716800) tell the tools apart
The posting machine's hostname in newsmangler Message-IDs links uploads made from one machine
new_for_atlas: More rows for a poster-tool fingerprint table (Message-ID regex, X-Newsposter, pcrc32 case, article size). The hostname in newsmangler Message-IDs is a poster-identity key.

title: nzb-monkey nzbmonkey.py: Message-ID part counters (JBinUp, PowerPost) and NZB completeness checks
summary: nzb-monkey resolves NZBLNK links by searching binsearch, NZBKing and NZBIndex. It checks the returned NZBs for completeness using subject counters and, for JBinUp and PowerPost posts, part counters inside the Message-IDs.
metadata_fields: file and segment counts from the subject
techniques: Take part/total and file index/total from the Message-ID when subjects are obfuscated
Completeness thresholds: max_missing_files=2, max_missing_segments_percent=2.5
Indexer quirks: NZBKing strips the segment part from the header; NZBIndex drops the file count from ($1/$2) subjects
Search engines: binsearch.info, nzbking.com, nzbindex.com (RSS)
new_for_atlas: Message-ID counters let Atlas assemble files and sets from JBinUp/PowerPost articles even when subjects are random. It only needs regexes over XOVER message-ids, with no ARTICLE fetch.

title: newznab-tmux NameFixingService.php + NameFixingQueryService + DonorMatchSelector: CRC/UID/hash16k donor renaming
summary: NNTmux renames releases from nfo, files, srr, crc, uid, hash, par2, xxx and media_movie sources. Its donor matchers copy the name of an already identified release to one that shares an inner CRC32, a MediaInfo unique_id or a PAR2 hash16k, within a size tolerance.
metadata_fields: flags proc_nfo, proc_files, proc_par2, proc_uid, proc_hash16k, proc_srr, proc_crc32
techniques: crcDonors: releases with the same inner-file CRC32 and predb_id > 0
hashDonors: same PAR2 hash16k and predb_id > 0 or anidbid > 0
uidDonors: same media unique_id and predb_id > 0, anidbid > 0, or fromname = 'nonscene@Ef.net (EF)'
Size tolerance |delta| / donorSize: CRC 5%, UID 10%, hash16k 5%; the smallest difference wins
Predb filename match on cleaned names of at least 8 characters through the search backend; SRR/SRS file names used as release names; PREDB_REGEX
new_for_atlas: Atlas has these keys but no propagation step. Add donor renaming: when an obfuscated release shares a CRC/UID/hash16k with a release already matched to predb, it takes that name, within these size tolerances. Only predb- or anidb-matched releases may be donors, which stops spam names from spreading.

title: newznab-tmux CollectionHandler.php + HeaderParser + NNTPService: subject part regex, file-count regex and collection hash
summary: NNTmux splits each subject into a base name and (part/total), finds the file counter, and hashes the cleaned name with the total file count into a collection hash. The hash includes no poster or group, so cross-posted parts merge; group names come from Xref. It also asks the server for compressed XOVER.
metadata_fields: Xref (group names become collection_groups; xref tokens stored)
techniques: Part regex /^\s*(?!Usenet Index Post)(.+?)\s+\((\d+)\/(\d+)\)/; ' yEnc' is appended if missing
collectionhash = sha1(cleanedName . totalFiles), with no From and no group
Sends 'XFEATURE COMPRESS GZIP' to get gzip-compressed XOVER
new_for_atlas: Check which collection-key variant Atlas ported: current NNTmux drops From and group, while nZEDb used name + group + totalfiles, and md5(subject + From + group) for binaries. XFEATURE COMPRESS GZIP can cut XOVER bandwidth a lot on providers that support it.

title: newznab-tmux ReleaseFileManager.php + NfoService + NzbParserService + Par2Processor: password, fake and NFO detection
summary: NNTmux flags passworded or fake releases from inner file listings, and finds NFOs (including 'hidden' ones) using a size range and a regex that rejects known file headers. It pulls external IDs out of NFO text and stores par2-listed file names, sizes and hash16k as release_files.
metadata_fields: inner file names, pass flag, innerFileBlacklist
NFO IDs: imdb tt\d{7,}, tvdb, tvmaze, tmdb, anidb, trakt
par2-derived file names, sizes and hash_16K (up to 21 entries)
techniques: PASSWD_RAR when an inner file is encrypted, matches innerFileBlacklist, or is Codec/Setup.exe
Release file limit 11; a predb match is tried for each inner file name

isNFO rejects content starting with <?xml, =newz[NZB]=, RIFF, RAR/PAR, JFIF/matroska/ftyp/ID3 in the first bytes, PK\x03\x04, gzip \x1f\x8b\x08, MZ, %PDF, GIF8[79]a, \x89PNG, or an SFV ';Generated by' line; it also uses file(1) and Par2Info/SfvInfo
Hidden NFO = a one-segment '(1/1)' subject with no known extension
PAR2 index = the .par2 subject that is not a vol file
new_for_atlas: Atlas could find hidden NFOs from XOVER alone (one segment, no extension), then fetch one article to read IMDb/TVDB/AniDB ids. Those ids are strong cross-release grouping keys. 'Codec/Setup.exe' and blacklist hits are cheap fake flags.

title: dariusiii/rarinfo (RarInfo.php, Par2Info.php, SrrInfo.php, SzipInfo.php, ZipInfo.php, SfvInfo.php): PHP archive/par2/srr parsers used by NNTmux
summary: These are the archive parsers NNTmux depends on. RarInfo reads RAR3 and RAR5 (with R50_* extra-record constants) and reports each inner file's byte range. Par2Info reports the creating client and block layout, SrrInfo reads SRR blocks including the OSO hash, and SzipInfo/ZipInfo report encryption and methods.
metadata_fields: Par2Info: all 13 packet types; client, block_count, block_size, file_count; per file name, size, hash, hash_16K, blocks
RarInfo per file: name, size, date, pass, compressed, range (byte offsets), crc32, split, split_after, is_dir, links
RarInfo summary: is_volume, has_auth, has_recovery, is_encrypted, rar_format
SrrInfo blocks: 0x69 app_name, 0x6a stored file, 0x6b OSO hash (file_size, file_size_high, file_hash, name), 0x71 RAR file
SzipInfo: solid_pack, enc_header, is_encrypted, METHOD_7Z_AES 06f10701, CRC32 digests
techniques: The 'range' byte offsets locate each inner file inside the volume, and so in the article segments
The OSO hash in SRR files is a direct key to the media file's OpenSubtitles hash
new_for_atlas: Inner-file byte ranges tell Atlas which segments to fetch for MKV/MP4 probing or the OSO hash (first and last 64 KiB), without downloading whole volumes. Atlas should also parse SRR files found in posts and read the RAR5 HTIME/UOWNER/HASH records.

title: nZEDb mysql-ddl.sql + NameFixer.php + PreDb.php + RequestID*.php: predb hash dehashing and request-ID lookup
summary: A database trigger in nZEDb stores the MD5, MD5(MD5) and SHA1 of every predb title, and NameFixer uses them to reverse hashed release names. It also detects request-ID subjects and resolves them against predb, using a per-group remap or a web request URL.
metadata_fields: NFO-derived imdb, anidb, upc, asin, isbn, tvrage, amazon ids (MiscSorter)
techniques: PreDb scans names for /[a-fA-F0-9]{32,40}/ and calls matchPredbHash (40 characters means SHA1)
Local request-ID lookup with a group remap (teevee, moovee, erotica, foreign->mom, inner-sanctum, sounds.flac, scnzb->boneless, hdtv.x264)
Multi-lookup matches the regex title or filename against predb title or filename; web lookup through request_url
new_for_atlas: Atlas should precompute md5, md5(md5) and sha1 of every predb title, plus the title+requestid variants from Leo's notes, so 32- and 40-hex subjects can be dehashed by index lookup. It should also add request-ID extraction with the group remap.

title: nZEDb Binaries.php + ProcessAdditional.php: original collection/binary hash keys and additional-processing limits
summary: In nZEDb a collection key is the cleaned name + group id (blank in multi-group mode) + total files, hashed with sha1, and a binary is md5(subject match + From + group id). ProcessAdditional sets how many segments are fetched for inspection and the password-check limits.
metadata_fields: binaryhash: subject regex match, From, groupId
techniques: collectionhash = sha1(name + groupId + totalfiles); groupId is blank in MGR mode so cross-posts merge
binaryhash = md5(subject match + From + groupId): same-named files from different posters stay apart
ProcessAdditional defaults: segmentstodownload 2, maximumRarSegments 3, maximumRarPasswordChecks 1, maxsizetopostprocess 100 GB; innerfileblacklist; PASSWD_POTENTIAL / PASSWD_RAR
new_for_atlas: This is the older key design to compare with NNTmux. Keeping From in the binary key stops two uploaders' same-named files from merging, which matters for twin detection. It also shows 2-3 RAR segments are enough to get listings.

title: Spotweb Services_Format_Parsing.php + Services_Nntp_SpotReading.php + Services_Format_Util.php: Spotnet signed spot headers
summary: Spotnet 'spots' are signed Usenet posts whose headers carry XML metadata (title, category, size, poster, tag, filename, newsgroup, and the message-ids of NZB segments). Spotweb parses and verifies them, and derives a stable spotterid from the poster's public key.
metadata_fields: X-XML (multi-line, concatenated), X-XML-Signature, X-User-Key, X-User-Signature, X-User-Avatar, X-Newsreader
XML: Created, Key, Category, SubCat (subcata/b/c/d/z), Website, Description, Size, Poster, Tag, Title, Filename, newsgroup, Image (segments, width, height), NZB/Segment, Extra/Newsreader
techniques: spotterid = base64(4-byte little-endian crc32(base64_decode(userKey))) with '/', '+' and '=' removed: one stable id per poster key
keyid 7 means self-signed, which requires hashcash: sha1('<msgid>') must start with '0000'
RSA signature check of X-XML and the user key before trusting spot metadata
The NZB segment message-ids in a spot link it to the binary posts
new_for_atlas: Atlas could ingest Spotnet spot groups and join spot NZB message-ids to binaries it has indexed. That names obfuscated posts with signed metadata tied to a poster, and spotterid is an uploader identity that cannot be faked without the key.

title: NZBHydra2 DuplicateDetector.java: cross-indexer duplicate thresholds
summary: NZBHydra2 treats search results from different indexers as duplicates when the normalized titles match, poster and group agree (when known), and age and size are within thresholds. The thresholds are doubled when only one of group or poster is known.
metadata_fields: newznab attrs read: usenetdate, password, nfo, info, poster, group, files, comments, grabs, guid, size, source, season, episode, showtitle
techniques: Duplicates must come from different indexers; torrents are excluded
Group and poster must be equal when both are known
Age within duplicateAgeThreshold 2.0 hours and size within 1.0% of the mean, both doubled when only one of group/poster is known
new_for_atlas: Tested defaults for Atlas's twin-candidate stage (normalized title, same poster/group, within 2 h and 1%), which Atlas's byte-level keys can then confirm or reject. Atlas should also emit the same newznab attrs so Hydra's dedup works on its results.

title: Sonarr Parser.cs + ReleaseGroupParser.cs: hashed-release rejection regexes, reversed titles and repost-tag cleaning
summary: Sonarr rejects hashed or obfuscated release names with a dated list of regexes, detects reversed titles, and rejects titles containing both 'password' and 'yenc'. It strips repost and indexer suffix tags before reading the release group.
techniques: RejectHashedReleasesRegexes: ^[0-9a-zA-Z]{32}, ^[a-z0-9]{24}$, ^[A-Z]{11}\d{3}$ and ^[a-z]{12}\d{3}$ (NZBGeek), ^Backup_\d{5,}S\d{2}-\d{2}$, ^123$ (Dec 2014), ^abc$ and ^b00bs$ (Jan 2015), ^abc[-_. ]xyz (2020), ^\d{6}_\d{2}$ (Aug 2018), plus length-specific alphanumeric hashes of 30 (Dec 2020) and 26/39/24 characters (Jan 2021)
ReversedTitleRegex (?:^|[-._ ])(p027|p0801|\d{2,3}E-?\d{2}S)[-._ ]: reversed 720p, 1080p and SxxEyy
Reject titles that contain both 'password' and 'yenc'

CleanReleaseGroupRegex strips -RP, -1, NZBGeek, [N-Z-B], Obfuscated, Scrambled, sample, Pre, postbot, xpost, Rakuv*, WhiteRev, BUYMORE, AsRequested, AlternativeToRequested, GEROV, Z0iDS3N, Chamele0n, 4P, 4Planet, AlteZachen, RePACKPOST; also website prefix/postfix regexes
new_for_atlas: Strip these repost tags before comparing names, so a '-Obfuscated' or '-postbot' repost groups with the original as a twin or alt. Detect reversed titles and un-reverse them before predb matching.

title: CPython nntplib.py: overview format and extra OVERVIEW.FMT fields
summary: Python's NNTP client defines the default overview fields, and reads LIST OVERVIEW.FMT to learn extra fields such as 'Xref:full', whose values include the header name. It falls back from OVER to XOVER.
techniques: Request LIST OVERVIEW.FMT per server and map the extra fields; strip the 'Xref: ' prefix from :full fields
Use OVER first, with XOVER as fallback
new_for_atlas: Atlas keeps subject/from/date/message-id/bytes from XOVER. It should also keep :lines, References and, where the server offers it, Xref:full from every overview line. That gives cross-post detection for every article, not just the one ARTICLE per release.

title: MediaInfoLib File_Mk.cpp + File_Avc.cpp, with exiftool Matroska.pm: Matroska identity fields and x264 settings
summary: MediaInfo maps the Matroska SegmentUID to General UniqueID, reads mux dates and apps, and parses per-track _STATISTICS tags, flagging a 'Statistics Tags Issue' when they disagree. File_Avc pulls the x264 options string from SEI user_data_unregistered. exiftool's Matroska table exposes the same UIDs and apps.
metadata_fields: DateUTC -> Encoded_Date; MuxingApp -> Encoded_Library; WritingApp -> Encoded_Application; Title
AVC SEI user_data_unregistered UUID dc45e9bd-e6d9-48b7-... (x264) -> Encoded_Library_Settings ('options: ...')
exiftool: SegmentUID, PrevUID, NextUID, TrackUID, EditionUID, ChapterUID, MuxingApp, WritingApp, DateTimeOriginal, TagName/TagString, CodecPrivate
techniques: SegmentUID is random per mux: equal in byte-identical twins, different after a remux, so it separates twins from alts
A statistics app/date mismatch means the file was edited after its original mux
The x264 options string plus per-track NUMBER_OF_FRAMES/BYTES fingerprint one encode across remuxes and containers
new_for_atlas: Atlas parses MKV tracks, chapters and HDR/DV. It should add SegmentUID, DateUTC, MuxingApp/WritingApp, per-track statistics tags and the x264 settings string (NNTmux already uses unique_id as a donor key). The same x264 settings and frame/byte counts with a different SegmentUID is a clean alt signal.

title: srrDB help (search keywords) + pyReScene osohash.py/rar.py: scene release lookup by ISDb/OSO hash and archive CRC
summary: srrDB's search accepts keywords for release name, group, date, NFO/SRS presence, ISDb (OpenSubtitles) hash, archive CRC and archive size. pyReScene defines the SRR block types, and its osohash_from() computes the ISDb hash straight from stored RAR volumes without extracting.
metadata_fields: srrDB keywords: r:, group:, date:, nfo:, srs:, foreign:, confirmed:, rarhash:, category:, imdb:, genre:, language:, country:, archive-crc:, archive-size:, isdbhash:, lower:, firstupper:, compressed:, skip:, skipr:, store-real-filename:, store-real-crc:
SRR blocks: 0x69 header (app name), 0x6A stored file, 0x6B 'SRR ISDb Hash (OSO hash previously)', 0x6C padding, 0x71 RAR subblock
ISDb/OSO hash = file size + 64-bit sum over the first and last 64 KiB
go-srrdb-API: name, size and crc of files and archived-files
techniques: Look up the scene release name with isdbhash:<OpenSubtitles hash>
Look up by archive-crc:/archive-size: using the inner-file CRC32 from RAR headers or PAR2-derived CRCs
osohash_from() reads through a RarStream over stored volumes, so it only needs the bytes at the start and end of the inner file
new_for_atlas: Atlas already computes the OpenSubtitles moviehash. Querying srrDB with isdbhash: (and archive-crc: with inner CRCs) turns an obfuscated payload into a scene name. For -m0 RARs Atlas can compute the hash from the two 64 KiB windows, located through RAR byte ranges, without a full download.

title: RAR 5.0 archive format technote (rarlab.com): header and extra-record fields
summary: RARLAB's technical note specifies the RAR5 main archive header, file and service headers, extra records, the archive encryption header and the end-of-archive header. Several of these fields are fingerprints or content keys that parsers which only list names usually skip.
metadata_fields: main header flags: volume, volume number present, solid, recovery record, locked; volume number
file header: flags (directory, mtime, CRC32, unknown unpacked size), unpacked size, attributes, mtime, data CRC32, compression info (version, solid, method, dictionary size), host OS, UTF-8 name
extra 0x01 file encryption (KDF count, salt, IV, check value)
extra 0x03 high-precision times; 0x04 file version; 0x05 redirection; 0x06 Unix owner (user and group names, numeric IDs); 0x07 service data
archive encryption header (KDF count, salt shared by all headers, check value)
service headers CMT, QO, ACL, STM, RR
end-of-archive flag: the archive is a volume and not the last one
techniques: Unix owner names and IDs, host OS and compression version/method/dictionary form a packer profile that stays the same across one uploader's posts
BLAKE2sp and data CRC32 are content keys for alt matching across differently packed archives
The 'not last volume' flag shows whether more volumes should exist
new_for_atlas: Atlas lists RAR5 names and sizes. It should also store mtime, data CRC32, BLAKE2sp, compression method/dictionary, host OS and Unix owner names, which link obfuscated reposts by the same packer and confirm alts by content hash.

title: Leo's Notes: Usenet - real newzNZB obfuscated article headers and hashing conventions
summary: A wiki page with a full header dump of a newzNZB private upload. It shows the obfuscated subject form, a Nyuu-style Message-ID with an @PRiVATE domain, server-added X-Received headers and custom signature headers. It also lists the hash schemes private indexers use for titles, and links an upload-logger repo as a predb source.
metadata_fields: Organization Usenet.Farm; Newsgroups alt.binaries.newznzb.bravo; Path not-for-mail
techniques: Hash candidates for titles: MD5(title), MD5(MD5(title)), SHA1(title), MD5(title.requestid), MD5(title.requestid.requestid)
The Message-ID shape (24 alternating-case letters, 13-digit ms timestamp) shows Nyuu with a custom domain and gives the post time
scriptzteam/newzNZB-Usenet-Upload-Logger-v1.1 is a log of uploads that can serve as a predb-like source
new_for_atlas: Add the title+requestid hash variants to the dehash table. Keep the X-Received-Body-CRC and X-Received-Bytes headers (added by the server; possibly an article-level twin key without decoding, unverified), plus X-Ufk and Verify-Signature-*. Recognise the newzNZB subject form.

title: yEnc encryption standards (Tensai75) + SABnzbd PR #3676: encrypted control lines and bodies
summary: This draft encrypts the yEnc control lines with FF1 format-preserving encryption, so line lengths stay the same, and the body with XChaCha20-Poly1305. The password travels in NZB <meta type="password">. The SABnzbd PR to support it (github.com/sabnzbd/sabnzbd/pull/3676) was closed without merge on 2026-11-01, so downloaders have not adopted it.
metadata_fields: segmentIndex and lineIndex used in tweaks and nonces
techniques: Control lines: FF1 with AES-256 over a 253-byte alphabet, Argon2id key, tweak HMAC(segmentIndex, lineIndex), deterministic salt SHA-256('yenc-control salt' || password)
Body: XChaCha20-Poly1305 with nonce HMAC(segmentIndex), a deterministic salt, and the tag in '=yencryption'
The README names pesto, Nyuu and ngPost as implementations
new_for_atlas: Atlas should detect this format (no parseable =ybegin keywords, or an =yencryption line) and mark such articles 'encrypted yEnc', not corrupt. With the NZB password it could decrypt the control lines to recover names and sizes.

title: nzb-rs (Rust crate) parser.rs + subparsers.rs, and the yencoding crate's header.rs
summary: nzb-rs is a Rust NZB parser. It keeps the first meta title/category, de-duplicates password/tag lists, requires poster/date/subject, sorts groups and segments, and rejects par2-only NZBs. It includes a port of SABnzbd's obfuscation check and subject filename extraction; the separate yencoding crate defines typed =ybegin/=ypart/=yend structs.
metadata_fields: meta title/category (first wins), password and tag lists (deduplicated)
yencoding YbeginFields size/line_length/part/total/name; YpartFields begin/end; YendFields size/pcrc32/crc32
techniques: OnlyPar2Files error for NZBs that contain only par2 files
sabnzbd_is_obfuscated port
extract_filename_from_subject: quoted name first, then ^(?:\[|\()(?:\d+/\d+)(?:\]|\))\s-\s(.*)\syEnc\s(?:\[|\()(?:\d+/\d+)(?:\]|\))\s\d+, then SABnzbd's basic filename regex
sort_key pads [n/N] counters so files sort numerically
new_for_atlas: Rust code Atlas can reuse almost unchanged for NZB import, subject filename extraction and the SABnzbd obfuscation verdict, so Atlas's behaviour stays in line with SABnzbd.

title: NNTmux NameFixingService: donor renaming by inner CRC32, MediaInfo Unique_ID and PAR2 hash_16K
summary: Current newznab-tmux renames unidentified releases (predb_id=0) using NFO text, file names, SRR/SRS names and PAR2 FileDesc names. It can also borrow the name of an already-identified 'donor' release that shares an inner-file CRC32, a MediaInfo Unique_ID or a PAR2 MD5-16k, as long as total sizes agree. The SQL is in NameFixingQueryService.php, tie-breaking in DonorMatchSelector.php and file ordering in FilePrioritizer.php (same directory; all opened).
metadata_fields: release_files.crc32 (CRC32 of each file inside the archive, from RAR headers)
par_hashes.hash (PAR2 FileDesc MD5 of first 16 KiB)
status flags proc_nfo, proc_files, proc_par2, proc_uid, proc_hash16k, proc_srr, proc_crc32
techniques: crcCheck: SELECT rf.crc32, r.size FROM release_files rf JOIN releases r WHERE rf.crc32 IN (...) AND r.predb_id > 0; a donor is accepted when abs(donorSize-targetSize)/donorSize*100 <= 5; the smallest difference wins, then the lowest release id

CRC candidates are tried in FilePrioritizer::getCrcPriority order: .srr=1, main .rar (not .partN)=2, .part01.rar=3, video (mkv/avi/mp4/m4v/wmv/divx/ts/m2ts)=4, .nfo=5, other rar/rNN=6, other=50, sample/proof/subs/thumbs=100
uidCheck: donors with the same media_infos.unique_id where predb_id>0 OR anidbid>0 OR fromname='nonscene@Ef.net (EF)'; size tolerance 10%
hashCheck: donors with the same par_hashes.hash (a 32-hex hash_16K written by ReleaseFile::addReleaseFiles while parsing the PAR2) and predb_id>0 or anidbid>0; size tolerance 5%
srrNameCheck: a release file named /^(.+)\.srr$/ or /^(.+)\.srs$/ gives its basename as the release name, if that basename matches PREDB_REGEX
mediaMovieNameCheck: the MediaInfo 'Movie name' (container title) is used as the name, with a trailing ', RMZ.cr' removed
fixNamesWithPar2: fetch the index .par2 (subject /\.(par[2" ]|\d{2,3}").+\(1\/1\)/i), add up to 21 FileDesc names to release_files, and run checkName on each
new_for_atlas: Atlas has the raw fields but no donor propagation. It should store each release's inner-file CRC32, MKV SegmentUID and PAR2 MD5-16k as indexed keys. When an unknown release shares one of these with an identified release and total sizes agree within 5% (CRC/16k) or 10% (UID), copy the verified name. Also adopt the CRC file priority order and a per-pass 'already tried' flag.

title: NNTmux PredbMatchSelector: scored file-name to PreDB matching that refuses weak matches
summary: Cleans a release file name and searches the PreDB index. It scores at most the top 50 hits against both predb.title and predb.filename and accepts a hit only if it scores 60 or more. Names that carry little information are refused outright.
metadata_fields: predb.filename (first file name from pre feeds)
techniques: score = similarity%*0.6 + tokenOverlapRatio*45 + 6*sharedTokens; +80 for an exact match; +18 if the query (8+ chars) is a substring; +8 if the longest shared token is 8+ chars; +5 when matched through predb.filename; -30 if only one side contains the token 'xxx'

ignored noise tokens: audio_ts, video_ts, bup, ifo, vob, vts, cd, disc, disk, dvd, cover(s), image(s), img, jpg, png, webp, nfo, par2, part, rar, sfv, srr, srs, zip, sample, proof, screen(s), sub(s), thumb(s), txt, url, the, of, a, an, and, file(s), folder, video, audio, pdf

refused queries: /^\d+$/, /^(?:audio|video)[ ._-]?ts$/i, /^vts[ ._-]?\d+(?:[ ._-]\d+)?$/i, /^(?:image|img)\d*$/i, /^(?:cd|dvd|disc|disk|part|vol)\d*$/i; cleaned names under 8 chars are skipped (matchPreDbFiles)
matchPreDbFiles walks release_files in FilePrioritizer::prioritizeForPreDb order and stops at the first accepted hit; results are cached (5000 entries)
new_for_atlas: Adopt this scoring and the 'no answer below 60' rule for PreDB matching. Match against PreDB's first-file name (FN) as well as the release dirname.

title: NNTmux DetectsHashedNames trait: rules for spotting obfuscated names
summary: A shared predicate isHashedOrGibberish() decides whether a release name or file name is obfuscated, using bounded hash regexes, token-shape rules and character-statistics tests. FileNameCleaner::isPlausibleReleaseTitle() uses it to refuse hashed strings as titles.
techniques: bounded hashes: md5 /(?:^|["'\s\[\]\/\-])([a-f0-9]{32})(?:["'\s\[\]\/.\-]|$)/i, the same pattern for sha1 {40} and sha256 {64}; a generic [a-z0-9]{24,128} token that contains a digit, has no 19xx/20xx year and looks random

base64-like token [A-Za-z0-9+/_=-]{24,} containing upper, lower and digit; UUID 8-4-4-4-12 with optional dashes; pure hex of 16+ chars; ^[A-Z0-9]{15,}$; ^[a-zA-Z0-9]{15,}$ unless CamelCase or it contains a year
Usenet subject shape: \[\d+\/\d+]\s*-\s*"([a-zA-Z0-9]{12,})\.(part\d+\.rar|7z\.\d{3}|rar|zip|vol\d+\+\d+\.par2|par2)" where the stem has no separators and looks random

character statistics: alnum core of 16+ chars with case/digit transition rate > 0.35 and no media words; core of 20+ chars whose longest letter run is under 5; 20+ chars with zero vowels (10+ letters); /^[a-zA-Z]{1,3}\d{6,}[a-zA-Z]*$/ or /^[a-zA-Z0-9]{2,4}\d{8,}$/
looksLikeRandomString: single-case string of 12+ chars; or transition ratio > 0.3 with no consonant-vowel-consonant-vowel pattern; or 5+ consonants in a row
new_for_atlas: Atlas needs one shared 'is this name obfuscated' test, both to send releases to deobfuscation and to stop hashed strings being used as titles. This trait is a tested rule set ready to port.

title: NNTmux header to collection to binary grouping, Xref cross-post merge, and nZEDb multi-group posters
summary: This shows how current newznab-tmux turns XOVER rows into collections and binaries. Related opened files: HeaderParser.php, HeaderStorageService.php, BinaryHandler.php, app/Services/XrefService.php, app/Services/CollectionsCleaningService.php, and nZEDb's nzedb/Binaries.php for the older multi-group mode.
techniques: HeaderParser: the subject must match /^\s*(?!Usenet Index Post)(.+?)\s+\((\d+)\/(\d+)\)/ (part/total), otherwise it is counted as notYEnc and dropped; ' yEnc' is appended if missing

collection key = cleaned subject (from the collection_regexes DB, else generic cleaning) + totalFiles; collectionhash = sha1(key) as raw bytes. Neither poster nor group id is in the key, so cross-posted copies collapse into one collection
binary identity = md5('file:'+fileNumber) when a [n/m] counter exists, else md5('subject:'+lower(subject)+'\0poster:'+lower(From))

Xref tokens are kept only if they match /(^[a-zA-Z]{2,3}\.(bin(aries|arios|aer))\.[a-zA-Z0-9]?.+)(:\d+)/; every group named in Xref is recorded for the collection and later written to the NZB <groups>

generic cleaning removes sizes, (n/m) counters, AutoRarPar\d+, .vol\d+\+\d+, .partN and extensions (7z, rar, rNN, par2, sfv, srr, srs, nzb, nfo...); in music groups it also removes quoted text and pads short subjects
nZEDb MGR mode: for posters listed in mgr_posters (or all, with indexer.mgr.allasmgr) CollectionKey = name + '' + totalFiles, leaving out the group id, and each new Xref is appended to the collection
new_for_atlas: Atlas uses the collection regexes already. It should also: leave the group id out of the key and merge the groups named in Xref, so a cross-post is one post; use subject+poster as identity when there is no [n/m] counter; and keep a configurable list of multi-group posters.

title: NNTmux backfill (article number to date) and the RFC 3977 numbering guarantee
summary: postdate() finds the date of an article number from local parts, or from a single-article XOVER, retrying with other article numbers. daytopost() binary-searches article numbers for a target date, and partRepair() re-fetches missed numbers. RFC 3977 section 6 (https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3977.html, opened) guarantees the ordering this relies on: 'articles arriving later MUST have higher numbers', and servers 'SHOULD allocate the next sequential unused number'.
metadata_fields: GROUP low/high water marks and count
techniques: postdate: SELECT c.date FROM collections c JOIN binaries b JOIN parts p WHERE p.number=? (indexed); else XOVER that one article and read Date; up to 20 attempts stepping to a neighbouring number
daytopost: if the goal date is before first or after last, clamp; otherwise binarySearchArticleByDate between the first and last article numbers
partRepair: missed numbers are grouped into ranges with attempt counters; numbers lost in storage rollbacks during backfill are queued too

RFC 3977: numbers follow arrival order per group; the same article has different numbers in different groups (Xref lists them); the high water mark is not monotonic but the low water mark should not decrease
new_for_atlas: Treat article numbers as a server-side clock that posters cannot fake. Keep an article-number to injection-time index per group. Runs of adjacent numbers, matched across groups through Xref, link the articles of one posting session even when subject, From and Date are randomized.

title: NNTmux NZB-content heuristics: hidden NFOs, obfuscated volume names, completion, PAR2 index
summary: These are the heuristics newznab-tmux applies to a release's own NZB. Companion files (opened) are Nzb/NzbContentsService.php, AdditionalProcessing/NzbContentParser.php, AdditionalProcessing/ReleaseFileManager.php and app/Models/ReleaseFile.php. They show the PAR2 being read from its first segment, and the inner CRC32 and PAR2 hash_16K being saved.
techniques: hidden NFO candidates: one segment with a subject ending (1/1); 2 or fewer segments with a word nfo|info|readme|release|file_id|about; a scene-style single-segment name /^[a-z0-9]+[._-][a-z0-9._-]+["\s]*\(1\/1\)/i; or 'yEnc (N) [1/1]'. A candidate is then excluded if its subject shows an executable, archive, audio, video, image, par2, sfv, md5 or sha extension
completion = 100 * segments actually in the NZB / sum over files of the (x/TOTAL) total parsed from each subject

archive-part regex (NzbContentParser): /(\.(part\d+|[rz]\d+|rar|0+|0*10?|zipr\d{2,3}|zipx?)("|\s*\.rar)*($|[ ")]|-])|"[a-f0-9]{32}\.[1-9]\d{1,2}".*\(\d+\/\d{2,}\)$)/i. The last alternative catches obfuscated '<32-hex>.<NN>' split volumes
PAR2 index = the first NZB file whose subject ends in .par2, parsed from its FIRST segment only; FileDesc names go into release_files; any 32-char hash_16K goes into par_hashes
the archive listing stores per-file crc32 from RAR headers into release_files.crc32; 'codec spam' inner files mark a release as possibly passworded
new_for_atlas: Add hidden-NFO detection, recognition of '<32hex>.<NN>' volumes, and completion computed from subject totals. Store inner CRC32 and MD5-16k as keys that other releases can be joined on.

title: xbmc4lyfe/newznab-tmux PR #274: detecting per-article obfuscated uploads from headers alone
summary: This fork detects, from XOVER rows alone, uploads (from nyuu) where every article has its own random subject token and Message-ID, and sometimes a random poster. Example shapes are '[40/62] "<32 random>" yEnc (n/687)' and '[<2 random>] - <40 random> yEnc (n/1250)'. Without detection each article becomes its own collection that never completes, about 690k collections per hour.
techniques: grouping key: subject shape with alphanumeric runs collapsed + part total + file counter, applied only to multi-part articles whose name has an alphanumeric token of 16+ chars

gates: group size >= CBP_PER_ARTICLE_OBFUSCATION_MIN_ARTICLES (default 16, minimum 8; 0 or less disables); at least 90% of names distinct, ignoring digit runs outside the token so <hash>.partNN.rar counts once; candidates must cover at least that many distinct part positions
candidates are articles whose name occurs exactly once, excluding part 1 and the last part, so the boundary parts of real uploads survive

observations: alt.binaries.boneless had 199 distinct From values in 202 rows; the pattern also appeared in alt.binaries.test and alt.binaries.multimedia; a Rust FFI version (libnzbyenc) ran about 2 to 2.8x faster than PHP
action: skip storage and part-repair but still advance the article cursor; log 'Skipping articles obfuscated per article'
new_for_atlas: Atlas can reuse this detector but rebuild these posts instead of dropping them. Within a detected shape group, sort by article number and injection time, use the shared part total and file counter, contiguous article-number runs and equal decoded part sizes (all parts but the last) to rebuild files. Confirm with yEnc =ybegin size/total and the PAR2.

title: xbmc4lyfe/newznab-tmux PR #1246: mapping obfuscated NZB files to their PAR2 names
summary: A Rust port (additional::par2_mapping, additional::media_source, nntmux_namefix::par2_info) of NNTmux's Par2FileMapper. It reads the release's PAR2 index within a byte budget and maps NZB files with random names to FileDesc entries by posted size. Ambiguous files are resolved by downloading their first article.
metadata_fields: NZB file posted bytes and segment count
yEnc name and size from the first article
techniques: size window from the PR text: 'a posted-size ratio of 0.90 to 1.001, a lower bound of size minus size/512, and the segment count once the article size is known'
a file maps only when 'each is the only fit for the other'; equal-sized volumes stay unmatched unless verified

ambiguous files are verified by the PAR2 16 KiB hash or the yEnc name and size of their first article, up to NN_PAR2_VERIFY_FILES downloads; the first matched capture gives the article size, and the remaining files are then mapped by size
order of verification: first archive volumes, then samples, then videos largest first, then images
checked against 11 golden cases generated from the PHP class (tests/par2_mapping_golden.rs)
new_for_atlas: Without decoding anything, assign real names to obfuscated NZB entries by matching encoded posted sizes against PAR2 FileDesc lengths, using a ratio window and a one-to-one rule. Download one first article only when sizes tie.

title: NNTmux PR #1897 / #1895: release fingerprints and an order-independent Message-ID multiset hash
summary: Adds Rust parsing of Message-ID relations across the requested ID, HEAD and OVER, and records 'every OVER row, command availability, response code, and provider response status' alongside yEnc, PAR2, archive and cross-provider evidence. It also adds releases.article_fingerprint, 'an order-independent multiset fingerprint of segment Message-IDs', so NZB imports are idempotent. PR #1895 (also opened) collects 'NNTP server profile/header, yEnc, PAR2, archive-format, timing, and provider-comparison evidence' per release.
metadata_fields: Message-ID as requested vs in HEAD vs in OVER (case-sensitive)
PAR2 recovery-set metadata and IFSC slices
techniques: an imported NZB whose segment-ID multiset fingerprint matches a stored one is treated as the same upload; legacy rows fall back to comparing stored NZBs of the same size; check, insert and write run under a per-fingerprint lock
IFSC slices verified against yEnc samples (commit titles)
IFSC records merged across PAR2 volumes, with conflicting definitions flagged
metadata schema versioning drives reprocessing (fingerprint schema v8)
new_for_atlas: Twin detection at the NZB level with no download: a multiset hash over all segment Message-IDs. Also new: per-provider OVER/HEAD evidence, and archive header checksums (RAR4 HEAD_CRC, 7z NextHeaderCRC, RAR5 locator) as cheap archive identity keys.

title: nZEDb PreDB hash tables and dehashing (MD5, MD5(MD5), SHA1 of the title)
summary: nZEDb keeps a predb_hashes table filled by database triggers, so releases posted under a hash of their scene name can be resolved by lookup. PreDb.php::parseTitles (opened) pulls the hex string out of the release name or any file name, and NameFixer::matchPredbHash resolves it.
techniques: trigger insert_hashes: INSERT INTO predb_hashes VALUES (UNHEX(MD5(title))), (UNHEX(MD5(MD5(title)))), (UNHEX(SHA1(title))) for every predb row; update and delete triggers keep it in sync
releases trigger: ishashed=1 when name or searchname matches REGEXP '[a-fA-F0-9]{32}'; release_files trigger: ishashed=1 for file names with 32 hex chars

parseTitles: preg_match('/[a-fA-F0-9]{32,40}/') on the name, else on release_files.name; 40 chars means SHA1, otherwise MD5; lookup WHERE h.hash = UNHEX(x); on a miss dehashstatus is decremented, with retries while it is BETWEEN -6 AND 0
new_for_atlas: Precompute md5(title), md5(md5(title)) and sha1(title) for every PreDB title (sha256 and case variants are cheap extras). Look up any hex string found in subjects, yEnc names, PAR2 names or archive member names.

title: nZEDb IRC pre-feed scraper and request-ID resolution
summary: nZEDb's scraper reads the IRC pre feed (default channel #nZEDbPRE) and turns its announce lines into predb rows, including request id and group, size, file count and first file name. RequestID.php and RequestIDWeb.php (opened) turn request numbers in subjects into release names. nZEDb issue #2359 (https://github.com/nZEDb/nZEDb/issues/2359, opened) shows the request id moving into the RAR file name of MD5-hashed moovee posts.
techniques: announce regex: /^(NEW|UPD|NUK): \[DT: (?P<time>.+?)\]\s?\[TT: (?P<title>.+?)\]\s?\[SC: (?P<source>.+?)\]\s?\[CT: (?P<category>.+?)\]\s?\[RQ: (?P<req>.+?)\]\s?\[SZ: (?P<size>.+?)\]\s?\[FL: (?P<files>.+?)\]\s?(\[FN: (?P<filename>.+?)\]\s?)?(\[(?P<nuked>(UN|MOD|RE|OLD)?NUKED?): (?P<reason>.+?)\])?$/i; RQ is split with /^(?P<req>\d+):(?P<group>.+)$/
RequestIDWeb sends batches of {reqid, group, ident} to the configured request_url, remaps alt.binaries.etc to alt.binaries.teevee, and inserts the answer into predb with requestid and groups_id
issue #2359: subject '[7fcddbe2bfadfd8a57ee97f7bec50596]-[006/108] - "164822.part005.rar" yEnc', where 164822 is the request id for A.League.of.Their.Own.1992.1080p.BluRay.DTS.x264-SbR
new_for_atlas: Store PreDB size, file count and first file name (FN) plus request ids per group. Look for request numbers inside RAR and yEnc file names, not only in subjects.

title: nZEDb nzb_guid (MD5 of the first segment Message-ID) used as a cross-indexer key
summary: nZEDb stamps each release with nzb_guid, the MD5 of the first segment Message-ID written to its NZB. Sharing.php (opened) uses that value as the release key when exchanging comments with other indexers over Usenet.
techniques: nzb_guid = UNHEX(md5(the first <segment> Message-ID in NZB write order))
Sharing: shared comments carry nzb_guid (as 'RID'); shareid = sha1(unix_time . text . nzb_guid); incoming comments are joined to local releases USING (nzb_guid)
new_for_atlas: A cheap identity for 'the same post' seen through different NZBs or indexers, which differs from Atlas's content-based twins. Pair it with an order-independent hash over all segment Message-IDs (NNTmux PR #1897).

title: nZEDb NameFixer: MediaInfo Unique_ID matching and date-anchored predb.filename matching
summary: This is the original Unique_ID (MKV SegmentUID) donor match and fuzzy file-name matching against PreDB's filename field. ReleaseExtra.php (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nZEDb/nZEDb/master/nzedb/ReleaseExtra.php, opened) shows where the UID comes from.
techniques: ReleaseExtra: Unique_ID is parsed with /\(0x(?P<hash>[0-9a-f]{32})\)/i from the General track and stored once per release
uidCheck: other releases with the same uniqueid and (predb_id>0 OR anidbid>0 OR fromname='nonscene@Ef.net (EF)') are accepted if round((donor-target)/donor*100) is within -10..10
matchPredbFiles: file names matching /(\d{2}\.\d{2}\.\d{2})+[\w.-]+[\w]$/i are fulltext-searched in predb.filename; the date string must be identical and similar_text must be 93% or more
_cleanMatchFiles strips the extension, .partNNN, .volNNN(+NN) and directory prefixes before matching
new_for_atlas: Atlas parses MKV but should keep the SegmentUID (what MediaInfo calls 'Unique ID') as a key other releases can be joined on. Also add date-anchored fuzzy matching against predb.filename.

title: SABnzbd deobfuscate_filenames.py: obfuscation classifier and 'biggest file' rule
summary: SABnzbd's post-processing renames files via the MD5-16k values in any par2 (e.g. rename.par2). Otherwise it renames the single dominant file, and files sharing its basename, to the job name, but only when that file's name looks obfuscated. The developer forum thread (https://forums.sabnzbd.org/viewtopic.php?p=122040, opened) gives the test cases.
techniques: is_probably_obfuscated returns TRUE for: ^[a-f0-9]{32}$; ^[a-f0-9.]{40,}$; [a-f0-9]{30} together with 2+ '[word]' groups; a name starting 'abc.xyz'

returns FALSE for: 2+ upper and 2+ lower and at least one space/dot/underscore; 3+ separators; 4+ letters and 4+ digits and a separator; or starts uppercase with more than 2 lowercase and upper/lower <= 0.25. Default is TRUE
get_biggest_file: rename only if the largest file is more than 3x the second largest (or is the only file)
excluded extensions .vob .rar .par2 .mts .m2ts .cpi .clpi .mpl .mpls .bdm .bdmv; skipped if DVD/Blu-ray folders exist; a MIN_FILE_SIZE constant of 10 MiB is defined
decode_par2: MD5 the first 16384 bytes of every file and rename it to the FileDesc name with the same MD5-16k
forum cases: 599c1c9e2bdfb5114044bf25152b7eaa.mkv is flagged; 9y5gNEsQaxB6H.mkv is not (a known miss)
new_for_atlas: Use the classifier and the 3x rule to decide which inner file carries the release's identity. Mapping by MD5-16k needs only the first article of each file.

title: SABnzbd par2file.py: whole-file CRC32 from IFSC, the Creator packet, and FileDesc offsets
summary: SABnzbd's PAR2 parser reads Main, FileDesc, Creator and IFSC packets. From the per-slice CRC32s it computes the CRC32 of every protected file, which allows quick checks and renaming without any MD5 work.
metadata_fields: Main slice size and file count
techniques: packet type at data[16:32], set id = data[:16]; FileDesc: file id data[32:48], hash16k data[64:80], length <Q at data[80:88], name data[88:] with NULs stripped
Main: slice size <Q at data[32:40], file count <I at data[40:44]; IFSC: 20-byte entries (16-byte MD5 + 4-byte CRC32) from offset 48, CRC at i+16..i+20

file CRC32: crc = crc32_multiply(crc, crc32_xpow8n(slice_size)) ^ sliceCRC over the full slices; the zero-padded tail is folded in with crc32_combine(crc, crc32_zero_unpad(lastCRC, slice_size - tail), tail)

the Creator packet is logged as the tool fingerprint; MD5-16k values that appear under different names are discarded to avoid false renames; large par2 files are not read past the point where all FileDesc and IFSC packets have been seen
new_for_atlas: Atlas reads Main/FileDesc/UniFileN but not IFSC or Creator. From the small index .par2 alone, IFSC gives every protected file's CRC32, which can be matched to yEnc crc32=, SFV lines, RAR member CRCs or srrDB archive-crc. Creator identifies the tool that made the par2.

title: SABnzbd quick-check and in-download renaming via yEnc CRC32 and MD5-16k
summary: quick_check_set() renames obfuscated downloads by matching the CRC32 built from yEnc part CRCs against the PAR2-derived CRC32 and size. Related opened files: sabnzbd/nzb/file.py (finalize_crc32), sabnzbd/nzb/object.py (verify_nzf_filename), sabnzbd/decoder.py and sabnzbd/misc.py (subject_name_extractor).
metadata_fields: per-article yEnc pcrc32 and decoded size
techniques: finalize_crc32: crc = crc32_combine(crc, article.crc32, article.decoded_size) over articles in order
quick_check_set: a downloaded file not yet matched, with crc32 == par2 filehash and size == par2 size, is renamed to the PAR2 name (subdirectories allowed)

verify_nzf_filename: MD5 of the first 16 KiB of the decoded first article is looked up in the par2 md5of16k map; otherwise the yEnc/uu name= is used if it is not is_probably_obfuscated and the NZB name is not a .par2
subject_name_extractor: first quoted string /"([^"]*)"/, else /\b([\w\-+()' .,]+(?:\[[\w\-/+()' .,]*][\w\-+()' .,]*)*\.[A-Za-z0-9]{2,4})\b/, else the whole subject
new_for_atlas: Atlas parses pcrc32 but should combine the per-part CRCs into a whole-file CRC32. ngPost and newsmangler never write crc32= on the last part. Comparing that CRC with the PAR2-derived one maps obfuscated files with no MD5 work.

title: NZBGet DirectRenamer: MD5-16k and PAR2 set-id detection from file content
summary: NZBGet hashes the first 16 KiB of each file while downloading and recognises par2 files by their packet magic rather than their names. It then renames files from PAR2 FileDesc data. Option docs are in https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nzbgetcom/nzbget/develop/nzbget.conf (opened).
techniques: MD5-16k is trusted only when the article is at least 16 KiB or the file has a single article
par2 detection by content: if the first bytes match Par2::packet_magic ('PAR2\0PKT') the file is par2 and its set id is read from the packet header, whatever its name
once a par2 is loaded with libpar2, Hash16k is mapped to the FileDesc name and queued and completed files are renamed
par2 files of the same set id with different base names, or without a .par2 extension, are renamed '<setid>.volNNN+01.PAR2' (or keep an existing .volXX+YY suffix)
nzbget.conf defaults: ParRename=yes, RarRename=yes, DirectRename=no; DirectRename 'works only for healthy downloads'
new_for_atlas: Classify obfuscated files by the content magic of their first article (PAR2\0PKT, Rar!\x1a\x07, 7z\xbc\xaf\x27\x1c, PK\x03\x04, Matroska \x1aE\xdf\xa3) instead of by name, and group par2 volumes by set id.

title: NZBGet RarRenamer/RarReader: chaining obfuscated RAR volumes from their headers
summary: Rebuilds the order and names of RAR volumes from header data alone, for posts without par2 or posts renamed before the par2 was made. RarReader.cpp (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nzbgetcom/nzbget/develop/daemon/postprocess/RarReader.cpp, opened) holds the flag parsing.
metadata_fields: inner file name continuing across volumes
techniques: RAR3 flags: MAIN_VOLUME 0x0001, MAIN_NEWNUMBERING 0x0010, FILE_SPLITBEFORE 0x0001, FILE_ADDSIZE 0x0100, ENDARC_NEXTVOL 0x0001, ENDARC_VOLNUMBER 0x0008 (volume number in the end-of-archive block); RAR5 volume number from the main header

set building: the first volume has volumeNo 0 and its first file is not split-before; the next volume has volumeNo+1, the same RAR version, and the previous volume has a next volume, with either (front file split-before AND previous back file split-after AND the same file name) or neither split
new names: part%04i.rar for new numbering, or .rar/.r00.. (old numbering: 'r' + (n-1)/100, then two digits)
new_for_atlas: Atlas lists RAR names but should chain obfuscated volumes into sets using only header fields (volume number, split flags, continuing inner file name). This groups random-named files into one archive.

title: Nyuu poster: Message-ID generator, yEnc output and header defaults
summary: Nyuu's default Message-ID carries a millisecond timestamp, and it writes the whole-file crc32 only on the last part. Related opened sources: config.js (default headers), https://raw.githubusercontent.com/animetosho/Nyuu/HEAD/help-full.txt (options), and the Nyuu wiki page listing 20 posting tools (https://github.com/animetosho/Nyuu/wiki/Usenet-Uploaders).
techniques: default Message-ID: 24 random letters alternating upper and lower case + '-' + a 13-digit millisecond timestamp of when the post was generated + '@nyuu'; regex ^[A-Z][a-z]([A-Z][a-z]){11}-\d{13}@
yEnc: '=ybegin part=N total=T line=L size=S name=..', '=ypart begin= end=', '=yend size= part= pcrc32=', plus ' crc32=<whole file>' only on the final part (computed with crc32_combine)
config.js defaults: User-Agent 'Nyuu/<version>', From built from $USER and the hostname, Date from the generation time, Path ''

help-full: default subject '{comment} [{0filenum}/{files}] - "{filename}" yEnc ({part}/{parts}) {filesize} {comment2}'; --yenc-name; --nzb-subject/--nzb-poster rewrite only the NZB; --date overrides Date, the Message-ID timestamp and NZB dates (to 'obfuscate your timezone'); --keep-message-id; -a 700K; --article-line-size 128; the {timestamp} and ${rand(N)} tokens change for every post
new_for_atlas: The shape of the Message-ID local part identifies Nyuu even with a custom domain (e.g. @PRiVATE). Its 13-digit timestamp orders articles and links the parts of one upload even when subject, poster and yEnc name are randomized. The NZB poster and subject may differ from the real headers.

title: ngPost: full header obfuscation (UUID subject, random From) and its yEnc output
summary: In ngPost's obfuscation mode the Subject is the same UUID as the Message-ID local part, and From is random. Only four headers are sent. The README (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mbruel/ngPost/master/README.md) and src/NgPost.h were also opened.
techniques: obfuscated Subject = Message-ID local part = QUuid Id128 (32 hex chars); Message-ID '<uuid32@ngPost>', with the signature configurable via msg_id
From = 13 chars from [A-Za-z0-9] + '@' + signature + '.com'; random by default, --gen_from gives a new one per post
only From, Newsgroups, Subject and Message-ID are sent (no Date, User-Agent or X-Newsposter), so Date and injection fields come from the server
plain subject: '"<filename>" (part/total)'; yEnc '=ybegin part= total= line=128 size= name=', '=ypart begin= end=', '=yend size= pcrc32=' printed as hex without zero padding (no part=, no crc32=)
default article size 716800; --gen_name random RAR name of 17 chars; --gen_pass 13 chars; -m 'password=...' goes into the NZB head; failed articles are retried with a new UUID
new_for_atlas: This gives an exact header and yEnc fingerprint for ngPost uploads. Because the Subject is just the Message-ID, it carries no grouping information, and the whole-file CRC has to be built by combining pcrc32 values.

title: newsmangler and GoPostStuff: Message-IDs that carry time and part number, plus X-Newsposter
summary: newsmangler's Message-ID contains the send time and the part number, and its domain is the NNTP server hostname it posts to. GoPostStuff (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/madcowfred/GoPostStuff/master/article.go, opened) puts a nanosecond time in the ID. Both add an X-Newsposter header.
techniques: newsmangler Message-ID '<%.5f.%d@%s>' = unix time with 5 decimals, the part number, and conf['server']['hostname'] (the posting server)

newsmangler X-Newsposter 'newsmangler <ver> (<yenc mode>) - https://github.com/madcowfred/newsmangler'; subject '<title> [NN/total] - "<file>" yEnc (PP/parts)' with zero-padded counters; yEnc line=128 and '=yend size= part= pcrc32=' (no crc32)
GoPostStuff: Message-ID '<%d$gps@gopoststuff>' from time.Now().UnixNano(); X-Newsposter 'gopoststuff <ver> - https://github.com/madcowfred/gopoststuff'; subject '%s [%d/%d] - "%s" yEnc (%d/%d)'
new_for_atlas: Add Message-ID parsers that recover the part number and send time (newsmangler) or nanosecond time (GoPostStuff) from posts with random subjects. The Message-ID domain can reveal the posting provider.

title: NxG Upper: Message-IDs derived from a shared 'NxG header'
summary: NxG Upper computes every article's Message-ID from a 28-byte NxG header, so anyone holding the header can fetch the post without an NZB or a search engine. NxG Loader downloads that way. Later versions add options to obfuscate the poster, the subject and the yEnc header.
metadata_fields: article counts for data and par2
techniques: header = base64( the 21-char random string with its tail overwritten by ':<dataArticles>:<par2Articles>' ), e.g. 'Vpjnfhd01U288Q:415:49' -> VnBqbmZoZDAxVTI4OFE6NDE1OjQ5; the full 21-char string is also used as the rar/par2 file name
per article: sha256 hex of '<NXGHEADER>:<data|par2>:<n>'; Message-ID = hex[0:40] + '@' + hex[40:61] + '.' + hex[61:64]
new_for_atlas: Recognise this Message-ID shape. If an NxG header is ever found (forums, NZB meta, an X-NXG header from Postie), Atlas can generate every Message-ID of the post and check its articles directly.

title: Postie obfuscation policies: random yEnc name per article and a Date header shifted up to 6 hours
summary: Postie, a Go poster 'inspired by Nyuu-Obfuscation', has full, partial and none policies set separately for data and PAR2 files. Under 'full' the client-set Date header is randomized within the last 6 hours, so it cannot be trusted. The config reference at https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/javi11/postie@v0.0.3 was also opened.
techniques: full: random Subject; yEnc header filename 'Randomized for every article'; Date 'Randomized within the last 6 hours'; poster 'Random for each article'; NXG header not added
partial: obfuscated subject and filename, but the same yEnc name and poster for every article in a post, and the real posting date
separate par2_obfuscation_policy, so PAR2 files can stay easy to find while data is obfuscated
config: posting.message_id_format random|ngx; post_headers.add_ngx_header ('X-NXG'); article_size_in_bytes 750000; par2 redundancy '1n*1.2', volume_size 150MB, max_input_slices 4000
new_for_atlas: For time-based grouping, rely on server-side times (Injection-Date, NNTP-Posting-Date, article numbers) rather than the client Date. Under 'partial', a yEnc name and poster that stay constant are still good grouping keys.

title: Spotweb/Spotnet: signed spot headers, poster key and spotter id
summary: Spotnet packs category, size, key id and an RSA signature into the From address and carries the spot XML in X- headers. Spotweb verifies the signature and derives a stable spotter id from the poster's public key. Also opened: Services_Signing_Base.php, Services_Format_Util.php and Services_Nntp_SpotReading.php in the same repo.
techniques: header signature check: RSA over title + (the header part after @, without its trailing signature) + poster, using the network key for that keyid
self-signed spots (keyid 7; or keyid 2 with filesize 999 and a long key) must have sha1('<'+messageid+'>') starting with '0000', a hashcash proof of work
full spot: RSA check of '<messageid>' (or the X-XML-Signature) with X-User-Signature and X-User-Key
spotterid = base64(little-endian crc32(base64_decode(pubkey))) with '/', '+' and '=' removed
subcategories are parsed from tokens like a09b04c00d05d15d11; spots after 2010 (stamp > 1293870080) or with keyid != 1 must be signed
new_for_atlas: A signed, verifiable poster identity: use spotterid as a stable poster key in place of a random From. Spot headers carry size and category, and the X-XML carries the NZB segment IDs and the spot's own metadata.

title: newz[NZB] uploader signature header: a real obfuscated binary post's headers
summary: An uploader group adds a 'Verify-Signature-newzNZB' header so its posts can be checked against impostors. The example header block shows a cross-posted upload with an obfuscated subject, a newsmangler-style Message-ID and an X-Newsposter value. The README is at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/scriptzteam/Usenet_-_Verify-Signature-newzNZB/master/README.md (opened).
techniques: the Message-ID local part '<unix>.<5 decimals>.<part>' matches newsmangler; part 110 equals (110/196) in the subject, and 1484241488 (2017-01-12 17:18:08 UTC) equals the 'Signature made' time, while the Date header is 17:21:59 UTC
the signature tuple embeds the Message-ID: ('-----BEGIN newzNZB SIGNATURE-----', <base64>, '<MSG_ID@PRiVATE>', '-----END ...')
new_for_atlas: Uploader-specific signature headers and constant tokens ([newzNZB], Organization: PRiVATE, X-Newsposter) group a poster's uploads even when names are hashed. The Message-ID timestamp and part number survive obfuscation.

title: Leo's notes: server-added X-Received-Body-CRC and X-Received-Bytes on a binary article
summary: A captured NNTP session against news.newsdemon.com shows an article with a body CRC added by the server, 'Path: not-for-mail', and a Message-ID in Nyuu's shape with a private domain.
techniques: the Message-ID local part has 24 letters alternating case + '-' + 13-digit ms (Nyuu's generator) with the domain changed; 1530199484291 = 2018-06-28 15:24:44 UTC, 26 s before the Date header
X-Received-Body-CRC appears to be a CRC of the article body added by the server, readable through HEAD/HDR without fetching BODY
Path 'not-for-mail' shows this provider strips the routing path, so Path-based tracing fails here
new_for_atlas: Where a provider adds X-Received-Body-CRC and X-Received-Bytes, matching identical articles across reposts or servers needs only HDR, no body downloads. Recognise Nyuu Message-IDs whatever their domain.

title: RFC 5536/5537: injection trace fields (Injection-Info, Injection-Date, Path diagnostics, Xref)
summary: These RFCs say which trace data an injecting server adds and what a posting tool can or cannot control. RFC 5536 (https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5536.html) and INN's posting-account note (https://lists.isc.org/pipermail/inn-workers/2014-November/018334.html) were also opened.
metadata_fields: Injection-Info: posting-host, posting-account, logging-data, mail-complaints-to, x-*
techniques: Path diagnostics: '!!' (verified), '!.SEEN.<id>', '!.MISMATCH.<id>', '!.POSTED[.<fqdn-or-ip>]' prepended by the injecting agent
Injection-Date: if one exists it MUST NOT be changed; otherwise it MUST be added, except when the proto-article already has both Message-ID and Date. Posting agents must never create Injection-Info
before re-injection, Xref must be removed and Injection-Info/Path/trace fields renamed or removed; injecting agents may reject articles that already carry NNTP-Posting-Host without Injection-*
INN adds posting-account=<login> to Injection-Info only when addinjectionpostingaccount is true (default false)
new_for_atlas: Whether Injection-Date is present tells you whether the client supplied Date+Message-ID itself (Nyuu does; ngPost sends no Date), which is a tool fingerprint. Collect Injection-Info posting-account/posting-host and the !.POSTED host for every article sampled per poster, not one per release.

title: PAR2 2.0 specification: packet catalogue, ID definitions and Creator fingerprints
summary: The full packet list, including optional packets, and how the File ID and Recovery Set ID are defined. Also opened: the GitHub-hosted copy (https://parchive.github.io/doc/Parity Volume Set Specification v2.0.html) and the Creator strings in ParPar (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/animetosho/ParPar/master/bin/parpar.js) and par2cmdline (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Parchive/par2cmdline/master/src/creatorpacket.cpp).
techniques: File ID = MD5(MD5-16k || length || ASCII name), and Recovery Set ID = MD5(Main packet body), so both change when file names change. For twins compare FileDesc full MD5 + length, not FileID or set id
IFSC = MD5 and CRC32 per slice (the CRC32 used by zip/Ethernet); the Creator packet is required in every PAR file
Creator strings: ParPar 'ParPar v<ver> <arch> [https://github.com/animetosho/parpar]' (includes CPU arch); library 'ParPar (library) v<ver> [...]'; par2cmdline 'Created by par2cmdline version X.Y.Z.'
the spec suggests putting Main/FileDesc/IFSC at the end so recovery packets are equal-sized, one per Usenet message
new_for_atlas: Parse Creator, CommASCI/CommUni, IFSC and the packed packets. Creator plus slice size form a fingerprint of who made the par2. Never use FileID or set id as a content key across reposts with renamed files.

title: NZB file format specification
summary: Defines NZB elements and attributes, and the meta types indexers and posters use to carry the name and password alongside obfuscated posts.
metadata_fields: file@date (unix time the server saw the article)
techniques: 'segment counter (xx/yy)' rewritten to '(1/yy)' in file@subject; yy lets a client check completeness
several password metas are allowed and all may be tried; type names are case-sensitive and private ones use an X- prefix
new_for_atlas: When importing NZBs from uploaders, keep the meta title/password/tag/X-* values and the per-file poster/date as evidence. Posting tools such as Nyuu's --nzb-poster/--nzb-subject can make these differ from the real headers.

title: RAR5 technote: archive header fields that identify archives and posters
summary: RAR5 headers carry per-file times, host OS, compression settings, hashes, encryption salts, Unix owner names and comments. For files split across volumes, only the last part holds the CRC of the whole unpacked file.
metadata_fields: main archive flags (volume 0x0001, volume number present 0x0002, solid 0x0004, recovery record 0x0008, locked 0x0010) and volume number
locator record (quick open / recovery record offsets)
file flags, unpacked size, attributes, mtime, Data CRC32
compression info (version, solid, method, dictionary size)
extra 0x01 encryption: KDF count, 16-byte salt, 16-byte IV, 12-byte check value
extra 0x06 Unix owner: user name, group name, uid, gid
service headers CMT, QO, ACL, STM, RR
techniques: Data CRC32 / BLAKE2sp for split files: 'for all file parts except the last' they cover only that volume's packed data, so read the LAST volume's file header for the CRC srrDB calls archive-crc
volume number: 'Not present for first volume, 1 for second volume, 2 for third and so on'
a random salt/IV per archive means the same salt in two posts = the same archive (a twin), while a different salt with the same inner CRC/mtime = re-RARed (an alt)
new_for_atlas: Atlas lists inner names and sizes. Add: inner CRC32 and BLAKE2sp taken from the last volume, mtime and host OS, Unix owner, comment, compression method and dictionary size, and encryption salt and check value, as twin/alt and poster keys.

title: 7-Zip 7zFormat.txt: header property IDs
summary: The official 7z layout: a signature header pointing to the next header (with its CRC), and property IDs for per-file names, times, attributes, CRCs and encoded (encrypted) headers.
techniques: with encrypted headers (kEncodedHeader) names are hidden, but NextHeaderCRC/size and the coder properties still fingerprint the exact archive
per-file kCRC (digests) plus kMTime/kCTime/kATime identify the same inner file inside different archives (alts)
new_for_atlas: Atlas lists 7z names and sizes. Add per-file CRC, the three timestamps, attributes and comment, plus the start-header NextHeaderCRC, as a key for header-encrypted 7z volumes.

title: Matroska RFC 9559 identity fields and the x264 encoder SEI string
summary: Matroska Segment Info holds a random 128-bit SegmentUUID (shown by MediaInfo as 'Unique ID' and used by newznab UID matching), the mux date and the muxing and writing apps. x264 (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mirror/x264/master/encoder/set.c, opened) embeds its build and full option string in an SEI message, which identifies an encode.
techniques: SegmentUUID equal = the same mux (a twin or the same release re-wrapped); different SegmentUUID but the same x264 options string and same video size = the same encode re-muxed
x264 SEI text: 'x264 - core <build><version> - H.264/MPEG-4 AVC codec - Copyleft 2003-2024 - http://www.videolan.org/x264.html - options: <param2string>', present near the start of the stream
new_for_atlas: Atlas parses MKV tracks, chapters and HDR. It should also store SegmentUUID, DateUTC, MuxingApp/WritingApp/Title and the encoder SEI string (x264/x265). These separate twins (same mux) from alts (same encode, new mux) from different encodes of the same film.

title: pyReScene SRR/SRS formats: stored RAR headers, OSO/ISDb hash and sample track signatures
summary: An SRR file stores the original RAR volume headers, small files kept inside it (nfo, sfv...) and an OpenSubtitles (ISDb) hash of the main media file. An SRS file stores signatures that rebuild samples. Also opened: resample/main.py, and the PHP SRR parser NNTmux uses (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DariusIII/rarinfo/master/SrrInfo.php, plus Par2Info.php and RarInfo.php in that repo).
metadata_fields: 0x6B SrrOsoHash (file size u64, OSO hash u64, name)
0x71 SrrRarFile (one per RAR volume, followed by that volume's original RAR headers)
SRS FileData 'SRSF' (app name, sample name, size, CRC32)
SRS TrackData 'SRST' (track number, data length, match_offset, signature bytes)
Chromaprint fingerprint + duration for FLAC/MP3 samples
techniques: the OSO hash block is described as a '64bit chksum of the first and last 64k (ISDb hash)', i.e. the OpenSubtitles moviehash
SRR RAR blocks reproduce every volume's file headers, giving the scene RAR names, volume sizes and inner-file CRCs to compare with what was posted
SRS lets you check a posted sample: the sample CRC32 equals srrDB 'store-real-crc', and the track signature bytes locate the sample inside the main file
