new_for_atlas: Atlas already computes the moviehash: look it up against SRR OSO blocks and srrDB isdbhash to get a scene name directly. Parse .srr/.srs found in posts as authoritative name and CRC sources.

title: srrDB API v1 search keywords (archive-crc, archive-size, isdbhash, rarhash, store-real-crc)
summary: srrDB can be searched by the CRC and size of the file inside the RAR, by the ISDb/OSO hash, by a hash of the RAR set, and by sample name or CRC. That turns content keys into scene release names. Also opened: https://www.srrdb.com/help (keyword meanings) and the scenecrc.py gist (https://gist.github.com/dawtmaytrikx/b69c6058dd127c04ebee05025fec28db).
techniques: keywords: r: (exact release), archive-crc:XXXXXXXX (CRC of a file archived in the RARs), archive-size:, isdbhash: (Internet Subtitles Database hash), rarhash: ('a unique string generated based on the set of rar-files'), store-real-filename: (sample name stored in the SRS), store-real-crc: ('CRC32 of the complete sample'), compressed:yes|no, nfo:, srs:yes|no|broken, imdb:, group:, category:, foreign:, confirmed:, order:, skip:

scenecrc.py flow: details by name -> search r: -> store-real-filename for <name>, -sample, .sample -> archive-crc using zlib.crc32 of the whole file; accept only one result with exactly one archived-files entry whose size (and optionally crc) match, then rename
new_for_atlas: Query archive-crc with the inner CRC32 from the last RAR volume (or the PAR2 IFSC-derived CRC of an unpacked mkv), isdbhash with Atlas's moviehash, and store-real-crc with a sample's CRC. Require a size match before accepting the name.

title: predb.ovh API: size, file count, pre time and nuke data for matching
summary: A public PreDB API with search, a live endpoint without caching, RSS and a WebSocket stream. Each release includes size and original file count, which can be matched against post metadata.
metadata_fields: nuke {id, typeId 1 nuke/2 unnuke/3 modnuke/4 delpre/5 undelpre, type, preId, reason, net, nukeAt}
techniques: endpoints: GET / (q goes to SphinxSearch, e.g. '@cat EBOOK'; count, page, offset, id), /live (rate 2 per 20s), /rss, /teams, /stats, /ws for near-realtime
matching: PreDB name candidates are confirmed when the release's total size and file count fit the pre's size and files
new_for_atlas: Use files and size as a check before renaming, and use nuke type/reason (delpre, modnuke) to drop or demote names. The /ws stream gives low-latency pre ingestion.

title: NZBHydra2 DuplicateDetector: grouping the same release across indexers
summary: NZBHydra2 groups search results from different indexers as duplicates when their normalized titles match and group, poster, age and size are consistent. The defaults come from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/theotherp/nzbhydra2/master/core/src/main/resources/config/baseConfig.yml (opened).
techniques: candidates must share normalizeTitle = lower(title) with [ .\-_] removed; results from the same indexer are never duplicates
if both groups are known they must be equal; if both posters are known they must be equal; if only one of group/poster is known, both thresholds are doubled
age: |date1-date2| in hours <= duplicateAgeThreshold (default 2.0); size: |s1-s2| / mean * 100 <= duplicateSizeThresholdInPercent (default 1.0)
grouping is greedy, newest first; sameness is not transitive
new_for_atlas: Cheap metadata-only rules for linking Atlas releases to other indexers' entries, and for grouping reposts before the content checks that define twins.

title: Sonarr/Radarr parser: hashed-name rejection list and reversed-title detection; nzbToMedia rename scripts
summary: Sonarr keeps a dated list of obfuscated release-name shapes seen in the wild and reverses titles that were posted backwards. Radarr (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Radarr/Radarr/develop/src/NzbDrone.Core/Parser/Parser.cs) and nzbToMedia (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/clinton-hall/nzbToMedia/master/core/scene_exceptions.py) were also opened.
techniques: RejectHashedReleasesRegexes: ^[0-9a-zA-Z]{32}; ^[a-z0-9]{24}$; ^[A-Z]{11}\d{3}$ and ^[a-z]{12}\d{3}$ ('Format seen on some NZBGeek releases'); ^Backup_\d{5,}S\d{2}-\d{2}$; ^123$ (Dec 2014); ^abc$ (Jan 2015); ^abc[-_. ]xyz (2020); ^b00bs$; ^\d{6}_\d{2}$ (Aug 2018); ^[0-9a-zA-Z]{30}, {26}, {39}, {24} (Dec 2020/Jan 2021)
ReversedTitleRegex (?:^|[-._ ])(p027|p0801|\d{2,3}E-?\d{2}S)[-._ ] -> reverse the title before parsing

nzbToMedia reverse tokens: \.\d{2}e\d{2}s\., \.[pi]0801\., \.p027\., \b[45]62[xh]\., \.yarulb\., \.ld[.-]?bew\., \.reporp\., \.kcaper\., \.lanretni\. ...; a garbage name is ^[a-zA-Z0-9]*$, which is then renamed to the job name
nzbToMedia runs a rename.sh/.bat found in the download, applying its 'mv'/'Move' lines, and runs par2 repair to restore names
new_for_atlas: Add the dated list of known obfuscation shapes and the reversed-title detector. Parse rename scripts (and rename.par2) inside posts as explicit name maps.

title: Newsbin forum: obfuscated subjects seen in the wild and what PAR2 can recover
summary: Users of the Newsbin client posted examples of unreadable subjects. The developer (Quade) said decoding them is not possible from headers alone and proposed probing the first RAR chunk instead. A related thread (https://forums.newsbin.com/viewtopic.php?p=222097, opened) notes that PAR2 usually covers only the RARs, not the files inside.
techniques: example shapes: '5759b30bd7b1f346127d4cb87d100071[01/13] - "150b6231...6a075bac.0"' (32-hex prefix + 64-hex name + numeric extension) and '4NTN3luRnKnbnQ0l3wwNl4[01/10] - "MVAsuvPKjogTvLSnL9Vq.par2"'
some posts are ROT13-encoded subjects with normal extensions; others use numbered extensions .1 .2; every post has a different named poster although they appear to come from one source
Quade: 'Newsbin can sample the first chunk of the of the first rar file and tell you what filenames it finds'; 'the only way to download it and know what's there is the NZB'
PAR2 'typically only covers the rars and not the inner files'; SFV helps 'if it's in the set'; renaming falls back to the NZB file name
new_for_atlas: Test the ROT13 and reversed forms of subjects. Treat 'hex.N' numeric extensions as split volumes. Read the first RAR article to get inner names when the subject is useless.

title: r/usenet (via a redlib mirror): header-based vs source-based indexing; r/newznab proposal for per-RAR hashes in NZBs
summary: Users explain that fully obfuscated posts cannot be indexed from headers, so indexers depend on uploaders who send NZBs or on uploads by their own staff. A 2013 r/newznab thread (https://pol1.lr.ggtyler.dev/r/newznab/comments/1dfuqi/a_worthwhile_modification/c9qa2h3/?context=3, opened) proposed adding a hash for every RAR to the NZB, so a missing RAR could be found in other posts.
techniques: header-based indexing (rebuild NZBs from subjects, posters and file names) 'was correct 10 years ago'; now 'everything is obfuscated so it's not possible anymore', and source-based indexing relies on uploaders who 'share the nzbs'
DMCA takedowns remove the articles themselves, so every NZB pointing at them fails regardless of where it came from

2013 proposal (newsmangler test, backward-compatible XML): indexers index per-file hashes and serve the locations where each hash was seen ('NZBv2'/'hashMap'), so clients can fetch a missing RAR from another post
new_for_atlas: Ingesting uploader NZBs is a primary data source, not a fallback. A content-hash-to-locations map (Atlas's twin keys) is exactly the 'hashMap' idea and can serve repair and alternate-source lookups.

title: GIAC/SANS paper 'Forensic Primer: Usenet Evidence'
summary: A forensic paper on tracing Usenet posts. It uses the Message-ID to find the injecting server, Path to reconstruct routing, and NZB Message-IDs as search terms, and notes that From is easily faked while forging a Message-ID 'would require administrator access' to a server.
techniques: Message-ID right-hand side and Path lead to the injecting server, then its logs to the posting IP
Path example traced from newsreader30.eweka.nl through relays to border1.nntp.dca.giganews.com
keyword-search disk images for NZB segment Message-IDs to find downloaded parts
new_for_atlas: Nothing new technically; it is the only academic-style source found and confirms that Message-ID and Path are the hard-to-forge fields (but see 'Path: not-for-mail' providers).

title: A Forensic Primer for Usenet Evidence (Mark Lachniet, SANS GIAC GCFA Gold paper, accepted Jan 2006)
summary: A forensic walkthrough of NNTP propagation and of recovering and attributing Usenet binaries: RFC 1036 headers, yEnc/RAR/PAR2/NZB signatures, carving parts from disk and putting them back together, and the subpoena chain from Message-ID to subscriber. It says From is unreliable and treats server-assigned identifiers (Message-ID, Path) as the evidence.
metadata_fields: RFC 1036 mandatory: From, Date, Newsgroups, Subject, Path, Message-ID
RFC 1036 optional: Reply-To, Sender, Followup-To, Expires, References, Control, Distribution, Organization, Keywords, Summary, Approved, Lines, Xref
PAR2 magic 'PAR2\0PKT' plus a trailing string naming the program that created it
NZB '<!DOCTYPE nzb' ... '</nzb>' listing Message-IDs and groups
techniques: The Message-ID right-hand side identifies the originating server, which leads to that server's logs and then the ISP subscriber
Each Path hop is a server that may hold logs
Carved yEnc segments are matched by yEnc name and CRC; RAR volume order is inferred from disk sector order
The PAR2 creator string identifies the software that built the set
Message-IDs from NZBs are searched for on disk to find downloaded segments
new_for_atlas: Use two uploader-toolchain features Atlas does not read yet: the PAR2 Creator packet text and the Message-ID right-hand side. The rest confirms parsing Atlas already does.

title: On Dominant Characteristics of Residential Broadband Internet Traffic (Maier, Feldmann, Paxson, Allman, ACM IMC 2009)
summary: In a large European DSL dataset, NNTP was about 4.8% of bytes in one trace and 2.2% in another; 6.5% on non-P2P lines and 0.6% on P2P lines. Almost all NNTP bytes were binary transfers, with RAR among the most common file types. NNTP got about 10x the per-flow throughput of P2P and used many parallel flows, which suggests bulk-download clients.
techniques: Bro dynamic protocol detection with an NNTP recognizer the authors added: about one third of NNTP volume was off port 119 (through proxy port 3128), and 95.3% of port-119 traffic was NNTP
Per-line application mix, splitting P2P from non-P2P lines
Parallel-flow and throughput analysis to infer bulk NZB-style downloaders
new_for_atlas: Nothing new for indexing. It is context showing that binary NNTP use is bulk, RAR-dominated and many-connection.

title: Analysis of New Trends in the Web from a Network Perspective (Fabian Schneider, TU Berlin PhD thesis 2010). Ch. 7 'Today's Usenet Usage: Characterizing NNTP Traffic' (also Kim, Schneider, Ager, Feldmann, IEEE Global Internet 2010)
summary: The thesis that contains the Kim et al. Usenet study, Chapter 7 from p. 99, with sections on command popularity, binary-to-text encoding, content types of binary files, newsgroups, news servers and throughput. Reported findings: NNTP is up to 5% of residential traffic, a small fraction of lines use it heavily, almost all traffic comes from paid monthly-subscription servers, and about 99% of content is typical file-sharing material (archives, multimedia).
metadata_fields: news server identity, commercial vs ISP (7.4.7)
techniques: Passive capture of residential lines with Bro NNTP analysis to classify each downloaded article's encoding and payload type
Mapping server IPs to commercial providers
new_for_atlas: Context only. The chapter body (pp. 99-112) could not be extracted, and the IEEE and ResearchGate copies of Kim et al. 2010 were blocked.

title: Remote Measurement of NNTP Internet Traffic (T. Surmacz, Wroclaw Univ. of Technology, MEASUREMENT 2009, pp. 214-218)
summary: Built a weighted server-to-server graph of Usenet propagation using only headers fetched over XHDR/XOVER from many servers. Data: 322,477 article headers, 71,236 unique articles and 258 distinct paths (pl.*, 7-14 Feb 2009). A follow-up EUROCAST 2011 chapter, 'Bandwidth Usage Optimization for NNTP Protocol', deals with the same article being sent in parallel over redundant links.
techniques: Header-only collection with XHDR/XOVER (RFC 2980), comparing per-group article-number ranges between sessions and fetching only new ones
Path parsed into a directed server-adjacency graph, with edges weighted by Bytes
Per-edge dedup by Message-ID
Comparing Message-ID sets across servers to estimate articles each node missed and correct edge weights
new_for_atlas: Atlas reads Path and injection headers from one ARTICLE per release. Running XHDR/HDR Path (and NNTP-Posting-Host/Injection-Info where the server allows HDR on them) across all segment numbers would give per-segment injection points cheaply, expose releases with mixed injection points, and support diffing Message-ID sets across providers for completion/takedown.

title: Handling Information Overload on Usenet: Advanced Caching Methods for News (Jan Ingvoldstad, Univ. of Oslo Cand. Scient. thesis, 2001)
summary: Reports a mid-2001 full feed of about 280 GB/day across about 1.5M articles. Admins estimated 95-98% of volume as binaries, which are a small share of article count; a text-only feed was about 2 GB/day in 1999. It argues that NOV/XOVER metadata is cheap while ARTICLE/BODY each cause a costly read event, and that filtering binaries by group name does not work.
metadata_fields: NOV/XOVER: Subject, From, Date, Message-ID, References, Bytes, Lines
feed size and article count growth
techniques: Header-only feeds with prefetch of likely-read articles
Correlating XOVER and ARTICLE commands per group to predict reads
Identifying binaries by size rather than by group name
new_for_atlas: Nothing new. It confirms Atlas's XOVER-first design.

title: UsenetDHT: A Low-Overhead Design for Usenet (Sit, Morris, Kaashoek, USENIX NSDI 2008)
summary: A measured design that keeps article bodies once in a DHT and floods only metadata. Measurements: the MIT CSAIL feed was about 1M articles/day (about 10% of the full feed, 2.5 MB/s); the full feed was over 1 TB/day new (top servers 3 TB/day received); text was about 1 GB/day from about 400k articles. Median binary article was 240 KB versus 2.4 KB for text, and clients read less than 1% of received articles.
metadata_fields: SHA-1 content hash of article (DHash key)
overview metadata (subject, author, newsgroups) per group in BerkeleyDB
techniques: Content-addressed article storage that is independent of the Message-ID
Separating metadata flooding (TAKEDHT) from body storage
Classifying articles as binary or text by size (240 KB vs 2.4 KB medians)
new_for_atlas: Address segments by content as well as Message-ID, for example pcrc32 + begin/end + size or a hash of the decoded part, so a repost with fresh Message-IDs collapses onto the existing segment records.

title: An Estimate of Infringing Use of the Internet (Envisional for NBC Universal, Jan 2011), Usenet section 2.6.3
summary: Sampled 100 random newsgroups from Giganews and took the last 100 complete files or messages per group. Results: 3.2% text, 93.4% copyrighted, 2.3% likely copyrighted, 1.1% unknown. It estimates up to 0.5M regular Usenet pirates and puts Usenet at 0.5-1% of internet use (Sandvine: 4.7% of traffic in Europe).
techniques: Random group sampling with the last 100 complete posts per group
Manual classification of copyright status
new_for_atlas: Nothing new. Context only; the report gives no method for identifying content from subjects or filenames.

title: Picturing Usenet: Mapping Computer-Mediated Collective Action (Turner, Smith, Fisher, Welser, JCMC 10(4), 2005; Netscan data)
summary: Uses Microsoft Research Netscan data (about 1.2B messages, 48M identities, 150k groups over 5 years) to map Usenet with 'social accounting metadata'. alt.binaries grows when measured by posts and shrinks when measured by replies. Binary posters show a distinct signature: automated tools, many initiated threads of one message each, and no replies.
metadata_fields: posts per author, authors per thread
techniques: Treemaps scaled by posts vs replies
AuthorLines and crowd plots: a 'tall thin plume' marks automated posting
Spammer/binary-poster profile: many initiated threads, one message each, zero replies
new_for_atlas: Build behavioral profiles per poster and per posting host (posts/day, thread-initiation ratio, group spread, active hours) to cluster automated uploaders that rotate random From names.

title: Cleanfeed Usenet spam filter (Perl source, crooks/cleanfeed)
summary: A production INN filter that detects binaries with regexes and catches floods/EMPs using rate-limited hash histories keyed on posting host, body, groups and sender+subject. It shows the server-side way to tie many differently-subjected articles to one injection source.
metadata_fields: Message-ID, Newsgroups, Followup-To, References, Subject, From, Sender, Reply-To, Organization
User-Agent, X-Mailer, X-Newsreader, X-Newsposter, X-Poster, X-Cancelled-By
techniques: yEnc detection '(?:^|\n)=ybegin\s+(.+)' requiring line=, size= and name=
uuencode 'begin [0-7]{3,4} name.ext'; four or more 'M[\x20-\x60]{60,61}' lines
base64 binary: more than 150 lines matching '[A-Za-z0-9+/]{59,76}'
Fuzzy body MD5: lowercase, drop quoted lines and 7-70 char tokens, keep only a-z0-9 (cutoff 5, ceiling 85, 7200 s)
PHL = posting host + line count (20/80/3600 s)
PHN = posting host + sorted Newsgroups (150/200/1800 s)
PHR = posting host or Path-derived server for flood groups (10/80/3600 s)
FSL = Sender/From + Subject with trailing digits stripped + line count (20/40/1800 s)
Posting host taken from Injection-Info posting-host, then NNTP-Posting-Host; injection host from Injection-Info, then X-Trace, then Path
maxgroups = 14 crosspost cap
new_for_atlas: Reuse PHN, PHL and FSL as uploader-session fingerprints for grouping random-subject segments: posting host + sorted groups, and sender + subject with counters stripped + lines. Adopt the posting-host precedence chain and detect uuencode/base64 binaries.

title: FAQ: The Newsgroup Care Cancel Cookbook
summary: Defines the third-party cancel format and the Breidbart thresholds that spam cancellers used. It also gives a deterministic rule for deciding which copy of a duplicated (stutter/spew) post is the original.
metadata_fields: Path pseudosites: cyberspam, bincancel, mmfcancel, spewcancel, udpcancel, retromod, htmlcancel
techniques: Recognise third-party cancels by '!cyberspam' in Path
Derive the cancel Message-ID from the target's so duplicate cancels collapse
Stutter/spew rule: keep the copy with the earliest Date; on a tie keep the lowest ASCII Message-ID
EMP spam scored with BI over any 45-day window
new_for_atlas: Pick the canonical twin deterministically: earliest Date, then lowest Message-ID. Watch cancel control messages ('<cancel.' IDs, Control: cancel) to mark segments as removed.

title: Breidbart Index (Wikipedia)
summary: The standard Usenet cancel index, which weighs crossposting and multiposting of substantively identical articles differently. It includes the BI2 and Skirvin-Breidbart (SBI) variants and the thresholds per hierarchy.
techniques: BI = sum over copies of sqrt(n_groups); limit 20 within 45 days
BI2 = sqrt(n) + n/2
SBI counts Followup-To groups instead of Newsgroups
Per-hierarchy limits: de.* 5 in 7 days; hamster.de.* 3 in 30 days; nl.* SBI 10; at.* ACI 11 in 45 days
'Substantively identical' covers byte-identical copies, per-group minimal edits, and the same advert or signature
new_for_atlas: Compute a spew/repost score per release fingerprint (sum of sqrt(groups) over copies within a window) to flag flooded or spam uploads and to rank twins.

title: perl-nocem(8): NoCeM-on-spool for INN (Debian manpage)
summary: INN's processor for PGP-signed NoCeM notices, which list Message-IDs (with their newsgroups) that an issuer has flagged. Notices are verified against a dedicated keyring and the listed articles are cancelled locally, filtered by an issuer:type allowlist.
metadata_fields: notice body: Message-ID followed by newsgroups
techniques: gpg --status-fd=1 --verify (or gpgv) against pathetc/pgp/ncmring.gpg
Notices fed from news.lists.filters through a newsfeeds entry (Tc,Wf,Ap)
local_want_cancel_id($msgid,$artid,$groups,$hdrs) hook for per-article decisions
new_for_atlas: Ingest signed NoCeM notices from news.lists.filters as third-party spam/abuse labels keyed by Message-ID.

title: An Open Digest-based Technique for Spam Detection (Damiani, De Capitani di Vimercati, Paraboschi, Samarati, c. 2004): analysis of Nilsimsa
summary: A formal analysis of the Nilsimsa locality-sensitive digest (from the cmeclax remailer operator) for detecting bulk messages. It sets match thresholds from false-match probabilities and tests the digest against random addition, synonym substitution and targeted 'aimed addition' attacks.
techniques: 5-character sliding window, trigrams hashed into 256 buckets, bucket counts thresholded at the median to give 256 bits
Compare value = matching bits - 128 (range -128..128)
Threshold 24 gives about 1.35e-4 false-match probability; threshold 54 gives about 7.39e-12
Robust to random appends up to 250% and about 20% synonym or character substitution; a prologue of about 10% defeats it, so combine with MD5
new_for_atlas: Near-duplicate digests (Nilsimsa or TLSH) of NFO, description and subject text to link releases from the same group or uploader when filenames are obfuscated.

title: Botnet Judo: Fighting Spam with Itself (Pitsillidis et al., NDSS 2010)
summary: Infers the generating template (a regex) behind machine-generated messages from samples of one source. It separates invariant anchors from dictionary macros and random-noise macros, and the resulting signatures had near-zero false positives.
metadata_fields: body text (dates, IPs and MIME boundaries tokenised)
techniques: Anchors: common substrings of length >= 6 in all samples (suffix tree), then LCS ordering
Gap classification: dictionary macro if a 99%-confidence completeness test passes, otherwise a noise macro using the smallest POSIX class with fixed length when lengths match
Micro-anchors on punctuation such as '.' and '@'; every signature must contain at least one anchor or dictionary node
k = 1000 samples inferred in under 10 s; incremental updates take 50-100 ms
new_for_atlas: Infer per-uploader or per-tool templates for obfuscated subjects, filenames, Message-IDs and From (e.g. '[[:alnum:]]{32} [nn/NN] ... yEnc'). Use them to group random-named segments into posts and attribute new obfuscated uploads to known sources.

title: Can Pseudonymity Really Guarantee Privacy? (Rao & Rohatgi, USENIX Security 2000)
summary: Linked pseudonymous Usenet authors (53,914 sci.crypt posts, over 10,758 personas) using body stylometry alone. Pairs were linked correctly 58.8% of the time with about 5k words per pseudonym and 80.9% with about 10k words, at roughly 2% false positives.
metadata_fields: From (used only for ground-truth personas, with name and address variants merged)
body function-word frequencies (headers, signatures and quotes stripped)
techniques: Burrows-style function-word frequency vectors, PCA (about 50 components), mutual nearest neighbour by Euclidean distance
Heuristics for merging From variants into one persona
new_for_atlas: Weak signal only, because NFOs are short: stylometric links from NFO/description text to known release groups. The From-variant merging heuristics carry over directly to poster normalisation.

title: Is Content Publishing in BitTorrent Altruistic or Profit-Driven? (Cuevas et al., ACM CoNEXT 2010)
summary: Identified who publishes file-sharing content by correlating portal usernames with the IP of the initial seeder, and separated fake publishers (anti-piracy or malware) from real ones. The top 3% of publishers produced about 40% of content; fake publishers produced about 30% of content and 25% of downloads.
metadata_fields: promo URLs in filenames, description text box and bundled text files
techniques: Poll the tracker early to catch the initial seeder; confirm with piece bitfields when there is 1 seeder and fewer than 20 peers
Many-to-many username-to-IP mapping: 45% of top IPs map to many usernames
Fake-publisher signals: many usernames per IP, concentration at hosting providers (tzulo, FDC, 4RWEB), long seeding of unpopular content
new_for_atlas: Usenet analogue: map From names to posting-host/Injection-Info/X-Trace. A host that rotates many random From names is probably one uploader; per-host fake or password rates flag polluters.

title: Pollution in P2P File Sharing Systems (Liang, Kumar, Xi, Ross, Polytechnic Univ.; IEEE INFOCOM 2005)
summary: A 1,600-thread KaZaA crawler grouped copies into versions by content hash and labelled polluted versions automatically, with no listening, using decodability and duration. Manual listening showed only 7-8% false negatives.
techniques: Version = identical content hash, so any metadata change creates a new version
Polluted if the file does not decode or its length is outside +/-10% of the official duration
new_for_atlas: Flag fake or broken releases when the parsed MKV/MP4 duration differs from the TMDb/TVDB runtime by more than about 10%, or when the stream fails to decode.

title: Perfect 10, Inc. v. Giganews, Inc. (9th Cir. 2017, No. 15-55500)
summary: The court's findings on how a major backbone handles articles: the Message-ID is the only reliable identifier, peers compare Message-IDs to avoid duplicates, articles already deleted are not copied again from peers, and removal works from machine-readable Message-ID lists. 565 Message-IDs that were not machine-readable took over 20 hours to process.
metadata_fields: binary content encoded in article bodies
techniques: Takedown per Message-ID (search-term notices were rejected as unreliable)
Dedup of peer feeds by Message-ID; deleted IDs blocked from re-propagation
Automatic blocking based on IWF lists
new_for_atlas: Takedowns are per Message-ID and per backbone, so periodically STAT a sample of each release's segments on each provider. Record takedown/completion state and prefer twins or alts whose segments are intact.

title: Twentieth Century Fox v Newzbin Ltd [2010] EWHC 608 (Ch) (Kitchin J)
summary: A court-documented description of a large indexer: crawled headers only, built an automatic RAW per-file index and a 'Condensed' index that grouped every file of one copy of a work, and had human editors write 'reports' with structured metadata.
metadata_fields: poster address, posting date/time, newsgroups, subject, message identifier, server path (para 23)
report fields: title, overall size, source, video format, region, genre, audio format, language, subtitles, IMDb/Amazon URL, NFO (paras 27, 33, 36)
techniques: Messages over 100 KB assumed binary and only their headers fetched (para 53)
Message ID table, then News table (RAW index of files), then Condensed table (automatic per-work grouping), then editor reports (paras 23-27, 55)
Title format 'Title (YEAR) (Additional Info)', dates YYYY-MM-DD (para 38)
Text under 20 KB grouped into daily digests (paras 48, 56)
new_for_atlas: Nothing new technically. It validates a RAW, then grouped, then curated layering, and gives a cheap XOVER :bytes > 100 KB binary prefilter.

title: US Patent Application 2006/0015555 'Storage cluster server network' (Douglass, Henigin, Molter, Swarin, Yokubaitis)
summary: A backbone article store in which each article's primary server is chosen as hash(Message-ID) mod N. Placement is therefore deterministic and the same article is never stored twice, with per-newsgroup age expiry and extra redundancy for fresh articles.
metadata_fields: per-server metadata memory index and expiration log
techniques: Primary server = hash(Message-ID) mod server count, which dedupes by Message-ID
Redundancy 5 for articles under 3 days old
Per-group retention rules instead of a single global age
new_for_atlas: Nothing new for indexing. It confirms that backbones dedupe only by Message-ID, so byte-identical reposts with new Message-IDs are stored and expire independently. That is why tracking twins matters for completion.

title: RAR 5.0 archive format (rarlab technote)
summary: The authoritative RAR5 header layout. Beyond names and sizes it holds several deobfuscation and fingerprint fields: a Metadata record with the original archive name and creation time, per-file BLAKE2sp hashes, a Unix owner record, high-precision timestamps, and the quick-open/recovery locators.
metadata_fields: main flags 0x0001 volume, 0x0002 volume number present, 0x0004 solid, 0x0008 recovery record, 0x0010 locked; volume number vint
Locator record 0x01: quick-open offset, recovery-record offset
Metadata record 0x02: original archive name, original creation time (Unix/FILETIME, nanoseconds)
file flags: 0x0001 directory, 0x0002 mtime, 0x0004 CRC32, 0x0008 unknown size; unpacked size; attributes; mtime; data CRC32
compression info: version 0x003f, solid 0x0040, method 0x0380, dictionary 0x7c00 (128 KB x 2^N)
extra 0x01 encryption (version, flags, KDF count, salt, IV, check value)
extra 0x03 file time mtime/ctime/atime, Unix vs FILETIME, nanoseconds
extra 0x06 Unix owner (user and group names, uid, gid)
service headers CMT, QO, ACL, STM, RR; end-of-archive flag 0x0001 = not last volume; archive encryption header
techniques: Order randomly named volumes by the volume-number field and the end-of-archive 'not last volume' flag
The original archive name in the Metadata record can survive renaming
The BLAKE2sp per-file hash identifies the inner file across different wrappings
Fingerprint the tool or uploader from Unix owner names, host OS, timestamp precision, dictionary size, method and solid flag
An archive encryption header means names are hidden
new_for_atlas: Parse past names and sizes: the Metadata record (original name and time), BLAKE2sp hash, Unix owner, file-time extras, compression-info bits, volume number, CMT comment, QO/RR locators, and the KDF count of encrypted sets.

title: RAR (Forensics Wiki)
summary: A forensic reference for RAR 1.5-3.x (RAR4) blocks and flags, covering carving signatures, host OS, version and method fields that fingerprint the creating tool.
metadata_fields: archive flags 0x0001 volume, 0x0002 comment, 0x0004 lock, 0x0008 solid, 0x0010 new volume naming, 0x0020 authenticity, 0x0040 recovery record, 0x0080 encrypted headers, 0x0100 first volume
file flags 0x01/0x02 split, 0x04 encrypted, 0x10 solid, 0x100 64-bit sizes, 0x200 Unicode name, 0x400 salt, 0x1000 extended time
HOST_OS 0-5, FTIME (DOS), UNP_VER (10*major+minor), METHOD 0x30-0x35, dictionary bits 7-5
techniques: Carve by marker and terminator blocks
The first-volume flag 0x0100 finds the start of a set regardless of filename
UNP_VER, METHOD, dictionary and HOST_OS form a tool and version fingerprint
new_for_atlas: Use each RAR4 file block's FILE_CRC (inner-file CRC32) plus unpacked size for alt matching and srrDB archive-crc lookups. Use the 0x0100/0x0010 flags to order obfuscated volumes.

title: 7z format description (7zFormat.txt, LZMA SDK)
summary: The 7z signature header and property-ID grammar. It defines where per-file CRCs, timestamps, attributes and the optional encoded (compressed or encrypted) header live.
metadata_fields: signature 37 7A BC AF 27 1C; ArchiveVersion major/minor; StartHeaderCRC; NextHeaderOffset/Size/CRC
kHeader 0x01, kMainStreamsInfo 0x04, kFilesInfo 0x05, kPackInfo 0x06, kUnPackInfo 0x07, kSubStreamsInfo 0x08, kSize 0x09, kCRC 0x0A, kFolder 0x0B
kCTime 0x12, kATime 0x13, kMTime 0x14, kWinAttributes 0x15, kComment 0x16, kEncodedHeader 0x17, kStartPos 0x18, kDummy 0x19
techniques: kEncodedHeader with an AES coder means file names are encrypted
Per-file CRC digests in SubStreamsInfo
Folder/coder layout shows solid blocks and methods
Which timestamps are present, plus kDummy padding, varies by writer
new_for_atlas: Extract per-inner-file CRC32 from SubStreamsInfo for alt detection. Classify 'names hidden' (encrypted header) separately from 'data-only encryption'. Use the timestamp and attribute presence pattern as a tool fingerprint.

title: Parity Volume Set Specification 2.0 (Parchive)
summary: Full PAR2 packet set. Besides Main/FileDesc it defines per-slice checksums, comments and a mandatory Creator packet. The spec says identical parameters give byte-identical packets except the client-identifying ones.
metadata_fields: packet header: magic 'PAR2\0PKT', length, packet MD5, Recovery Set ID, type
Main: slice size, file counts, sorted File IDs
FileDesc: File ID, MD5, MD5-16k, length, name
Creator: ASCII client ID (should include URL or email)
UniFileN, CommASCI, CommUni, FileSlic, RFSC, PkdMain, PkdRecvS
techniques: Recovery Set ID = MD5(Main body), so two sets with the same parameters are twins
File ID = MD5(MD5-16k, length, name): renaming changes the File ID but not the MD5
IFSC per-slice CRC32 and MD5 let single decoded segments and partially overlapping uploads be verified
The Creator string fingerprints the toolchain (par2cmdline, ParPar, MultiPar)
new_for_atlas: Atlas reads Main/FileDesc/UniFileN only. Add parsing of the Creator packet, comment packets and IFSC slice checksums, and key twins on MD5 rather than File ID.

title: pyReScene: scene release reconstruction (SRR/SRS) (srrDB/pyrescene)
summary: SRR files keep the metadata of a scene RAR set (all RAR headers, no data) plus the NFO/SFV, so the exact volumes can be rebuilt from extracted files. SRS files store a sample's container structure without its track data, and for MP3/FLAC they keep tags and a Chromaprint fingerprint.
metadata_fields: SRR: RAR volume headers, stored NFO/SFV, creating application
SRS: AVI/MKV/MP4/WMV sample structure minus track data, plus a signature to locate the track data; MP3/FLAC tags; fpcalc fingerprint
techniques: Rebuild byte-identical RAR volumes from the SRR and the extracted files (store mode, some compressed modes)
Check samples against the main file
new_for_atlas: Confirm a posted RAR set is the untouched scene original by comparing volume names, sizes and CRCs with the srrDB SRR. Such a release is a reconstructable twin even when its names are obfuscated.

title: SrrInfo.php: SRR parser in the newznab lineage (DariusIII/rarinfo fork of zeebinz)
summary: PHP SRR reader that exposes the creating app, stored files, RAR volume list and an OSO-hash block. The OSO block shows that srrDB SRRs carry the OpenSubtitles hash of the main video.
metadata_fields: 0x71 RAR file (volume name), followed by that volume's RAR headers
techniques: Parse SRRs locally to get the scene release's volume names, inner file list and OSO hash, then match them against posted files
new_for_atlas: Atlas already computes the OpenSubtitles moviehash. Matching it against the OSO hashes in SRRs (or srrDB isdbhash:) can name an obfuscated bare video or RAR set.

title: srrDB help: search keywords (also usable in API v1 at https://api.srrdb.com/v1/docs)
summary: The scene-release database supports exact searches by inner-file CRC32 and size, by OpenSubtitles/ISDb hash, by RAR-set hash, and by sample CRC or filename. Each is a direct deobfuscation lookup.
metadata_fields: rarhash: (hash of the release's RAR set)
techniques: API: https://api.srrdb.com/v1/search/archive-crc:0053CA13 (slash-separated keyword:value pairs); /v1/details/{release}; /v1/nfo/{release}; /v1/imdb/{release}
API docs say 'Use but don't scrape'
new_for_atlas: New lookup ladder: RAR/7z inner-file CRC32 + size (archive-crc, archive-size), the OpenSubtitles hash (isdbhash), sample CRC or name (store-real-crc, store-real-filename), and RAR set (rarhash) to recover scene names for obfuscated posts.

title: Investigate: yEnc whole-file CRC32 to srrdb for nameless bare video posts (KurzonDax/newznab-tmux-kd issue #476)
summary: A field test of using the =yend whole-file crc32 of bare (un-RARed) video posts as an srrDB archive-crc key. In a 500-release rerun (releases over 1 GiB) there were 0 usable whole-file CRCs: 472 final segments carried only pcrc32 and 28 NZBs lacked the final part. In a 200-release mixed sample, all 53 usable CRC+size searches returned 0 hits; the issue was closed wontfix.
techniques: Fetch the last segment per post to read the whole-file crc32 (about 1 extra segment per release; 503 bodies, 193 MiB in about 145 s)
Exact CRC+size srrDB search
Positive-control check that exposed a separate srrDB response-field bug (#481)
new_for_atlas: Empirical warning: posters rarely emit the yEnc whole-file crc32, and non-scene content does not hit srrDB. Use RAR/7z inner CRCs, PAR2 MD5 or the OSO hash instead. A posted RAR volume's CRC is never the inner file's CRC, even in store mode.

title: OpenSubtitles Hash (OSHash): reference and limitations (opensubtitles/oshash)
summary: Definitive OSHash algorithm and its stated limits: a non-cryptographic sum over the first and last 64 KB plus the file size. Collisions and preimages are trivial, and everything between head and tail is ignored.
metadata_fields: first 64 KB and last 64 KB read as 8,192 little-endian uint64 each
techniques: hash = size + sum(first 64 KB) + sum(last 64 KB), mod 2^64; minimum file size 128 KB
Test vectors: breakdance.avi gives 8e245d9679d31e12; a >4 GB case gives 61f7751fc2a72bfb
new_for_atlas: Use it only as a candidate key and confirm with size and duration. Inference: any remux or retag that changes the first or last 64 KB changes the hash for identical content.

title: OpenSubtitles: don't rely on hash that much (Diaoul/subliminal issue #538)
summary: Maintainers report many wrong or duplicate hashes in the OpenSubtitles DB, '0' placeholder hashes, mis-tagged files carrying another video's hash, and uploader-typed release names returned in place of real filenames.
techniques: A fail-safe on hash matches
Query with title plus hash
Score tag matches by the subtitle's stored name
new_for_atlas: Treat OSDb hash hits as weak evidence that needs corroboration by name, size or duration before renaming a release.

title: PDQ & TMK+PDQF: A Test Drive of Facebook's Perceptual Hashing Algorithms (Dalins, Wilson, Boudry, AFP/Monash, arXiv 1912.07745, 2019)
summary: An empirical robustness test of PDQ image hashing and TMK+PDQF video hashing. It gives concrete thresholds and failure modes for 'same video, different encode' matching.
metadata_fields: TMK+PDQF 258 KB hash (level-1 1 KB average, level-2 256 KB)
techniques: PDQ match at Hamming distance <= 30 (random pairs about 128)
TMK: level-1 cosine >= 0.7 and level-2 score >= 0.7 are both required
Robust to bitrate, format and half-scaling
Weak on more than 10-20% crop, watermarks, added title screens and short trims (improves toward 300 s)
TMK hashing takes about 1/40 of runtime
new_for_atlas: Calibrated frame-level thresholds and known blind spots for Atlas's 'same film' matching.

title: vPDQ video hashing (Python bindings, ThreatExchange)
summary: Per-frame PDQ video hashing with order-insensitive frame-set matching. It returns query-side and target-side match percentages instead of one boolean.
techniques: Sample frames at some interval (e.g. 1 fps); optional pruning of consecutive near-identical frames (Dprune = 2)
Drop frames with quality < 50; frame match at distance <= 31
q_pct and c_pct = matched/filtered frames; match if c_pct >= 80% and q_pct >= 0% (frame order ignored)
new_for_atlas: Two-sided match percentages separate the same cut or encode (both about 100%) from partial overlaps such as extended cuts, recaps or samples.

title: [FFmpeg-devel] [PATCHv2] add signature filter for MPEG-7 video signature
summary: Stock FFmpeg 'signature' filter that computes MPEG-7 video signatures and can detect matching sequences between inputs, with tunable word, frame and sequence thresholds.
metadata_fields: MPEG-7 video signature (binary or XML output)
techniques: th_d = 9000 (one word similar)
th_dc = 60000 (all words similar)
th_xh = 116 (frames similar)
th_di = 0 (minimum matching sequence length, frames)
th_it = 0.5 (minimum fraction of matching frames)
Detection mode on/off or stop at first match; multiple inputs (nb_inputs)
new_for_atlas: Temporal alignment of matching intervals between two encodes with no extra dependency. It can tell different cuts apart and report offsets, which a whole-file 'same film' verdict cannot.

title: A Highly Robust Audio Fingerprinting System (Haitsma & Kalker, Philips, ISMIR 2002)
summary: The classic 32-bit sub-fingerprint audio scheme with a precise bit-error-rate match threshold and robustness table. Notably, linear speed changes beyond about 2.5% break matching.
metadata_fields: fingerprint block of 256 sub-fingerprints (about 3 s, 8,192 bits)
techniques: 0.37 s Hanning frames with 31/32 overlap; 33 log-spaced bands 300-2000 Hz; bits are signs of band-energy differences across time and frequency
Match if BER < 0.35 (false-positive rate about 3.6e-20)
Robust to MP3 and to +/-4% time-scaling; linear speed +/-4% gives BER 0.355-0.472
Lookup table on sub-fingerprints plus flipping the least reliable bits
new_for_atlas: PAL speed-up (25 vs 23.976 fps, about 4%) defeats audio-fingerprint matching. Speed-normalise or resample before comparing audio of PAL and film-rate releases.

title: Video identification with AcoustID (acoustid Google Group, Jan 2021)
summary: The AcoustID author confirms Chromaprint can identify movie audio and proposes a matching protocol. The public service cannot do it because it keeps only the first two minutes and queries around 0:15 and 0:30.
metadata_fields: Chromaprint fingerprint of the full movie audio track
techniques: Index the full track; query three 30 s samples at random positions, avoiding the first and last 10 minutes (intros and studio logos collide)
Accept only if all three samples agree
Map each language track to the same video
new_for_atlas: A concrete audio sampling and agreement protocol that avoids intro and logo collisions when deciding 'same film'.

title: A Low-bandwidth Network File System (Muthitacharoen, Chen, Mazieres, SOSP 2001)
summary: Content-defined chunking: Rabin fingerprints over a sliding window choose chunk boundaries from content, so shared byte runs are found even when offsets and framing differ.
metadata_fields: SHA-1 chunk IDs (index keyed by a 64-bit prefix)
techniques: Breakpoint when the low 13 bits of the fingerprint equal a magic value: about 8 KB average chunks, 2 KB minimum, 64 KB maximum
Results: 76% overlap between emacs 20.6 and 20.7 sources; 90% after adding one page to a PostScript file
new_for_atlas: A way to detect alts: chunk and hash decoded yEnc payloads with content-defined chunking. When the same inner file is wrapped differently, especially in store-mode RAR (-m0) or 7z -mx0, it shares chunks despite different volume sizes, segment boundaries and archive headers.

title: MagnetDB: A Longitudinal Torrent Discovery Dataset with IMDb-Matched Movies and TV Shows (Seidenberger, Pursell, Maiti, 2025)
summary: Matched about 86.6M torrent video file names to IMDb at scale using scene-convention parsing plus BM25 retrieval with a statistical acceptance threshold. Only 1.81% of video files (about 1.56M) matched confidently.
metadata_fields: file names parsed with PTN: resolution, codec, audio, hdr, fps, bitDepth, encoder, site, network, repack, region, language, directorsCut, unrated
techniques: Elasticsearch analyser: edge n-grams 4-15, lowercasing, ASCII folding
BM25 top hit accepted if its score is at least 2 standard deviations (138)
new_for_atlas: A published baseline for matching names to IMDb with a statistical cut-off. Its low recall shows why name matching needs hash or metadata keys for obfuscated content.

title: ngPost README: Usenet poster with built-in obfuscation (mbruel/ngPost)
summary: Documents exactly what a popular uploader randomises (subjects, Message-IDs, From, archive names, passwords) and what it leaves constant. The constants are fingerprints that can tie obfuscated segments to one tool and session.
metadata_fields: random From by default; --gen_from draws a new random poster per post
Subject = UUID (the same as the Message-ID) under full obfuscation
--gen_name random archive name, 17 chars; --gen_pass random password, 13 chars
techniques: Tool fingerprint from the Message-ID right-hand side, subject equal to the Message-ID left-hand side, and the fixed 716800-byte part size
Without the NZB, obfuscated posts cannot be found by indexers
new_for_atlas: Rules for uploads by this tool: Message-ID domain, UUID subjects, 716800-byte parts and 17-char names. Combine with posting time and posting host to group obfuscated segments into posts.

title: Spot Header format (Spotnet wiki)
summary: Spotnet 'spots' are Usenet articles whose headers carry signed release metadata and NZB pointers, plus a stable uploader identity in the form of an RSA public key.
metadata_fields: X-XML: Key, Created, Poster, Tag, Title, Description, Website, Image, Size, Category/Sub (e.g. 04a03), NZB Segment message-id
techniques: The signed poster key gives a stable uploader identity across random nicknames
The NZB segment Message-ID in X-XML points to the release's NZB
new_for_atlas: Harvest spots as a signed metadata source that maps NZB segment Message-IDs to titles and categories, with stable poster keys, for Dutch/European uploads.

title: How does Chromaprint work? (Lukas Lalinsky, 2011)
summary: The author's description of the Chromaprint audio fingerprint pipeline used by AcoustID and by pyReScene for music SRS.
metadata_fields: sequence of 32-bit fingerprint items derived from a 12-bin chroma image
techniques: Resample to 11025 Hz; 4096-sample frames with 2/3 overlap; FFT, then 12 chroma bins
16 learned filters over a 16x12 sliding window, quantised to 0-3 and Gray-coded into 2 bits each, giving a 32-bit item
Compare fingerprints by XOR bit-error rate
new_for_atlas: Parameters for audio-track fingerprints. Pair them with the AcoustID sampling protocol, and speed-normalise PAL audio first.

title: SABnzbd deobfuscate_filenames.py: is_probably_obfuscated() rules, par2 16 KiB-MD5 rename, biggest-file rename
summary: SABnzbd first renames files from any par2 in the job by matching the MD5 of each file's first 16384 bytes to FileDesc hash16k (the 'rename.par2' convention). Next, if the biggest file is more than 3x the next one and its basename looks obfuscated, SABnzbd renames it to the job name, along with every file that shares its stem (-sample, .dut.srt). Files with uncommon extensions get an extension appended, chosen by sniffing their contents.
metadata_fields: MD5 of first 16384 bytes of each file
file sizes / size ratio biggest vs 2nd
techniques: Certainly obfuscated: ^[a-f0-9]{32}$ ; ^[a-f0-9.]{40,}$ ; any [a-f0-9]{30} together with >=2 \[\w+\] tags ; basename starting 'abc.xyz'

Certainly clear (in order): >=2 upper and >=2 lower and >=1 of space/dot/underscore; >=3 space/dot/underscore; >=4 letters and >=4 digits and >=1 separator ('Beast 2020'); starts with a capital and upper/lower <= 0.25 ('Catullus'); otherwise default = obfuscated
Rename only when biggest file > 3x second biggest; never rename .vob .rar .par2 .mts .m2ts .cpi .clpi .mpl .mpls .bdm .bdmv or jobs containing DVD/Blu-ray folder structures
Propagate the new stem to every file whose path starts with the obfuscated stem; rename orphan .srt files by prefixing the main file's stem
new_for_atlas: Atlas has newznab-tmux regexes but no per-filename obfuscation classifier. These thresholds, and the 3x biggest-file rule for picking the 'main' inner file, port directly.

title: SABnzbd issue #1682 (+#1768): [PRiVATE]-[GROUP]-[name]-[n/N] - "" subjects vs abc.xyz.<hex> yEnc names
summary: Users showed NZBs whose subject holds the real name in brackets and leaves the quoted filename empty, e.g. `[PRiVATE]-[GROUPNAME]-[INSTALLER.ISO]-[3/82] - "" yEnc 100000 (1/1)`, while the yEnc name= is `abc.xyz.32dee2f83eae13.mkv`. The fix prefers the yEnc name only if it differs, is not .par2 and passes is_probably_obfuscated(). Issue #1768 (also opened) shows names that themselves contain brackets (`[Video_(2001)_AC5.1_-RELEASE_[TAoE].mkv]`) breaking simple regexes.
techniques: Keep the subject-derived name and the yEnc name as separate candidates and arbitrate with an obfuscation score instead of always trusting yEnc
Treat abc.xyz.<14 hex>.<ext> yEnc names as one obfuscation family
[PRiVATE] layout: 2nd bracket = group tag, 3rd = real file name/path, 4th = file index/total; the quoted name is intentionally empty
Parse brackets by depth (names can contain [..]); if the extracted name is empty, fall back to the whole subject
new_for_atlas: Check that Atlas's ported collection regexes cover this layout and nested brackets. Arbitrating between the yEnc name and the subject name is new.

title: SABnzbd issue #1795: per-file hex.hex.hex names in season packs with no par2
summary: Season packs arrived as files named like `0675e29e9abfd2.f7d069dab0b853283cc1b069a25f81.6545` with no PAR2. The developers said job-name renaming 'will never work for season-packs'. The reporter identified one file as S02E01 only by grepping its subtitle text, and the case led to SABnzbd's ^[a-f0-9.]{40,}$ rule.
techniques: Pattern ^[0-9a-f]{14}\.[0-9a-f]{30}\.[0-9a-f]{4}$ marks this uploader family
Missing par2 plus per-episode random names is deliberate; identify episodes by content (subtitle lines, runtime vs TV metadata, chapter titles) rather than by name
new_for_atlas: Atlas's list has no content-based identification of individual files inside multi-file obfuscated packs.

title: SABnzbd assembler.py: spotting cloaked/encrypted fakes from the first RAR volume
summary: As soon as a RAR volume is written, SABnzbd opens it (part_only) and checks for header encryption, 'cloaked' content and unwanted extensions, trying the NZB and user passwords. It pauses or aborts the job before the rest downloads.
techniques: is_cloaked: an inner .rar whose stem prefixes the outer file name with < 8 extra chars, fewer than 3 inner files, not matching \W+sub|subs|subpack|subtitle(s)
Inner name containing 'password' with extension not in .mkv/.mp4/.avi/.wmv/.mpg/.webm => encrypted bait
Password test on a single volume: RarWrongPassword = wrong; RarCRCError mentioning 'cannot find volume' or 'unexpected end of archive' = password accepted
User unwanted-extension list (exe, lnk, ...) matched against inner names => pause/abort
new_for_atlas: Atlas lists inner names but has no fake/bait rules. This adds them, plus a password test from a single volume.

title: SABnzbd misc.py: subject filename extraction and NZB-name password conventions
summary: subject_name_extractor() takes the first non-empty quoted string, else a 'basic filename' regex, else the whole subject. Job names are split into name and password using 'name / pw', 'name password=pw', 'name{{pw}}' or 'name/pw'. nzbparser.py collects every NZB <meta type=...> value, since types may repeat.
techniques: RE_SUBJECT_FILENAME_QUOTES = "([^"]*)"
Password parse order: 'name / pw' (if '/' precedes any '{{' and no 'password='), then 'password=', then '{{pw}}', then 'name/pw'
new_for_atlas: If Atlas ingests uploader NZBs or NZBLNKs, these conventions and multi-valued meta carry passwords. The basic-filename regex is a fallback when the quotes are empty.

title: NZBGet Deobfuscation.cpp (v24.6+): token-level hash-blob classifier and subject parser
summary: NZBGet takes the filename from the quoted text in the subject. If the quotes are empty it uses a [PRiVATE]-[..]-[name] parser, otherwise the word before ' yEnc' or the 'Re: ... (' form. It flags names as 'excessively obfuscated' using whole-stem regexes plus per-token entropy rules, and per the ChangeLog renames such post-unpack files to the NZB name (RenameAfterUnpack, RenameIgnoreExt).
metadata_fields: extension (numeric extensions resolved to real one)
techniques: Tokens split on [._- \[\]()]: hash if mixed-case alnum >=10, single-case alnum >=12, lower+UPPER start >=8 with >=2 caps, >=6 letter/digit alternations, >=16 digits, >=3 case transitions in >=8 letters, vowelless >=8, or >=24 letters with <20% vowels

Whitelist: CamelCase titles (years, roman numerals, 720p/1080p prefixes), all-caps words <=15 chars with >=20% vowels (INTERSTELLAR), part\d+.rar / vol\d+\+\d+.par2, single archives with 16-256 alnum stems
Adjacent mixed-case tokens are concatenated and re-tested when the stem is <=32 chars
new_for_atlas: This is the most complete open-source hash-vs-title heuristic found. Port it to score subjects, yEnc names and inner names.

title: NZBGet DirectRenamer: par2 detection and 16 KiB MD5 from each file's first article
summary: NZBGet downloads the first article of every file. If the decoded bytes start with the PAR2 packet magic, the file is treated as par2 whatever its name, and its Recovery Set ID is read from that header; otherwise NZBGet computes the MD5 of the first 16 KiB. It then fetches the smallest par2 per set, loads FileDesc packets and renames every file before the rest downloads.
metadata_fields: PAR2 packet header magic 'PAR2\0PKT' + recovery set id
techniques: hash16k is only valid if the first article is >= 16 KiB or the file has a single article
Download only the smallest par2 of each set id, then match hash16k -> FileDesc name; par2 files are renamed too
ChangeLog: downloads with no obviously named par2 assume 85% critical health (par2 may be hidden under random names)
new_for_atlas: This yields a file identity from a single segment: yEnc size= plus MD5 of the first 16 KiB. That identity can be compared with FileDesc hash16k from other releases' par2, linking obfuscated reposts and alts even when the post has no par2. It also groups random-named par2 volumes by set id.

title: NZBGet RarRenamer/RarReader: rebuilding obfuscated RAR volume sets from header flags
summary: Without par2, NZBGet reads RAR3/RAR5 headers of every file and chains volumes. It starts from volume 0 whose first file isn't split-before, then appends a volume with number+1, the same RAR version, the previous volume's next-volume flag set, and a first entry continuing the same inner filename. A set is complete when the last volume lacks next-volume (RarRenamer.cpp, also opened, renames to .partNNNN.rar or .rar/.r00 and decrypts RAR3 header encryption with the password).
metadata_fields: RAR3 MAIN flags 0x0001 VOLUME, 0x0010 NEWNUMBERING, 0x0080 PASSWORD (header encryption)
RAR3 ENDARC flags 0x0001 NEXTVOL, 0x0002 DATACRC, 0x0008 VOLNUMBER (+u32 volume number)
RAR5 block flags 0x08 SPLITBEFORE, 0x10 SPLITAFTER; ENDARC 0x01 NEXTVOL; block type 4 = encryption header
techniques: Chain rule as above; when several candidates fit, prefer the one whose archive name has the same length/stem
Set complete = last volume has no NEXTVOL and its last file is not split-after
new_for_atlas: Atlas lists inner names and sizes but does not chain volumes. Volume number plus split flags plus the spanning inner name can assemble and order RAR sets that arrive under random names, even across separate posts.

title: Nyuu defaults: Message-ID with a millisecond clock, User-Agent, From user@hostname
summary: Nyuu's createMessageId emits 24 letters alternating A-Z/a-z, '-', a 13-digit millisecond Unix timestamp of encode time, then '@nyuu'. config.js sets User-Agent 'Nyuu/<version>' and a default From of '<local user> <user@hostname>'. help-full.txt documents 700K articles, 128-byte lines and subject `{comment} [{0filenum}/{files}] - "{filename}" yEnc ({part}/{parts}) {filesize} {comment2}`.
techniques: Regex ^(?:[A-Z][a-z]){12}-\d{13}@ identifies Nyuu IDs even with a custom domain (Leo's notes shows <IgLnZpOzUcUfNzGyQaCiZfVw-1530199484291@PRiVATE>)
Parse the 13-digit timestamp to get the real encode time even if Date was overridden (--date); use it to order articles and cluster one upload job
Default From leaks the OS username and hostname, giving a stable uploader key
new_for_atlas: Atlas keeps message-ids but does not classify posting tools or mine timestamps from the IDs.

title: Nyuu issue #146: the Message-ID clock 'survives everything else', and STAT 223 with truncated bodies
summary: A contributor argued that `-<unix ms>@nyuu` and `User-Agent: Nyuu/<ver>` name the tool and that the clock is 'a per-article timestamp that survives everything else a user does to obfuscate a post'. animetosho replied that Date is mandatory and servers record arrival time anyway. The same thread reports providers answering STAT with 223 while BODY comes back short with no =yend trailer; it settled on hash-checking the fetched encoded body.
techniques: Use the ID timestamp vs Date vs NNTP-Posting-Date deltas as a timing fingerprint
Don't treat STAT/HEAD success as completeness: a body with no =yend, or with =yend size != decoded length, is truncated
Hash the encoded article (CRC32) to verify without decoding
new_for_atlas: Add truncated-article detection to completion scoring: availability is not the same as integrity.

title: Nyuu-Obfuscation fork: per-article random yEnc names, random Date within 6 h, random From/Subject/Message-ID
summary: With --obfuscate-articles, each article's yEnc name becomes crypto.randomBytes(n).toString('hex'), where n is 16-32 and fixed per file. Each article's Date is set to a random time in the last 6 hours, and User-Agent is removed. The README/bin preset `obfuscation: true` uses -f "{rand(14)} <{rand(14)}@{rand(5)}.{rand(3)}>" --message-id "{rand(32)}@{rand(8)}.{rand(3)}" --subject "{rand(32)}", with rand charset [A-Za-z0-9].
metadata_fields: yEnc name (32-64 lowercase hex, even length)
techniques: Regroup articles into files by identical (yEnc size=, total=, line=) and identical yEnc-name length, then order and verify by =ypart begin/end contiguity (inference from the code)
Date is useless (random -6 h); order by NNTP-Posting-Date/Injection-Date or article number
new_for_atlas: newznab-tmux collection regexes cannot group posts whose subject, From and yEnc name change on every article.

title: ngPost: UUID IDs and subjects, random From @ngPost.com, no Date/User-Agent, nonstandard =yend
summary: ngPost sends only From, Newsgroups, Subject and Message-ID. The Message-ID is `<32-hex QUuid Id128@ngPost>`, and with -x the Subject equals that same 32-hex UUID; random From is 13 random chars + '@' + signature + '.com' (NgPost.h). Unobfuscated subjects are `[NN/M] "file" (p/P)` with no 'yEnc' token, and yEnc is `=ybegin part= total= line=128 size= name=` / `=yend size=<part> pcrc32=<hex, no zero padding>` with no part= or crc32=.
techniques: Obfuscated ngPost: Subject == Message-ID local part, ^[0-9a-f]{32}$
From ^[A-Za-z0-9]{13}@ngPost\.com$ (signature configurable via --msg_id)
Absence of Date/User-Agent before injection = minimalist poster
Subjects lacking the literal 'yEnc' are missed by regexes that require it
Parsers must accept =yend without part= and left-pad short pcrc32
Defaults: 716800-byte articles, 17-char random RAR names, 13-char passwords
new_for_atlas: New poster fingerprint plus yEnc tolerance. Zero-pad pcrc32 and don't require part= in =yend.

title: Nyuu wiki 'Usenet Uploaders': roster of posting tools to fingerprint
summary: A community-edited table of about 20 binary posters with their NZB, par2, post-checking and multi-connection features. It lists EasyUSENET Uploader, GoPostStuff, JBinUp, NewsBin, Newsmangler, Newspost, NewsUP, ngPost, NxG Upper, nntpPoster, Nyuu, Postie, Sanguinews, yEncBin Poster, Yencee and Ypost, plus PowerPost variants (CamelSystem, PowerPost 2000, YEnc-Power-Post-A&A, PowerPost-GB12).
techniques: Seed a per-tool signature table (Message-ID template, From template, header set, yEnc line length and field order, article size, par2 Creator string) from this roster
PowerPost-family subjects are the classic `comment [n/N] - "file" yEnc (p/P)` form
new_for_atlas: A catalogue to build a fingerprint table from; no new technique by itself.

title: NxG Upper/Loader: Message-IDs derived from a 28-byte 'NxG header' (no NZB needed)
summary: The NxG header is base64 of a 21-char random string whose tail is overwritten with ':<data articles>:<par2 articles>' (Vpjnfhd01U288Q:415:49 -> VnBqbmZoZDAxVTI4OFE6NDE1OjQ5). Each Message-ID is SHA256('<header>:data|par2:<n>') split as [0:40]@[40:61].[61:64], and the random string doubles as the rar/par2 filename. NxG Loader (README also opened) reads an X-Nxg article header so yEnc names can be obfuscated; links look like nxglnk://?h=&p=&t=.
techniques: Given a published NxG header (forums, links), compute every data/par2 message-id directly
The header itself encodes total data and par2 article counts, which gives a completeness check
new_for_atlas: A new deterministic-ID scheme. Atlas could detect it and, where headers are public, enumerate a release without an NZB.

title: javi11/nxg (used by Postie): X-Nxg payload, hash-derived obfuscated Subject and poster
summary: X-Nxg = encrypt('fileNumber:totalFiles:filename:partType:totalDownloadSize', key = NxG header). The obfuscated Subject is sha256 of the segment hash (64 hex). The obfuscated From is posterHash[10:15] + ' <' + posterHash[10:25] + '@' + posterHash[30:45] + '.' + posterHash[50:53] + '>'.
techniques: From fingerprint: the 5-hex display name equals the first 5 chars of the local part, ^([0-9a-f]{5}) <\1[0-9a-f]{10}@[0-9a-f]{15}\.[0-9a-f]{3}>$
Subject ^[0-9a-f]{64}$
An X-Nxg header means an NxG-aware poster; with the key it reveals the real filename, file index/count and total size
new_for_atlas: New header and fingerprints.

title: Postie obfuscation policies: full / partial / none, with a separate par2 policy
summary: 'full' gives a random subject, a yEnc filename randomized per article, a Date randomized within the last 6 hours, a random poster per article and no NXG header. 'partial' keeps one yEnc name and one poster for all articles of a post and uses the real date. par2 files can have their own policy (e.g. none) to stay discoverable; configuration.md (opened) adds message_id_format random|nxg and add_nxg_header.
techniques: Under 'partial', group by the constant From or yEnc name per post
An unobfuscated par2 next to obfuscated data (par2_obfuscation_policy: none) gives real names via FileDesc
Date skew of up to 6 h: order by server-side dates
new_for_atlas: Spells out which fields stay constant at each obfuscation level, i.e. which grouping key still works.

title: NZB Monkey Go: NZBLNK header search, direct XOVER scan and completeness thresholds
summary: An NZBLNK (h=<subject token>, p=<password>, t=<title>, g=<groups>, d=<date>) is resolved via nzbindex, nzbking, binsearch or easynews, or by scanning the server's overview directly. The direct scan covers ±12 h around d with 20 connections and 20,000 articles per XOVER request, building an NZB from matching headers. NZBCheck keeps the most complete result with max_missing_segments_percent=1 and max_missing_files=1 (README and NZBCheck page opened).
techniques: Map date to an article-number window, then chunk XOVER in parallel
Match on the subject token; completeness from (part/parts) counts
first_group_only, because 'the chance of getting different results in different groups is virtually zero'
new_for_atlas: Atlas could harvest NZBLNKs from forums as name + password + group + date hints. The completeness thresholds are a community norm.

title: WtFnZb-Renamer.py gist: the three [PRiVATE]-[WtFnZb] subject layouts
summary: An NZBGet scan script that rewrites WtFnZb subjects into `WtFnZb "<filename>" yEnc (<n>/<N>)`. It first validates that all files share one total and that the total equals the number of <file> elements.
techniques: \[PRiVATE\]-\[WtFnZb\]-\[(?P<total>\d+)\]-\[(?P<segment>\d+)/(?P<filename>.{3,}?)\]\s+-\s+""\s+yEnc\s+
\[PRiVATE\]-\[WtFnZb\]-\[(?P<filename>.{3,}?)\]-\[(?P<segment>\d+)/(?P<total>\d+)\]\s+-\s+""\s+yEnc\s+ (and a [n_N] variant)
Sanity checks: segment <= total, a single distinct total, total == number of files; dedupe repeated names by prefixing the file index
new_for_atlas: Validated regexes for this family, including paths inside the bracket.

title: AIOStreams subject parser hardening: N3wZ-prefixed WtFnZb subjects and fallback chain
summary: Adds SABnzbd's canonical filename regex and then an extension-list fallback for when quoted names fail. Doc examples include `[PRiVATE]-[WtFnZb]-[real.name.r16]-[20/22] - "" yEnc 74688367 (1/105)` and `[N3wZ] \LQ1OaY347934\::[PRiVATE]-[WtFnZb]-[real.name.r16]-[20/22] - ...`.
techniques: QUOTED /"([^"]+)"/ ; COUNTER /[([]\s*\d+\s*\/\s*\d+\s*[)\]]/g ; TRAILING_SIZE /\b\d{4,}\b\s*$/
FILENAME_LIKE fallback with an extension list (mkv|mp4|...|r\d{2}|par2|nzb|srt|...) after stripping counters and sizes
Recognise the '[N3wZ] \<token>\::' prefix (matches the newzNZB header dump in Leo's notes)
new_for_atlas: Add the '[N3wZ] \token\::' prefix variant to the subject regexes.

title: Sonarr Parser.cs: dated catalogue of hashed release names and reversed-title detection
summary: RejectHashedReleasesRegexes lists obfuscated-name patterns with the date each first appeared. ReversedTitleRegex detects release names written backwards and reverses them, minus the extension, before parsing.
techniques: Reversed names: (?:^|[-._ ])(p027|p0801|\d{2,3}E-?\d{2}S)[-._ ] then reverse the string
new_for_atlas: Reversed-name deobfuscation and the dated hash patterns.

title: Sonarr ReleaseGroupParser: indexer/reposter junk suffixes to strip before matching
summary: CleanReleaseGroupRegex removes tags that indexers and re-posters append to scene names. InvalidReleaseGroupRegex rejects 'groups' that are really 8-hex CRCs or SxxEyy.
techniques: Strip (-(RP|1|NZBGeek|\[N-Z-B\]|Obfuscated|Scrambled|sample|Pre|postbot|xpost|Rakuv[a-z0-9]*|WhiteRev|BUYMORE|AsRequested|AlternativeToRequested|GEROV|Z0iDS3N|Chamele0n|4P|4Planet|AlteZachen|RePACKPOST))+$
Invalid group: ^([se]\d+|[0-9a-f]{8})$ ; ParserCommon also strips \[(?:ettv|rartv|rarbg|cttv|publichd)\]$
new_for_atlas: Normalise names with this list before predb/hash matching. nZEDb #2494 shows -postbot/-Obfuscated names failing predb hash matches.

title: nZEDb #2494: hash schemes used for release names (md5/sha1 of predb title, +requestid)
summary: Users reverse-engineered names in a.b.moovee, a.b.etc and bloaf as UNHEX(MD5(CONCAT(title, requestid))) and MD5(title+requestid+requestid), on top of the defaults MD5(title), MD5(MD5(title)) and SHA1(title). The scheme was later reported abandoned. Names carrying '-postbot' (a.b.etc) or '-Obfuscated' (bloaf) still did not match.
techniques: Precompute a predb_hashes table for each scheme; hash column VARBINARY(40); triggers recompute hashes when a title changes
Strip reposter suffixes before hashing
new_for_atlas: Probably already covered by newznab-tmux's predb hash matching; confirm the requestid variants and suffix stripping.

title: nZEDb #2568: PreDB filename matching false positives from generic filenames
summary: matchPredbFiles tied one predb entry to hundreds of releases because IRC-scraped filenames such as Cover, autorun, image, reload, setup and Folder (m2v) are generic. Proposed safeguards: a stopword list, a minimum filename length, and NNTmux's similar_text() >= 93%.
techniques: Stopwords plus minimum length for filename keys
Similarity threshold of 93%
Flag predb ids matched to an abnormal number of releases
new_for_atlas: A pitfall to check. It is probably known already.

title: nZEDb NameFixer uidCheck: naming by MediaInfo Unique_ID (Matroska SegmentUID)
summary: nZEDb stores MediaInfo's Unique_ID per release in release_unique. It renames a release when another release with the same Unique_ID is already named from PreDB, AniDB or the trusted poster 'nonscene@Ef.net (EF)', provided sizes are within ±10%. nZEDb issue #2154 (opened) lists this as one of five fixReleaseNames passes: subject->predb, NFO, file names, par2 and MediaInfo Unique_ID.
techniques: Key on SegmentUID; accept a donor name if |size diff| / size <= 10%
Only accept donors that are predb-, anidb- or trusted-poster-named
new_for_atlas: Atlas parses MKV but doesn't list SegmentUID as a twin/alt key. It is strong evidence for 'same encode, different wrapping'.

title: Leo's Notes 'Usenet': real header dump of a PRiVATE/newzNZB post (X-Received-Body-CRC, X-Ufk, Verify-Signature-Newznzb)
summary: Shows an alt.binaries.newznzb.bravo article with From: nEwZ[NZB] <pr3d@NET.world>, a Nyuu-pattern Message-Id <IgLnZpOzUcUfNzGyQaCiZfVw-1530199484291@PRiVATE>, Organization: Usenet.Farm, Path: not-for-mail, and server headers X-Received-Bytes: 6481 and X-Received-Body-CRC: 2720885501. It also has nonstandard Verify-Signature-Newznzb (a 'newzNZB SIGNATURE' base64 block) and X-Ufk (~200-250 chars, base64 with percent-encoding). It lists nZEDb hash guesses MD5(title), MD5(MD5(title)), SHA1(title), MD5(title.requestid) and MD5(title.requestid.requestid).
techniques: X-Received-Body-CRC is a server-computed body CRC available via HEAD, a cheap exact-duplicate check for re-injected or reposted articles (inference)
The ID timestamp 1530199484291 (15:24:44Z) vs Date 15:25:10 shows the encode->post lag, so the poster tool is Nyuu despite the custom domain
Signed bot posts (Verify-Signature-Newznzb) identify the feed source
new_for_atlas: X-Received-Bytes, X-Received-Body-CRC, X-Ufk and Verify-Signature-Newznzb are not in Atlas's kept-header list.

title: scriptzteam newzNZB Usenet Upload Logger: daily public map of release names to upload tags
summary: Per-day text logs, from 2017 on, list every newz[NZB] upload as `HH:MM -> Release.Name[newzNZB]_[9-hex]` or `Release.Name-newzNZB_[9-hex]`. The 2017-11-17 file alone has 11,487 entries.
techniques: Use as an external name oracle: join the 9-hex tag and/or posting minute against obfuscated posts from the same bot (From nEwZ[NZB]), then strip [newzNZB] / -newzNZB to get the scene name
new_for_atlas: An external naming source Atlas doesn't have. Still to confirm: where the 9-hex tag appears in the posted subject.

title: srrDB search keywords: archive-crc, archive-size, isdbhash (OSO hash), rarhash, store-real-crc
summary: srrDB can be searched by the CRC of a file archived inside the RARs (archive-crc:3D7C3182), archived file size, ISDb/OpenSubtitles hash (isdbhash:db7b7928f550789c), a hash of the release's RAR set (rarhash:<40 hex>), and sample name/CRC (store-real-filename, store-real-crc). It also supports r:, group, imdb and nfo/srs flags. The API docs (https://api.srrdb.com/v1/docs, opened) expose /search/<keywords>, /details/<rls>, /nfo/<rls> and /imdb/<rls> and ask users to 'use but don't scrape'.
techniques: Look up obfuscated posts by the OSO moviehash Atlas already computes (isdbhash:)
Look up by inner-file CRC32 + size from the first RAR volume's file header (archive-crc:/archive-size:)
Look up by sample CRC (store-real-crc:)
new_for_atlas: Atlas computes the OSO hash but doesn't query srrDB. These lookups turn twins and alts into scene names.

title: SRR format (rescene Go parser): what srrDB stores per release
summary: An SRR is a RAR-style block stream: 0x69 SRR header (creating app), 0x6A stored files (NFO, SFV...), 0x6B OSO hash (name, size, 64-bit hash) and 0x6C RAR padding. Then come 0x71 SRR RAR sub-blocks (volume filename), each followed by that volume's raw RAR headers (0x72 mark, 0x73 main, 0x74 file with CRC32/sizes).
techniques: Build an offline match corpus: inner name/size/CRC from the first volume's file header, volume count and sizes, and the OSO hash vs Atlas's computed values
new_for_atlas: New offline matching source.

title: Pre-network IRC bot protocol (prenet TCL): !addpre / !info / !gn / !nuke / !addvideoinfo fields
summary: An eggdrop script for pre channels: `!addpre <rls> <section>`, `!info <rls> <files> <size>`, `!gn <rls> <genre>`, `!nuke|!unnuke|!modnuke <rls> <reason> <nukenet>`, `!addold <rls> <section> <time> <files> <size> <genre> <reason> <nukenet>`. It also handles `!addvideoinfo <rls> <vcodec> <fps> <resolution> <res/frames> <acodec> <bitrate> <hz> <channels>`, `!addmp3info <rls> <genre> <year> <hz> <type> <bitrate> <bittype>`, `!addurl`, `!addimdb` and `!delpre`.
metadata_fields: video/audio codec, fps, resolution, bitrate, hz, channels
techniques: Match obfuscated posts by predb files == RAR volume count and size
Corroborate with MKV/MP4 track facts against !addvideoinfo
Nuke reasons flag dupes and fakes
new_for_atlas: If Atlas's PreDB keeps only name and time, files, size and videoinfo give extra match keys.

title: alt.privacy.anon-server: hashed NNTP-Posting-Host / Injection-Info posting-host
summary: Shows an obfuscated `NNTP-Posting-Host: nefoedcffmbcnkpppqlnajincaaajkkm` and mixmin's filter_nnrpd.pl, which replaces the Injection-Info posting-host with base64(SHA1(host + fixed salt)) and deletes X-Trace. Posters note that a fixed salt keeps the value stable per IP, and that User-Agent/X-Face stay constant across posts.
techniques: Cluster posts by hashed posting-host where the salt is fixed
The 32-char a-p string is 16 bytes in a nibble alphabet, i.e. a 128-bit hash (inference)
Stable client headers link posts
new_for_atlas: Atlas already stores these headers; this explains when they identify an uploader rather than a provider.

title: hashcat forum 'Decrypting usenet headers': posting-host = MD5(IP), posting-account = OpenSSL-encrypted
summary: eternal-september's Injection-Info posting-host is an unsalted MD5 of the IP, crackable with an IPv4 mask. posting-account="U2FsdGVkX19..." is base64 'Salted__' OpenSSL output (one 8-byte block, likely DES/3DES via EVP_BytesToKey) and logging-data is numeric. The individual.net X-Trace ('individual.net q8cNyBZr...') appeared to embed the same IP across one poster's samples.
techniques: Equal posting-host hash = same IP, hence the same uploader
posting-account uses a random salt, so it can't be linked
The X-Trace prefix identifies the injecting server
new_for_atlas: Field-level reading of Injection-Info subfields Atlas already stores.

title: Cleanfeed (INN filter) EMP heuristics: fuzzy body MD5, posting-host/lines, posting-host/groups, from/subject/lines
summary: Cleanfeed rejects excessive multi-posts using decaying rate histories. The keys are: fuzzy body MD5 (cutoff 5, ceiling 85, 7200 s; bodies < 2000 lines, fuzzing < 700 lines), posting-host+lines (20/80/3600 s), posting-host+sorted groups (150/200/1800 s), and From|Sender+Subject+lines (20/40/1800 s). Binaries are recognised by '=ybegin' with line=, size= and name=, or by uuencode; the FAQ (http://www.mixmin.net/cleanfeed/faq.html, opened) adds header scoring on Subject/From/Message-ID/Organization and X-Newsreader rejects.
techniques: Fuzzy body: lowercase, drop lines that are a single 7-70 char non-URL token, drop quoted lines and the last line if > 5 lines, keep only [a-z0-9], then MD5
FSL key: lc(From+Subject) with trailing digits stripped, keep [a-z0-9@\x80-\xFF], append line count
Posting-host+lines is skipped for binaries with (n/m) subjects over 100 lines
new_for_atlas: Tested repost/flood keys and thresholds. They adapt to binaries as (poster, normalised subject, bytes) and (posting-host, size) histories.

title: Harley Hahn's Usenet Center: X-Usenet-Provider and per-user encrypted X-Trace
summary: Providers add headers to every upload, e.g. `X-Usenet-Provider: http://www.giganews.com` and an encrypted `X-Trace: sv3-wzuNQKSmDeZigAUEf/uQhpC7SJnrCeZFJT09...` that the provider can decrypt back to the account. ngprovider's anonymity page (https://www.ngprovider.com/usenet-anonymity.php, opened) says Newsgroupdirect, Blocknews, Usenet.Farm, Newsdemon and theCubeNet replace NNTP-Posting-Host with the server address and encrypt X-Trace.
techniques: X-Usenet-Provider / X-Trace prefix (sv3-) = injecting provider
On those providers NNTP-Posting-Host is provider-level, not per-uploader
new_for_atlas: X-Trace and X-Usenet-Provider are not in Atlas's kept-header list.

title: Spotnet (Spotweb): metadata in the From and X-XML headers, RSA-signed poster identity
summary: Spots encode `From: Nick <PUBKEY-MODULO.USERSIG@[CAT][KEYID][SUBCAT].[SIZE].[RANDOM].[DATE].[CUSTOM-ID].[CUSTOM-VALUE].[SIGNATURE]>`, so category, size and date are visible in XOVER. The full spot XML sits in repeated `X-XML:` headers plus X-XML-Signature, X-User-Key (RSA public key XML), X-User-Signature, X-Server-Key/Signature, X-User-Avatar, X-User-Rating and `X-Newsreader: SpotWeb vX` (Services_Nntp_SpotPosting.php/SpotReading.php opened).
techniques: Extract spot metadata from overview data alone
A stable poster identity from the RSA key modulo gives uploader reputation
The spot XML references the NZB's own message-ids
new_for_atlas: The Spotnet header family and signed identity are not covered.

title: NZBHydra2 duplicate detection across indexers
summary: Two results are duplicates if their normalized titles match (lowercase, remove space . - _), they come from different indexers, and poster/group match when both are known. Posting times must fall within duplicateAgeThreshold (default 2.0 h, baseConfig.yml) and sizes within duplicateSizeThresholdInPercent (default 1.0% of the mean). Thresholds double when only one of poster or group is known.
techniques: normalizeTitle = lower().replaceAll('[ .\-_]','')
age <= 2 h and size diff <= 1% of the average; x2 when only poster or only group is known
new_for_atlas: A simple, tested repost/duplicate rule to fall back on when there is no par2/CRC evidence.

title: node-yencode: crc32_combine and yEnc escape-ratio statistics
summary: Provides crc32_combine (CRC of a+b from crc(a), crc(b) and len(b)), described as 'useful for amalgamating pcrc32s into a crc32', and crc32_zeroes. It states the expected escape ratio is about 1.58% for random data at line size 128: exceeding 5% at 1 KB has probability ~2.2e-12, and >1.85% at 128 KB ~1.2e-14. The decoder also handles NNTP dot-unstuffing ('\r\n.=' -> '\r\n=').
techniques: Combine all parts' pcrc32 values with their sizes into the whole-file CRC32, then compare with SFV, srrDB or the last part's crc32=
Compare XOVER bytes with the yEnc part size to estimate escape ratio; far from ~1.6% means a non-random payload (unencrypted text, zero-filled fakes) (inference)
new_for_atlas: CRC combining gives Atlas file CRC32s for twin matching even when crc32= is missing from the last part.

title: PAR2 Creator and Comment packets identify the PAR2 tool
summary: ParPar writes a Creator packet ('PAR 2.0\0Creator\0') defaulting to 'ParPar (library) v<ver> [https://github.com/animetosho/parpar]', supports ASCII and Unicode Comment packets (--comment), auto-adds Unicode filename packets and uses pow2 packet redundancy. par2cmdline writes 'Created by par2cmdline version X.' (src/creatorpacket.cpp opened).
techniques: Fingerprint the uploader tool from the Creator string plus slice size, volume naming/distribution and packet redundancy
Comment packets may carry uploader text
new_for_atlas: Atlas reads only Main/FileDesc/UniFileN. Creator and Comment packets add fingerprint fields.

title: sabctools yEnc/UU decoder: tolerant parsing rules used by SABnzbd
summary: An =ybegin without part= is single-part, so the body starts immediately and covers the whole size. name= is the rest of the line with trailing whitespace/NUL stripped and a non-UTF-8 fallback; =ypart begin is 1-based; =yend uses pcrc32 first, else crc32. UUencode is still decoded ('begin <perm> <name>', or 60-61-char 'M' lines when begin is missing) along with dot-unstuffing.
techniques: Treat =ybegin without part= as a whole file
Trim NUL/whitespace from name=; decode non-UTF-8 bytes with a fallback
