Detect legacy uuencoded binaries
new_for_atlas: Minor: legacy UU posts and NUL-padded names.

title: newznab-tmux-kd #1088: an advert .html inside the PAR2 set hijacks release names
summary: In alt.binaries.erotica, PAR2 sets included an advert file named like 'B4E Info.. 1080p.html', and PAR2 naming renamed 22 releases to it (19 of them from 2026-10-15). The fix never takes names from .html adverts and restores the subject-derived 'formation name' via releaseCleaner().
techniques: Exclude advert-like FileDesc entries (.htm/.html/.url, tiny size) when picking the naming file from par2
new_for_atlas: Probably your own fork, in which case nothing new. Otherwise, add an advert-file exclusion to PAR2 naming.

title: yEncode draft v1.3 (05-Mar-2002) with the 1.1 to 1.2 to 1.3 change log (SourceForge mirror of the yenc.org text)
summary: Full text of Juergen Helbing's yEnc 1.3 draft. It includes the revision table (v1.0 31-Jul-2001, v1.1 17-Feb-2002 by Steve Blinch, v1.2 28-Feb-2002, v1.3 05-Mar-2002), the per-version change lists, the =ybegin/=ypart/=yend keywords, the escaping rules, multipart semantics and the subject conventions. The original yenc.org copy could not be opened: the Wayback Machine is blocked here and yenc.org is robots-disallowed.
metadata_fields: =ybegin line= size= name= (name MUST be last; up to 256 chars; may contain 0x80-0xFF, control chars, / \ : ? * @; decoders cut leading/trailing spaces)
=ypart begin= end= (1-based inclusive byte offsets in the original file)
=yend size= (part size in multipart) part= pcrc32= crc32= (whole-file, optional)
critical chars NUL 0x00, LF 0x0A, CR 0x0D, '=' 0x3D; TAB removed in 1.2; leading/trailing TAB/SPACE and leading '.' MAY be escaped (1.3 changed 'should' to 'may')
escape = '=' then (byte+42+64)%256; a line may be n+1 chars when an escape falls in column n; typical line=128/256
techniques: Scan for '=ybegin ' WITH a trailing space (the spec reserves '=ybegin2'). If line=/size=/name= are missing, treat the article as text about yEnc, not as a binary.
Validate a part by checking that end-begin+1 equals the =yend size. If the header size, trailer size and decoded size disagree, the part is corrupt.

The spec says begin/end offsets let parts be 'combined from several different sources regardless of the part size'. This means segments of byte-identical reposts that used different article sizes can be aligned and cross-verified.
Subject heuristics: the filename is always quoted, and 'yEnc' sits between the filename and (n/m). Alternate placements (after (#/#) or after the size) are explicitly allowed.
new_for_atlas: Build a byte-range map per file from =ypart begin/end so segments of twins with different article sizes can be aligned and cross-checked. Add an explicit 'not a binary' rule when =ybegin lacks line/size/name. Expect pre-1.2 posts with no total= and with TAB escaped.

title: yEnc FAQ for alt.binaries.sounds.music.classical (geocities.ws mirror, ca. 2002)
summary: An early newsgroup FAQ on posting and decoding yEnc with Agent, XNews, yDec and patched PowerPost. It records which subject layouts let clients join segments, the segment-size limits of the time, and the use of (0/n) parts for NFO text.
metadata_fields: PowerPost template 'Rossini - La gazza ladra [yEnc] [$1/$2] - "$F"' ([yEnc] must come before the filename)
Agent shows (*/8) for a joined file and (1/8), (2/8) for separate segments; listing numbers are line counts, not bytes
(0/n) part used to carry the NFO text
segments of at most 3000-4000 lines, because some servers had problems with larger yEnc segments
XNews 4.12.x mishandled yEnc v1.3 posts made with XNews 5.x
techniques: Old clients joined multipart files purely from subject text, and text after the filename broke Agent's joining. Collection regexes must tolerate comments placed after the quoted filename.
Treat (0/n) articles as NFO/text carriers that belong to the n-file set.
Account for version-era decoder incompatibilities when judging old posts.
new_for_atlas: Attach (0/n) plain-text posts (NFO in the body) to their collection. Accept the PowerPost-era '[yEnc] [$1/$2] - "name"' subject layout in backfilled groups.

title: NZB Format Specification 1.1 (SABnzbd mirror of the defunct docs.newzbin.com)
summary: Mirror of Newzbin's NZB 1.1 specification: DTD '-//newzBin//DTD NZB 1.1//EN' at http://www.newzbin.com/DTD/nzb/nzb-1.1.dtd, namespace http://www.newzbin.com/DTD/2003/nzb. It defines the file-level fields that indexers derive from the overview data.
metadata_fields: head/meta type=title | tag (repeatable) | category | password (repeatable); private types prefixed X-
file@date (Unix time the server saw the article; 'not completely reliable')
segment@bytes (article size), segment@number (from (yy/zz), starts at 1), segment body = Message-ID without < >
techniques: The normalised (1/yy) subject gives a file-level identity that does not depend on any one segment.
Multiple password metas are listed so clients can try each one.
new_for_atlas: Mostly known. Make sure repeated password/tag metas round-trip, and treat file@date as advisory only.

title: Newzbin:NZB Specs ('Retrieved from docs.newzbin.com'): NZB versions 0.9 to 3.0
summary: A copy of the docs.newzbin.com spec page. It lists NZB 0.9, 1.0, 1.1, 1.2, 1.3, 2.0 and 3.0 (DTD/RNC/RNG/XSD) and documents later meta types and attributes that are missing from the common 1.1 spec. Provenance rests only on the page footer.
metadata_fields: meta types title, tag, category, password, hashed (v1.3/v2.0), hash (v3.0)
per-file <meta> (v1.2); a file-level password overrides head-level passwords
v3.0 file@bytes and file@segments; poster/groups not used in v3
techniques: Per-file passwords support releases that mix archives with different passwords.
The 'hashed'/'hash' metas point to NZB-level hashing for identity or obfuscation.
new_for_atlas: Parse and emit per-file <meta> (including a per-file password). Tolerate NZB 1.2-3.0 variants with file@bytes and file@segments.

title: WWW::Newzbin 0.03: Perl wrapper for Newzbin's FileFind and DirectNZB APIs
summary: Documents Newzbin's two-level model. FileFind searches raw files (fileid, subject, posttime, filesize, author, groups), and DirectNZB builds an NZB from either a reportid (an editor-curated release 'report') or a fileid. With a reportid it also returns the report name and Newzbin category.
metadata_fields: search_files params: query, category, group, retention, minsize, maxsize, filetype, resultoffset, resultlimit, sortfield, sortorder
result: fileid, subject, posttime, filesize, author, groups
get_nzb(reportid | fileid): NZB plus report name and category
error codes -1..-5; a positive value is the rate-limit wait in seconds
techniques: Keep stable file-level IDs (fileid) separate from human-assembled release IDs (reportid), so files can be regrouped into reports without losing their identity.
new_for_atlas: Give binaries/files a stable ID independent of the release ID, so deobfuscation or regrouping can move files between releases and keep their history.

title: Newzbin DirectNZB (X-DNZB-*) protocol as implemented in hellanzb (2005-2010) and still parsed by SABnzbd
summary: hellanzb POSTs username/password/reportid to http://www.newzbin.com/api/dnzb/ (citing docs.newzbin.com/Newzbin::DirectNZB) and reads its status and metadata from X-DNZB-* response headers. SABnzbd's urlgrabber.py (https://github.com/sabnzbd/sabnzbd/blob/develop/sabnzbd/urlgrabber.py) still parses an extended X-DNZB set from today's indexers.
metadata_fields: X-DNZB-RText (the 4th token is the wait in seconds)
SAB also reads X-DNZB-MoreInfo, X-DNZB-ProperName, X-DNZB-EpisodeName, X-DNZB-Year, X-DNZB-Failure, X-DNZB-Details, X-DNZB-Password, category_id, Retry-After, Content-Disposition
techniques: Release metadata (name, category, password, proper name, episode) is delivered out of band in HTTP headers, not inside the NZB.
new_for_atlas: Have the Atlas NZB download endpoint send X-DNZB-Name/Category/MoreInfo/ProperName/EpisodeName/Year/Password/Details/Failure for client compatibility.

title: hellanzb ArticleDecoder/SmartPar/DupeHandler: first-segment filename discovery and real-world yEnc quirks
summary: An early NZB downloader whose code and CHANGELOG record posting quirks seen in the wild. Real filenames come from the first segment's =ybegin (uuencode 'begin 644 name' appears only in segment 1), names containing '=' break naive parsing, segments of one file can carry conflicting names, and NZBs can repeat filenames or segment numbers.
metadata_fields: =ybegin split into a fixed number of fields (3, plus part, plus total) so 'name=--=GRUB=-- Puker_S1_D1.par2' survives
pcrc32 preferred; crc32 trusted only when part is 1
PAR2_VOL_RE '(.*)\.vol(\d*)\+(\d*)\.par2'; GET_PAR2_SIZE_RE '.*\.vol\d{1,8}\+(\d{1,8}).par2$' gives the block count
techniques: Smartpar (SmartPar.py): fetch segment 1 of every file first, identify par2 files by their real names, dequeue the extra .volNN+MM.par2 files, and requeue only the blocks actually needed.
Log '<file> has incorrect filename header!' when segments of one file carry different =ybegin names. This signals mixed reposts or a broken NZB.
Requeue segments that fail the CRC check onto another server (multi-backbone completion).
Handle NZBs that list the same filename or segment number twice (newzleech-made NZBs).
new_for_atlas: Use per-segment yEnc-name consistency as a quality and correlation signal. Parse =ybegin with a fixed field split. Read block counts from vol names to estimate repair capacity.

title: newznab 0.2.x SVN mirror (2011): binaries.php and releases.php grouping and request-ID rules
summary: The original newznab pipeline that newznab-tmux descends from. XOVER subjects ending in (n/m) become binaries keyed by md5(subject without counter + From + groupID), and per-group release regexes with named groups name/parts/reqid assemble binaries into releases (binaries.php, db/latestregex.sql).
metadata_fields: binaries: name, fromname, date, xref, totalparts, groupID, binaryhash, relname, relpart, reltotalpart, regexID, reqID, procstat, procattempts
parts: messageID, number (article number), partnumber, size
releaseregex: groupname, regex, ordinal, status, categoryID
techniques: Part regex '/\((\d+)\/(\d+)\)$/i' must match at the end of the subject; binaryhash = md5(subject-minus-counter . From . groupID).
A regex that yields only (?P<reqid>) uses the reqid as the name, later resolved through the allfilled request-ID XML feed.
Binaries with no parts info and older than 18000 s (5 h) are released as '01/01'.
The separators '-', '~' and ' of ' are normalised to '/'. A 'repost\d?|re-?up' token is appended to the name.
Release key is (relname, groupID, reqID, fromname), gated by minfilestoformrelease and ready when num >= reltotalpart.
Dupes are suppressed when the same searchname appears within ±1 day of postdate. Completion % = parts present / sum(totalParts).
new_for_atlas: Mostly inherited through newznab-tmux. Check the ±1-day searchname dupe window, the repost-token handling and the reqid-only name fallback.

title: newznab backfill.php daytopost(): retention probe by binary search over article numbers
summary: Finds the article number closest to N days ago using the GROUP low/high watermarks and repeated postdate() calls (the XOVER Date of a single article), halving the interval each step. It warns when the target is older than the first stored article, which marks the provider's retention edge for that group.
metadata_fields: XOVER Date of a single article number
techniques: Retention probing: postdate(first article) gives the oldest retained post date per group and server.
Map a date to an article number by interval-halving search, comparing on daysOld().
new_for_atlas: Run this probe per provider and group, and store each server's first-article date. Comparing backbones separates retention gaps from takedowns.

title: nZEDb NameFixer.php: predb, hash, filename, PAR2, NFO and mediainfo Unique-ID renaming
summary: nZEDb's deobfuscation engine. It matches release text to predb titles, dehashes 32/40-hex names through predb_hashes, matches inner filenames to predb.filename, and copies names between releases that share a mediainfo Unique ID. MiscSorter.php in the same repo also mines NFOs for IMDb IDs, ISBN/ASIN, Amazon /dp/ links, UPCs and 'presents Artist - Title' lines.
metadata_fields: predb_hashes.hash (binary md5 = 32 hex, sha1 = 40 hex) joined to predb
release_unique.uniqueid (mediainfo Unique ID, i.e. the MKV SegmentUID)
flags proc_nfo, proc_files, proc_par2, proc_uid, dehashstatus, isrenamed; categories OTHER_MISC and OTHER_HASHED
techniques: uidCheck: if another release has the same Unique_ID and already has a predb_id or anidbid (or poster nonscene@Ef.net), and sizes are within ±10%, copy its searchname.
matchPredbFiles: a filename containing \d{2}\.\d{2}\.\d{2} is full-text matched to predb.filename and accepted at similar_text >= 93%.
_cleanMatchFiles strips .partNN, .volNN+NN, path prefixes and leading 'NN-' track numbers before the predb lookup.
Hex-named releases are looked up by the md5/sha1 of the pre title.
checkName runs in order: preDB, then PAR2/filenames, then UID, then the NFO TV/movie/music/game/misc regexes.
new_for_atlas: Index the MKV SegmentUID (Atlas already parses MKV) and use it to carry names between obfuscated twins and alts, gated on ±10% size. Add a predb md5/sha1 hash table for hex-named releases.

title: nZEDb IRC pre/request bots: predb schema and the announce formats of a.b.* request channels
summary: IRC scrapers that feed a predb with request IDs, groups, nuke reasons, file counts and filename stems. Their regexes record the exact announce lines of the Usenet request/fill and pre channels. nZEDb's RequestIDLocal.php resolves releases through predb(requestid, groups_id), and RequestIDWeb.php batches up to 75 lookups to a remote request_url.
metadata_fields: predb columns: title, size, category, predate, source, md5, sha1, requestid, groupid, nuked, nukereason, files, filename, nfo (schema_predb.sql)
PRE: [TV-X264] <title>; NUKE:/UNNUKE:/MODNUKE: <title> [reason] [net]; [SBINDEX] title :: cat :: size :: Aired
'A new NZB has been added: <title> ... <filename> NxSIZE ... -sendnzb <reqid>'
request groups: a.b.teevee, moovee, inner-sanctum, erotica, console.ps3, games.wii/xbox360/nintendods, sounds.flac, mp3.complete_cd, warez, mom, boneless, cd.image, sony.psp, movies.divx
techniques: Request-ID deobfuscation: a '[12345]' subject plus its group maps through predb(requestid, groupid) to a title.
Filenames:[stem] is the scene RAR base name, so releases whose inner or outer names use that stem can be matched.
'FULL 53x100MB' gives volume count times volume size, a shape fingerprint for obfuscated RAR sets.
Parsing 'Pred X ago' gives the pre time, which bounds the post time.
new_for_atlas: Ingest request-channel fills as (group, reqid) mapped to title, filename stem and files x volume-size, and use the stem and shape to match obfuscated sets.

title: nZEDb wiki/docs: crosspost vs duplicate rule, 2-hour collection timeout, predb dumps
summary: Operator documentation. Release-Management gives the SQL for finding crossposts and duplicates; the FAQ says incomplete collections are released 2 hours after their last article; nZEDb_Docs predb.rst and ircscraper.rst describe daily predb dumps (since 2014) and ZNC-based IRC scraping (#nZEDbPRE on synIRC).
techniques: 'select name,fromname,size,count(*) as dupes from releases group by name,fromname,size HAVING dupes > 1': a match in the same group is a true duplicate, and a match in a different group is a crosspost.
Collections with poor subjects or missing parts are force-released 2 h after the last article.
Bulk naming from the nZEDb predb dumps (nZEDb/nZEDbPre_Dumps).
new_for_atlas: When merging twins, label same-group matches as duplicates and different-group matches as crossposts, keyed on name, poster and size.

title: nZEDb comment sharing over Usenet and nzb_guid = md5(first Message-ID)
summary: nZEDb indexers exchanged release comments by posting JSON articles to alt.binaries.zines. The articles are keyed by a release fingerprint that nzedb/NZB.php derives from the first segment Message-ID written into the NZB.
metadata_fields: JSON body USER, TIME, SID, RID, BODY; From <anon@anon.com>
RID / releases.nzb_guid = UNHEX(md5(first segment Message-ID in the NZB))
techniques: Cross-indexer release identity built from Message-IDs, independent of names or regex grouping.
Usenet used as a metadata side channel, as Spotnet does.
new_for_atlas: Compute a deterministic release fingerprint from message-IDs (see also SABnzbd's MD5 over all segment IDs) for cross-indexer matching and federation.

title: Spotnet protocol wiki: spot headers, X-XML, RSA user keys and category codes
summary: Spotnet, a decentralised Dutch Usenet indexing system, posts signed 'spots'. The From header and X-XML carry the category, size, timestamp and the Usenet location of the NZB itself (see also the Spot-Xml-format, Public-Keys and Category-Codes pages).
metadata_fields: X-XML <Spotnet><Posting>: Key, Created, Poster, Tag, Title, Description, Website, Image (Width/Height/Segment), Size, Category/Sub (e.g. 04a03), NZB/Segment <...@spot.net>
Key-IDs: 2 moderator (Team ONG), 3 Spotnet client, 7 decentral/public; a trusted-keys list
category codes, e.g. cat 1: Z type, A format (A15 UHD), B source (B11 WEB-DL, B12 WEBRip), C subtitles/language, D genre
techniques: Link every spot by one uploader through the RSA modulus / X-User-Key, whatever nickname is used.
The signed XML references the NZB by Message-ID, tying an obfuscated post to curated metadata.
new_for_atlas: Ingest Spotnet spots as a naming and metadata source, and use the RSA user key as a poster-identity correlation key.

title: pynntp: XZVER/XZHDR (deflate + yEnc) and XFEATURE COMPRESS GZIP [TERMINATOR]
summary: Implements the undocumented provider extensions for compressed overview data. XZVER/XZHDR return XOVER/XHDR text as raw deflate (zlib wbits -15) wrapped in yEnc with a =yend crc32, and XFEATURE COMPRESS GZIP (reply 290) makes later multi-line replies gzip-compressed. An ietf-nntp post (S. Gucukoglu, 2009-11-28, https://lists.eyrie.org/pipermail/ietf-nntp/2009-November/006066.html) credits COMPRESS GZIP to Giganews and xzver to Astraweb, and Giganews' Accelerator page claims header downloads up to 10x faster.
metadata_fields: XZVER <range>: 224 reply; body = yEnc(=ybegin .. =yend crc32) of raw deflate
XFEATURE COMPRESS GZIP: 290; later status lines contain 'COMPRESS=GZIP'; gzip (wbits 15+32)
'XFEATURE COMPRESS GZIP TERMINATOR': '.\r\n' sits inside the compressed stream; without it the terminator follows the stream
LIST OVERVIEW.FMT drives the field mapping
techniques: Cut header bandwidth for XOVER backfill.
Check decompressed overview data against the yEnc crc32.
new_for_atlas: Use XZVER or XFEATURE COMPRESS GZIP for XOVER when the server offers it, and verify the crc32 on XZVER payloads.

title: RFC 8315 Cancel-Locks in Netnews Articles (2018)
summary: Defines Cancel-Lock and Cancel-Key, which authenticate 'Control: cancel' and Supersedes, and updates RFC 5537. It says the scheme 'prevents tracking of individual users'.
metadata_fields: schemes: sha256 (mandatory to implement), sha512, sha1 (limited/obsolete), md5 obsolete, sha224/sha384 limited
lock = Base64(hash(Base64(K))), key = Base64(K), recommended K = HMAC(sec, uid+mid) where mid includes <>
techniques: To verify a cancel or supersede, hash each c-key and compare it with the c-lock of the same scheme in the target article.
K is per-Message-ID, so locks cannot link one poster's articles. Only the presence and scheme of the header fingerprint the client or server software.
new_for_atlas: Record Cancel-Lock presence and scheme as a software fingerprint. Verify Supersedes/cancel before dropping a target article from a release.

title: INN nnrpd/post.c: Injection-Info construction, obsolete trace headers, server-side Cancel-Lock
summary: Shows the exact Injection-Info that INN (the reference server) adds, and marks NNTP-Posting-Host, X-Trace, X-Complaints-To and NNTP-Posting-Date as obsolete. It also generates Cancel-Lock server-side, keyed on the username or the client IP.
metadata_fields: obsolete (HTobs): NNTP-Posting-Host, X-Trace, X-Complaints-To, NNTP-Posting-Date, Date-Received, Posting-Version, Relay-Version, Also-Control, Article-Names, Article-Updates, See-Also
Cancel-Lock identity = username or IP (addcanlockuser); Cancel-Key added for cancel/supersede
techniques: logging-data is the nnrpd process id, one per client connection. Articles that share path-identity, posting-host and logging-data came from the same NNTP session.
posting-account can expose, or stably hash, the account.
new_for_atlas: Parse Injection-Info into separate fields instead of one string, and group articles by (path-identity, logging-data) as a same-session hint.

title: Big-8 wiki 'Usenet headers' sample: INN X-Trace field order and reinjection Old-* headers
summary: A real header block showing the classic INN X-Trace format and the headers left behind when a moderation robot reinjects an article.
metadata_fields: X-Trace: reader1.panix.com 1260746750 22049 166.84.1.6 (13 Dec 2009 23:25:50 GMT): server, Unix time, pid, client IP, date
Old-X-Complaints-To, Old-NNTP-Posting-Date (the original injection is preserved on reinjection)
X-User-ID and X-NNTP-Posting-Host (opaque or hashed provider IDs)
Cancel-Lock: sha1:..., Bytes:, Lines:, Xref:, Approved:, X-Auth (PGPMoose)
techniques: Split INN-style X-Trace: the same server and pid with close timestamps means the same posting session.
Opaque per-account IDs such as X-User-ID are stable per account and link posts within one provider.
new_for_atlas: Parse X-Trace when it matches '<host> <unix> <pid> <ip> (<date>)', and keep X-User-ID, X-NNTP-Posting-Host and Old-* headers.

title: Highwinds/Easynews injection headers in a quoted article (pcreview.co.uk thread, Dec 2014)
summary: A complete header block for an article posted through Easynews on the Highwinds backbone. It shows the Highwinds-specific X-Received-* headers and the POSTED path marker.
metadata_fields: X-Complaints-To: abuse@easynews.com; X-Complaints-Info: 'Please be sure to forward a copy of ALL headers...'
techniques: The element before '.POSTED' (fx06.iad) names the Highwinds front-end and PoP that accepted the post; Organization and X-Complaints-To name the reseller brand.

X-Received-Body-CRC looks like a decimal 32-bit checksum of the body as received, with X-Received-Bytes as its size. This is an inference to verify. If it holds, a cheap HEAD can flag byte-identical article bodies across reposts without fetching BODY.
new_for_atlas: Atlas keeps X-Complaints-To but not X-Received-Bytes, X-Received-Body-CRC, X-Complaints-Info or the POSTED path token. Capture them and test whether equal body-CRCs detect article-level twins.

title: RFC 5536 Netnews Article Format (2009): ABNF for Path diagnostics, Injection-Info, Archive, Supersedes, Control, Xref
summary: Normative syntax for the headers Atlas stores, and for several it does not.
metadata_fields: Path: path-identity ['!' diag]... tail-entry ('not-for-mail'); diag '!!' (verified), '!.KEYWORD[.identity]' (e.g. POSTED), deprecated '!IPv4'
Injection-Info params posting-host (host, IP or host:IP), posting-account, logging-data, mail-complaints-to, x-*
Supersedes: one msg-id (same effect as a cancel plus the new article)
Control: verb args (must not appear together with Supersedes)
Message-ID at most 250 octets; id-right case-sensitive; agents 'should make identifiers unpredictable'
Lines deprecated; Date-Received, Posting-Version, Relay-Version obsolete
techniques: Use the '!.POSTED' and '!!' Path diagnostics to find the injecting server.
Several group:number pairs in Xref mean one Message-ID was crossposted.
Follow Supersedes chains to replace outdated articles in a release.
new_for_atlas: Parse Path diagnostics plus Archive, Supersedes, Control and Approved into fields, and mark crossposts at article level from multi-group Xref.

title: X-No-Archive (Wikipedia): header or first body line, standardised as 'Archive: no'
summary: History and meaning of X-No-Archive, which DejaNews (1995) honoured, and of its RFC 5536 successor 'Archive: no'. Some archives also look for the token in the first line of the body.
metadata_fields: X-No-Archive: yes (as a header or as the first body line)
techniques: Check both the header and the first body line for the opt-out.
new_for_atlas: Minor: store X-No-Archive/Archive flags, including the first-body-line form, as poster-intent metadata. They are rare in binaries.

title: Parity Volume Set Specification 2.0 (May 2003): packet-level PAR2
summary: The PAR2 specification. It defines packets Atlas does not read yet (IFSC slice checksums, Creator, comments, RFSC and packed variants), says the slice-free index file carries the Main, FileDesc and IFSC packets, and gives Usenet posting conventions.
metadata_fields: packet header: magic 'PAR2\0PKT', 8-byte length, 16-byte packet MD5, 16-byte Recovery Set ID, 16-byte type
Main 'PAR 2.0\0Main': slice size, file count, sorted File IDs of the recovery set plus the non-recovery set
FileDesc: File ID, MD5, MD5-16k, length, name; File ID = MD5(MD5-16k, length, name)
IFSC 'PAR 2.0\0IFSC': per-slice MD5 + CRC32, with the last slice zero-padded
RecvSlic (exponent + data); Creator 'PAR 2.0\0Creator\0' (client name and version, mandatory in every file)
optional UniFileN, CommASCI, CommUni, FileSlic, RFSC, PkdMain, PkdRecvS
naming file.vol20-29.par2; Appendix B example packet holding a newsgroup name and an article-subject regex
techniques: Whole-file CRC32 from the small index .par2 alone: chain the IFSC slice CRCs with crc32_combine, then remove the last slice's zero padding. That gives a CRC32 for every protected file, for SFV, srrDB archive-crc and yEnc crc32 matching, without downloading any data.
Recovery Set ID = MD5(Main body), and File IDs include the filename, so renamed or obfuscated reposts of identical content get different set IDs. Key twins on FileDesc MD5 + length instead.
The Creator packet text (QuickPar, par2cmdline, MultiPar, ParPar plus version) fingerprints the uploader's tool.
File IDs in the non-recovery set show files (e.g. NFO, SFV) that ship unprotected.
new_for_atlas: Parse IFSC, Creator and comment packets; derive whole-file CRC32s from IFSC; key twins on (MD5, length), not on set ID.

title: Parity Volume Set Specification 3.0 (2022-01-28 ALPHA DRAFT)
summary: Draft successor to PAR2. It uses CRC-64-ISO rolling hashes and 16-byte BLAKE3 fingerprints and can carry directory trees and OS metadata.
metadata_fields: Creator 'PAR CRE\0' (must include the client version), Comment 'PAR COM\0'
Start 'PAR STA\0' (parent InputSetID, parent Root checksum or a unique number, block size, Galois field)
Data 'PAR DAT\0'; External Data 'PAR EXT\0' (CRC-64 + BLAKE3 per block)
matrix packets 'PAR CAU\0', 'PAR SPA\0', 'PAR EXP\0'; Recovery Data 'PAR REC\0'
File packet: name, rolling hash of the first 16 kB, chunk descriptions (length, BLAKE3, first block index, tail)
UNIX Permissions 'PAR UNX\0': atime, ctime, mtime (ns), UID, GID, i_mode, owner name, group name, xattrs; FAT Permissions packet
techniques: Owner and group names, UID/GID and nanosecond mtimes would be strong uploader fingerprints if posters ship PAR3.
The rolling CRC-64 finds blocks at unexpected offsets, which helps match content across re-wrapped posts.
new_for_atlas: Future-proofing: recognise PAR3 packets and extract Creator, file names and 16k hashes, and the UNIX/FAT permission metadata.

title: Parity Volume Set Specification v1.0 (PAR1, 2001-2003)
summary: The PAR1 index (.PAR, with volumes .P00 to .P99, then .Q00 onwards) stores each file's MD5, MD5-16k, size and name plus a comment. Its set hash is the MD5 over the full-file MD5s of the protected files.
metadata_fields: control hash (MD5 of the file from offset 0x0020)
set hash = MD5(array of full-file MD5s, not the 16k hashes)
techniques: The PAR1 set hash depends only on content, so identical sets reposted under new names keep it. PAR2's set ID changes with the filenames.
Renaming by 16k MD5 already existed in PAR1.
new_for_atlas: Parse PAR1 (.PAR/.Pnn) in old or backfilled groups and use its content-only set hash as a twin key.

title: SABnzbd deobfuscate_filenames.py: obfuscation classifier, biggest-file rule, PAR2 16k renaming
summary: Post-download deobfuscation in the most widely used client. It encodes explicit, testable thresholds for deciding whether a filename is obfuscated.
metadata_fields: PAR2 FileDesc md5of16k mapped to the real name
techniques: Certainly obfuscated: ^[a-f0-9]{32}$; ^[a-f0-9.]{40,}$; [a-f0-9]{30} together with at least two '[word]' groups; names starting 'abc.xyz'.

Not obfuscated: (upper >= 2 and lower >= 2 and spaces/dots/underscores >= 1), or separators >= 3, or (letters >= 4 and digits >= 4 and separators >= 1), or (starts uppercase, lower > 2, upper/lower <= 0.25). Everything else defaults to obfuscated.
Rename only the biggest file when it is more than 3x the next one (plus look-alikes such as -sample). Add missing extensions by content sniffing, and skip when DVD/Bluray folders are present.
decode_par2: compare md5(first 16384 bytes) of every file with the par2 md5of16k map.
new_for_atlas: Adopt an explicit is_obfuscated(name) classifier with these thresholds, to decide when to spend NNTP budget on deobfuscation and how far to trust a name.

title: SABnzbd at download time: first articles first, md5of16k renaming, NZB message-ID hash, STAT pre-check
summary: SABnzbd fetches the first article of every file first and renames files from PAR2 md5-of-first-16KiB before writing them. It falls back to the yEnc name only when that name does not look obfuscated. nzbparser.py fingerprints an NZB as the MD5 over all segment Message-IDs, and newswrapper.py pre-checks articles with 'STAT <msgid>'.
metadata_fields: nzo.md5of16k {hash: name} built from every par2 file
nzf.md5of16k of the decoded first article
nzo.md5sum = MD5 over every segment Message-ID in NZB order (dupe key)
techniques: Hash the first 16 KiB of decoded segment 1 (a ~700 KB article always covers it) and look it up in the union of all par2 maps. The code notes that 'due to strong obfuscation on article-level the parset could have a different name'.
Prospectively add repair blocks from every par set when files cannot be tied to one set.
An NZB's content fingerprint is the MD5 of its Message-ID list.
STAT pre-check decides completeness before downloading.
new_for_atlas: If not already done, match md5(first 16 KiB of segment 1) for every file against all PAR2 sets in the release, and add a message-ID-set hash as a post-identity key. NNTmux upstream already does a similar 16 KiB check.

title: Usenet retention/removal test: methodology and results (usenet.rexum.space, July 2026)
summary: A large probing study of about 78,000 NZBs from Aug 2008 to Jul 2026, with 7,309,251 sampled segments checked against 10 providers. It probes with ARTICLE because STAT/HEAD 'can sometimes remain positive even when the article body' is gone. Context: Tom's Guide (13-Nov-2012, https://tomsguide.com/us/Usenet-DMCA-Takedown-File-Retention-Piracy,news-16296.html) reports anti-piracy firms watching indexers such as Newzbin/NZBMatrix and sending notices right after links appear.
metadata_fields: probe = ARTICLE with the body fully drained
430 (no such article) and 451 (article removed) count as unavailable; broken transfers retried up to 3 times
up to 100 segments per NZB, evenly spaced, including the first and last
age = checked_at - nzb_date; 90-day buckets; at least 30 checks; >= 95% passes; two consecutive failing buckets end the horizon
horizons: Eweka 6,570 d, Newshosting 6,570 d, PureUsenet 4,140 d, TweakNews 4,050 d, EasyUsenet 990 d, Blocknews 450 d, Giganews/UsenetExpress/ViperNews 90 d, Usenet.Farm 0 d
techniques: Header-only survival (STAT/HEAD succeed, BODY returns 430/451) is a visible signature of body removal or takedown.
Deterministic segment sampling scores availability per backbone.
Keep 451 separate from 430.
new_for_atlas: Health checks should sample BODY/ARTICLE, not only STAT, and record 451 vs 430 per backbone. STAT-positive with BODY-negative flags a likely takedown.

title: ngPost (mbruel) obfuscation: UUID subject equals Message-ID, random From per article, random groups
summary: A popular uploader that sends only From, Newsgroups, Subject and Message-ID. In obfuscation mode the Subject is the same 32-hex UUID used as the Message-ID local part, and the random From addresses reuse the Message-ID signature domain (NgPost.h, ngPost.conf).
metadata_fields: Subject = the same 32-hex UUID when obfuscate = article
From = 13 random characters @<signature>.com (GEN_FROM: random per post or per article)
no Date or User-Agent sent by the client
GROUP_POLICY ALL / EACH_POST / EACH_FILE (random group per file)
random archive name length 22, password length 15
techniques: Fingerprint: subject equals the Message-ID local part (32 hex) and the From domain equals '<msgid-domain>.com'. This groups articles even when every poster name is random.
EACH_FILE scatters files across groups, so merge collections across groups by Message-ID domain, time window and the 716800-byte payload.
No client User-Agent or Date header points to ngPost-style posting.
new_for_atlas: Add posting-tool detection from Message-ID shape and header set, and merge scattered obfuscated uploads across groups.

title: Nyuu (animetosho) defaults: Message-ID with a millisecond timestamp, From built from the local user and host
summary: Nyuu's default Message-ID is 24 letters alternating upper and lower case, then '-', a 13-digit millisecond Unix time and '@nyuu'. Its defaults in config.js and help-full.txt also set User-Agent Nyuu/<version> and a From built from the local username and hostname.
metadata_fields: Message-ID default ([A-Z][a-z]){12}-\d{13}@nyuu (time the post was generated; --date overrides)
From default: '$USER <$USER@<hostname>.localdomain>' (nyuu.uploader when the hostname is unusable)
--yenc-name, --nzb-subject and --nzb-poster overrides (the NZB can differ from what was posted)
techniques: Read the exact generation time from the Message-ID even when the Date header is altered.
The default From leaks the uploader's OS account and hostname, a strong poster link.
When the NZB subject or poster differs from the article headers, the obfuscation is deliberate.
new_for_atlas: Parse Nyuu-style Message-IDs for timestamps, record From local-part and host patterns, and flag NZB-vs-article header mismatches.

title: node-yencode README: CRC32 combine and zeroes math, escape ratio, NNTP dot-unstuffing
summary: A fast yEnc/CRC32 library that documents the CRC algebra needed to merge per-part CRCs and the expected yEnc overhead.
metadata_fields: crc32_combine(crc1, crc2, len2), described as useful for amalgamating pcrc32s into a crc32
crc32_zeroes(len), where a negative len removes trailing zero bytes
expected escape ratio about 0.0158 for random data at line length 128

decode with stripDots; end markers '
=y' or '
.
'; '
.=' becomes '
='
techniques: Whole-file CRC32 from the per-part pcrc32 values and part sizes when every trailer is available.
Strip the PAR2 zero padding from the last IFSC slice CRC with a negative crc32_zeroes.
Estimate the decoded payload from XOVER bytes (about decoded x 1.0158, plus CRLF every 128 bytes, plus headers) to infer article size, posting tool and file size before downloading.
new_for_atlas: Add CRC32 combine/unpad helpers (port zlib crc32_combine to Rust) for IFSC and pcrc32 derivations, and estimate decoded size from XOVER bytes.

title: newznab-tmux-kd issues #476 and #481: last-segment yEnc crc32 coverage test and the srrDB archived-files fix
summary: In this test, 0 of 500 releases over 1 GiB had a whole-file crc32 on the final =yend: 472 final segments carried only pcrc32 and 28 never reached the last part. About 193 MiB and 145 s were spent, and the idea was closed wontfix on 2026-09-06. Issue #481 (https://github.com/KurzonDax/newznab-tmux-kd/issues/481) fixed srrDB validation to check 'archived-files' (inner name, size, crc, e.g. tdf-hpatcos.avi 731893760 0053CA13) instead of the outer 'files'.
metadata_fields: srrDB details: files (outer RAR, NFO, SFV, sample) vs archived-files (inner name, size, crc)
techniques: Search srrDB by archive-crc plus exact size, then verify the inner file in archived-files, requiring a unique candidate and a release-size tolerance.
new_for_atlas: Don't rely on last-segment crc32 (it is absent in practice). Get the inner CRC32 from PAR2 IFSC or from the last RAR volume's file header instead, then apply the archived-files check.

title: srrDB API v1 docs: archive-crc, archive-size, isdbhash and store-real-crc search keywords
summary: API of srrDB, the scene release reconstruction database. Its search keywords allow lookups by archive CRC and size, OpenSubtitles hash, and stored-file CRC. A PowerShell client (https://www.powershellgallery.com/packages/SrrDBAutomationToolkit/0.4.0/Content/Public%5CSearch-SatRelease.ps1) also exposes RarHash, ArchiveCrc, ArchiveSize, InternetSubtitlesDbHash, SampleFilename and SampleCrc.
metadata_fields: keywords: r, date, nfo, srs, foreign, confirmed, rarhash, category, imdb, start, archive-crc, archive-size, isdbhash, lower, endorstartwithdot, firstupper, compressed, word, order, page, skip, skipr, store-real-filename, store-real-crc; 'group:' appears in an example URL
techniques: OpenSubtitles moviehash (Atlas already computes it) into an isdbhash: search returns the scene release name.
Inner file CRC32 plus size into archive-crc:/archive-size: returns the release, then verify it against archived-files.
store-real-filename/store-real-crc for bare, non-RAR files; sample CRC and filename for -sample files.
new_for_atlas: Feed the existing moviehash into srrDB isdbhash lookups, and add rate-limited archive-crc/size and store-real-crc queries.

title: RAR 5.0 archive format technote (rarlab): volume numbers, split-file CRC rules, owner, time and hash records
summary: The field-level RAR5 format. Several fields order obfuscated multi-volume sets, fingerprint the packer, and identify the inner file whatever the wrapper.
metadata_fields: main flags 0x1 volume, 0x2 volume number present, 0x4 solid, 0x8 recovery record, 0x10 locked; volume number absent in the first volume, 1 = second
main extra records 0x01 Locator (quick-open and recovery-record offsets), 0x02 Metadata (original archive name and original creation time)
service headers CMT (comment), QO, ACL, STM, RR
file header: flags, unpacked size, attributes, mtime, data CRC32, compression info (version, solid, method 0-5, dictionary 128 KB x 2^N), host OS (0 Windows, 1 Unix), UTF-8 name

extra 0x01 encryption (log2 KDF count, 16-byte salt, 16-byte IV, 12-byte check value), 0x02 BLAKE2sp hash, 0x03 file times (mtime/ctime/atime, ns), 0x04 version, 0x05 redirection, 0x06 Unix owner (user and group names, uid/gid), 0x07 service data
end-of-archive flag 0x1 'volume and not last'; header flags 0x8/0x10 mark data continuing from or into the adjacent volume
techniques: Order randomly named volumes by the volume-number field and the EOA 'not last' flag instead of .partNN names.

Split files: non-last volumes store the CRC32/hash of the packed data in that volume, while the last part (and unsplit files) store the unpacked file's CRC32/BLAKE2sp. The first article of the last volume therefore identifies the inner file, for alt detection across different wrappings and for srrDB archived-files lookups.
The Metadata record can reveal the original archive name and creation time behind obfuscated volume names.
A shared encryption salt/KDF groups volumes. Unix owner names, host OS, method/dictionary and mtimes fingerprint the packer.
new_for_atlas: Atlas lists inner names and sizes. Add volume number/EOA ordering, inner CRC32/BLAKE2sp from the last volume, the Metadata-record archive name, owner names, host OS, method/dictionary, file times and encryption salt as correlation keys.

title: SANS GCFA paper 'Forensic Primer: Usenet Evidence' (Mark Lachniet, accepted 2006, revised 2008)
summary: A forensic overview of binary Usenet artefacts. It documents carving signatures and notes that the Message-ID and Path identify the originating server, whose logs investigators subpoena for the poster's IP.
metadata_fields: 'Rar!' and 'PAR2\0PKT' signatures; PAR2 footer naming the creating program
techniques: Message-ID and Path lead to the originating server, then to provider logs (the identity route investigators use).
new_for_atlas: Nothing new, beyond confirming that old .rNN RAR and .PNN PAR1 naming still needs grouping in backfilled groups.

title: UsenetDHT: A Low Overhead Usenet Server (Sit, Dabek, Robertson; IPTPS 2004)
summary: Academic measurement and design paper. In early 2004 the feed was about 1.4 TB/day (about 4M articles/day); binaries grew from about 300 GB/day (2001) to about 2 TB/day, while text stayed near 1 GB/day from 400k articles. Overview costs about 512 bytes per article, and only about 1% of articles were read at a Giganews-outsourcing ISP.
metadata_fields: NOV/overview cost of about 512 bytes per article
techniques: Content-addressed storage keeps identical articles once (dedup at article level).
Overview sizing for capacity planning.
new_for_atlas: Nothing new technically; a sizing baseline for overview storage.

title: NZBIndex API: raw collections with per-file availableParts/totalParts
summary: A public raw-indexer API (no release curation) exposing collections and their files. It is a reference for a binsearch/nzbindex-style raw view next to curated releases.
metadata_fields: search: q, max, sort (agedesc/ageasc/sizedesc/sizeasc), minage, maxage, minsize, maxsize, poster, groups (repeatable), complete=1, page
collection: id, name, poster, posted (Unix), size, fileCount, complete (bool), groups[]
files[]: name, totalParts, availableParts, posted, size
techniques: Completeness per file = availableParts / totalParts.
The poster email filter works as a correlation pivot.
new_for_atlas: Optional: expose a raw collection/file view with availableParts/totalParts.

title: Internet Archive item 'fanzub': retired anime NZB indexer's source code and 2015-03-01 database dump
summary: Archived when Fanzub, a Japanese-media Usenet indexer, shut down, and uploaded 2015-11-24. It holds fanzub-data.2015-03-01.sql.bz2 (8,631,875,683 bytes), fanzub-source-code.zip (165,960 bytes, 65 files) and a torrent. The contents were not inspected because the zip listing failed.
techniques: Use a historical indexer database as ground truth for regression-testing grouping on anime posts.
new_for_atlas: A possible large real-world test corpus (posts and collections up to 2015) for Atlas's grouping and twin logic.

title: NNTmux wiki 'Postprocessing': upstream PAR2 mapping and obfuscated-file probing budgets
summary: The upstream project already probes the first article of up to 3 of the largest unclassified files, reads PAR2 indexes to recover names, and maps files by unique size or by first-16KiB hash / yEnc name and size. This is a parity baseline for the Rust port.
metadata_fields: 7z end header recovered from the final article of the highest volume, checked against its CRC
techniques: Map PAR2 files to NZB files only where the size is unique in both directions; verify ambiguous ones by first 16 KiB hash or yEnc name/size.
Build 7z listings from the final article of the highest volume (the end header).
new_for_atlas: Parity check only: confirm the Rust port has all of this. The genuinely new items are the IFSC-derived CRCs, the last-RAR-volume CRC and the Creator fingerprints.

title: rapidyenc encoder (the core of node-yencode and Nyuu): exact yEnc escape set and line-length rule
summary: rapidyenc is the SIMD yEnc library behind node-yencode (which Nyuu uses), and its README lists bindings for Go, .NET, Rust, Kotlin and SABnzbd's sabctools. It escapes NUL, CR, LF and '=' anywhere. TAB, SPACE and '.' are escaped only as the first byte of a line, TAB and SPACE (but not '.') as the last byte of a line, and a TAB or SPACE that ends the article is also escaped. A line closes after line_size-1 columns plus one more byte, which may be escaped, so encoded lines are line_size or line_size+1 bytes long.
metadata_fields: src/encoder.cc escapeLUT: the critical bytes NUL, CR, LF and '=' are escaped anywhere
src/encoder.cc escapedLUT: also TAB, SPACE and '.', used at the start of a line, and at the end of a line except for '.'
doEnd: a TAB or SPACE as the final byte of the article is escaped
line_size (default 128): encoded lines are 128 or 129 bytes
README: CRC32 combine and zero-run helpers (pcrc32 to crc32)
techniques: Body-level encoder fingerprint: rapidyenc never escapes a TAB ('=I') or SPACE ('=`') in the middle of a line, and never leaves a TAB or SPACE unescaped as the last byte of a line; seeing either rules it out
Per-article line-length profile: every line is 128 or 129 bytes except the last. This separates rapidyenc from encoders that count escapes inside a fixed 128-byte width
These quirks are in the body, so header obfuscation and Message-ID spoofing cannot hide them. Compare the body style with the tool implied by the Message-ID or X-Newsposter and flag mismatches
new_for_atlas: New. Atlas reads only the =y lines. Recording an encoder style per article (escape set, line lengths, trailer formatting) gives a tool fingerprint that header obfuscation cannot change. It needs one raw BODY sampled per file.

title: NewsUP yEnc.pm, copied into ngPost Yenc.cpp: trailing whitespace left unescaped and pcrc32 not zero-padded
summary: NewsUP's Inline-C encoder uses maxwidth 128, counts escapes in that width, and escapes NUL, LF, CR and '=' anywhere but TAB, SPACE and '.' only at column 0. Its end-of-line test 'column - 1 == maxwidth' can never be true, so a TAB or SPACE that ends a line is left raw. pcrc32 is printed with %x and is not zero-padded. ngPost's src/utils/Yenc.cpp (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mbruel/ngPost/master/src/utils/Yenc.cpp) is the same code and carries the line 'Copyright (C) 2015-2018 David Emanuel Santiago and NewsUP contributors'.
metadata_fields: =ybegin part= total= line=128 size= name=<real file name>
=yend size= pcrc32=<lowercase hex, not zero-padded>, with no part= and no crc32= (Article.pm)
TAB or SPACE may appear raw as the last byte of a line
techniques: Lineage test: escaped leading whitespace, raw trailing whitespace and a pcrc32 shorter than 8 hex digits together point to NewsUP or ngPost
Left-pad pcrc32 and crc32 values to 8 hex digits before comparing them with CRCs from PAR2, SFV or srrDB

Tell NewsUP and ngPost apart by their headers. In ngPost obfuscation mode the Subject equals the 32-hex local part of the Message-ID. NewsUP article subjects look like '[n/N] - "file" (p/P)' with no 'yEnc' token, and NewsUP adds an 'X-' prefix to any custom header
new_for_atlas: New. An encoder-lineage signal, plus a normalization rule for short CRC strings.

title: NewsUP --obfuscate: per-article Message-IDs that imitate JBinUp, JBinDown, Nyuu, PowerPost, newsmangler and GoPostStuff
summary: In obfuscation mode, generate_random_ids picks one of eight Message-ID generators for each article. Article.pm gives each article a random From and a random Subject of 1-32 lowercase letters. newsup.pl posts each article to a random subset of the configured groups and does not post the NZB. The yEnc name= still carries the real file name; a code comment says hiding it would break the yEnc spec.
metadata_fields: newsmangler imitation: <sec>.<usec>.<0-1023>@<one of 28 provider hosts such as news.giganews.com or news.usenet.farm>
random alphabet: [0-9A-Za-z] plus '-', '_', '.' and '$', never two symbols in a row
techniques: If one file's articles switch between Message-ID formats of different tools, that is the NewsUP obfuscation signature. Do not assign a tool to each article separately

Check imitations strictly against the real formats. A real Nyuu ID has 24 letters in alternating case, a '-' and a 13-digit millisecond timestamp; the imitation has a local part of about 12 characters that can include symbols, plus a sec+usec number. Real GoPostStuff IDs are '<UnixNano$gps@gopoststuff>'; the imitation uses the domain 'gpoststuff'. The partNofM in a PowerPost imitation does not match the yEnc part and total
Most imitation formats embed sec and usec from gettimeofday, the real generation time, so they still order and cluster articles
Subject, From and Newsgroups are all random per article, so group articles by yEnc name=, size= and total= and by =ypart ranges across all the configured groups
new_for_atlas: New. Atlas's tool fingerprints must use strict, validated patterns, and 'mixed Message-ID tool formats within one file' should be a first-class obfuscation feature.

title: Newspost 2.x (C): User-Agent, 'File NN of M:' subjects, no client Message-ID, and a yEnc encoder that escapes TAB
summary: Newspost (base/nntp.c) sends From, Newsgroups, Subject and 'User-Agent: Newspost/2.2.1 (http://github.com/PietjeBell88/newspost)', plus optional Reply-To, Followup-To, Organization, References, 'X-No-Archive: yes' and extra headers, but no Message-ID or Date. Subjects (base/newspost.c) take the form '<subject> - File 01 of 12: "name" yEnc (001/123)'. Its encoder escapes NUL, TAB, LF, CR and '=' anywhere and '.' only at column 0, and never escapes SPACE; lines are 128 columns with escapes counted, and base/encode.c writes '=yend size= part= pcrc32=%08x' with ' crc32=%08x' added on the last part.
metadata_fields: Subject: '<subject> - File NN of M: "<name>" yEnc (PP/P)', zero-padded
single part: '=ybegin line=128 size= name=' and '=yend size= crc32=%08x'
multipart: '=ybegin part= total= line=128 size= name=', '=ypart begin= end=', '=yend size= part= pcrc32=%08x [crc32=%08x]'
techniques: An escaped TAB in the middle of a line, with raw SPACE at line edges, points to a newspost-style encoder
'File NN of M:' explains why the newznab file-count regexes accept ' of ' as a separator
Newspost sends no Message-ID, so the injecting server creates it (see the INN generator finding). Its shape identifies the server, not the client
new_for_atlas: New poster profile covering headers, subject format and body style.

title: sanguinews (Ruby): X-Newsposter with the Ruby version, a local-offset Date, and wrong =ypart offsets on the last part
summary: sanguinews writes From, Newsgroups, a Subject of the form '<prefix>"name" yEnc (n/N)', 'X-Newsposter: sanguinews v<VERSION> (ruby <RUBY_VERSION>) - https://github.com/tdobrovolskij/sanguinews', an optional 'X-No-Archive: yes', and a Date from DateTime.now that carries the poster's local %z offset. It computes =ypart begin and end as (part-1)*len+1 and part*len from the current chunk's own length (sanguinews.rb sets msg.length to that chunk's length), so a short last part gets offsets that do not continue from the previous part. pcrc32 and crc32 are written with to_s(16) and are not zero-padded.
metadata_fields: Date: local time with a numeric offset
=yend size=<len> part=<n> pcrc32=<hex>, plus crc32=<hex> on the last part
techniques: The Date offset gives the uploader's time zone, and the Ruby version narrows down the machine

Bug signature: a last part whose =ypart begin is not the previous end+1, and whose end is not the file size, identifies sanguinews. Reassemble by part number and NZB order rather than trusting begin and end
Zero-pad CRC hex values before comparing them
new_for_atlas: New poster profile, and a reassembly edge case Atlas must tolerate.

title: nntpPoster autoposter: GUID-named obfuscated uploads reported to an indexer through 'api?hash={0}&name={1}' or an NZB upload
summary: nntpPoster renames each upload to Guid.NewGuid().ToString("N"), which is 32 lowercase hex characters, and can set a random GUID as the RAR password. It then tells 'a select indexer' the real name in one of two ways. NewznabHash sends a GET to ObfuscatedNotificationUrl with {0} = obfuscated name and {1} = original name (sample: https://api.apiserver.com/api?hash={0}&name={1}&apikey=${ApiKey}); NzbPost uploads '<CleanedName>.nzb' as a multipart form field named 'file'. It checks the result with a newznab search (t=search&q={0}&maxage={1}). Its posting client (PostingNntpClient/SimpleNntpPostingClient.cs) uses the Message-ID offered in the server's 340 reply, otherwise '<32-hex GUID@server address>', writes the Date with a literal '(UTC)' after the numeric offset, and folds Newsgroups onto continuation lines indented with TAB.
metadata_fields: obfuscated name: 32 lowercase hex characters (GUID 'N' format)
RAR password: 32 hex characters (GUID) when ApplyRandomPassword is set
NZB upload: multipart field NzbPostFilenameParam=file, with NzbPostExtraParams
Message-ID: from the server's 340 reply, else <guid@host>
Newsgroups: one group per TAB-indented continuation line
techniques: Build the receiving side in Atlas: a newznab-compatible hash=&name= endpoint and an NZB-upload endpoint that store the mapping from obfuscated name to real name as a high-trust donor (source-based indexing)
Treat 32-hex GUID release names and 32-hex passwords as one obfuscation family
Header signatures: '@<posting server host>' in client-made IDs, '(UTC)' after the numeric offset, and multi-line Newsgroups
new_for_atlas: New. A name feed from uploader to indexer that Atlas can accept instead of having to infer names.

title: INN nnrpd server-generated Message-IDs '<sec32$pid32$count@domain>' and the '340 Ok, recommended Message-ID' reply
summary: INN's GenerateMessageID returns '<%s$%s$%d@%s>'. The first part is Radix32(now - 673416000), the second Radix32(getpid()), and the number is a counter that increases with each post in the same NNTP session; lib/radix32.c writes most-significant digit first with the alphabet '0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuv'. nnrpd/commands.c offers this ID to the client as '340 Ok, recommended Message-ID <...>'. Clients that omit a Message-ID (newspost) or take the recommended one (nntpPoster) end up with this format.
metadata_fields: sec32: base-32 count of seconds since 673416000 (1991-05-05 04:00 UTC)
pid32: base-32 PID of the nnrpd process, one per client connection
count: article counter within the session
domain: the domain of the access realm, else the server FQDN
techniques: Decode the local part with int(x, 32) to get the injection time, the session (PID) and the order within the session. The same pid32 with close timestamps means one posting session, and the counter gives exact order even when subjects are random
Recognise server-generated IDs before applying client-tool Message-ID fingerprints
new_for_atlas: New. A decoder for a common server-side Message-ID format.

title: Olaf Titz's draft X-Trace protocol (inn-workers, July 2000): a comparable ctoken built from user or IP plus the top 16 bits of time
summary: The draft proposes 'X-Trace: <systemid> [:ctoken] [ntoken] (comment)', under 255 octets, where systemid must match the server's Path name. The ctoken (base64, prefixed with ':') exists so that outsiders can compare postings from one source: it is built from the client IP or authenticated user ID plus the upper 16 bits of Unix time, then encrypted or hashed, so it stays constant for one user for about a day and differs between users. The ntoken holds admin-only details such as exact time or PID. Gateways put base64(original Message-ID) as the first ctoken, and robots omit the ctoken. The draft was meant to replace INN's X-Trace, NNTP-Posting-Host/Date, X-Complaint-To and the '.POSTED' Path entries.
metadata_fields: X-Trace systemid (equal to the Path identity)
ctoken: ':'-prefixed base64; packed as 16-bit time + marker 0001 + user ID, or 16-bit time + marker 0010 + IPv4; for IPv6 the time replaces a zero 16-bit word
ntoken: base64, local-only data (exact time, PID)
comment: free text, may hold a complaint address
techniques: Where a server emits such a ctoken, equal ctokens link posts from one account or IP within the same 65,536-second (about 18.2 h) window of the top 16 time bits. Store them as opaque grouping keys
Base64-decode gateway ctokens to recover the original Message-IDs for loop and duplicate detection
new_for_atlas: New. Atlas does not keep X-Trace yet. Add it and parse systemid, ctoken and ntoken generically.

title: inn-workers, October 2011 (Hochstein): sites rewrite or scramble the IP inside INN's X-Trace with filter_nnrpd.pl
summary: INN sets X-Trace before nnrpd's Perl filter runs, so admins can replace the poster IP (the example regex puts 127.0.0.42 in place of the IPv4 address that comes just before ' ('), scramble it, or drop the header. INN's X-Trace value is therefore set by each server's policy, and its IP field cannot be trusted.
metadata_fields: INN X-Trace layout '<host> <unixtime> <pid> <ip> (<date>)', with the IP just before ' ('
techniques: Parse INN X-Trace, but treat the IP as untrusted. A placeholder value marks a server that sanitizes the header
Link articles from one session by host + PID + nearby times, not by IP
new_for_atlas: New rule for handling X-Trace.

title: news.software.readers thread (January 2008): how providers encode or hash X-Trace and posting-host
summary: The thread asks whether the encrypted X-Trace values that Giganews, AIOE, Motzarella and Google used to record the username or IP can be decoded. Replies say that professional providers hash an identifier that only their own logs can resolve, that albasani.net publishes its X-Trace encoding, and that Google Groups then put the poster's IP in plain NNTP-Posting-Host. One reply notes that if a provider hashes only the IP with no salt, the hash can be checked against hashes precomputed for candidate addresses.
metadata_fields: NNTP-Posting-Host (a plain IP at Google Groups then)
techniques: Classify each provider's trace field as a plain IP, an unsalted hash, or a salted or encrypted token, and use the last two only as opaque grouping keys
An unsalted hash of an IPv4 address comes from a space of only 2^32 values, so it is a pseudonym, not anonymity. Atlas should re-hash such values with a local secret and never expose them
new_for_atlas: New notes for provider-specific trace parsing and privacy handling.

title: Matroska schema (ebml_matroska.xml): attachments, ordered-chapter links to other segments, original file names, and tag targets
summary: The schema defines element IDs that the earlier Matroska finding did not cover: attachments (with a random FileUID per file), TrackEntry AttachmentLink, the Info elements SegmentFilename, PrevFilename and NextFilename, and chapter-level links to other segments. ChapterSegmentUUID 0x6E67 holds 'The SegmentUUID of another Segment to play during this chapter' and must not be the segment's own UUID. SegmentFamily 0x4444 is required when ChapterTranslate is present.
metadata_fields: Attachments 0x1941A469 / AttachedFile 0x61A7: FileDescription 0x467E, FileName 0x466E, FileMediaType 0x4660, FileData 0x465C, FileUID 0x46AE, FileReferral 0x4675, FileUsedStartTime 0x4661, FileUsedEndTime 0x4662
Info SegmentFilename 0x7384, PrevFilename 0x3C83AB, NextFilename 0x3E83BB, ChapterTranslate 0x6924 (ID 0x69A5, Codec 0x69BF, EditionUID 0x69FC)

Chapters: EditionUID 0x45BC, EditionFlagOrdered 0x45DD, ChapterUID 0x73C4, ChapterStringUID 0x5654, ChapterSegmentUUID 0x6E67, ChapterSegmentEditionUID 0x6EBC, ChapterSkipType 0x4588, ChapProcessPrivate 0x450D
Tag targets: TagTrackUID 0x63C5, TagEditionUID 0x63C9, TagChapterUID 0x63C4, TagAttachmentUID 0x63C6
techniques: Ordered chapters: a ChapterSegmentUUID that equals another file's SegmentUUID links the two files, for example an episode that plays a shared OP/ED file. Build a graph from these links to group the files of one release even when names are random
SegmentFilename, PrevFilename and NextFilename can hold the original file names, a direct source for deobfuscation when present
The attachment set (FileName + FileMediaType + size, plus FileUID) fingerprints a release: font sets point to a fansub group, and identical FileUIDs mean the same mux source
Hash each FileData (fonts, cover.jpg) to link releases from one group across different encodes
new_for_atlas: New. Atlas parses tracks and chapters, but not attachments, chapter links to other segments, or the filename elements.

title: Matroska attachments.md and subtitles.md: cover-art names, font attachments, and SSA/ASS headers stored in CodecPrivate
summary: Cover art SHOULD be JPEG or PNG named cover.(jpg|png) (600 px), small_cover (120 px on the smallest side), cover_land or small_cover_land; the names are case-sensitive. Fonts MAY be attached with the official font media types (font/sfnt, font/ttf and others) and are matched by font name and FileName. A subtitle track's AttachmentLink can limit which fonts it uses. cellar-codec/subtitles.md (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ietf-wg-cellar/matroska-specification/master/cellar-codec/subtitles.md) says that for SSA and ASS, 'All the headers, "[Script Info]" and the "[V4 Styles]"/"[V4+ Styles]" list, are stored in CodecPrivate'. Events go into Blocks as ReadOrder, Layer, Style, Name, MarginL, MarginR, MarginV, Effect, Text.
metadata_fields: font attachments (font/sfnt, font/ttf) and their font names
S_TEXT/ASS CodecPrivate = the [Script Info] and [V4+ Styles] text
techniques: Read the ASS header straight from CodecPrivate without demuxing any blocks. The [Script Info] fields and any extra header sections (see the Aegisub finding) are in the first article or two of the MKV
Cover names that break the convention, or extra attachments such as group logos, are group fingerprints
new_for_atlas: New.

title: Matroska official tag list (matroska_tags.xml): purchase, encoder and disc identifiers beyond IMDB/TMDB/TVDB
summary: Besides IMDB, TMDB, TVDB and TVDB2, the official tag names include purchase tags (PURCHASE_ITEM, PURCHASE_INFO, PURCHASE_OWNER, PURCHASE_PRICE, PURCHASE_CURRENCY, DATE_PURCHASED), tags about encoding and provenance (ENCODED_BY, ENCODER, ENCODER_SETTINGS, DATE_ENCODED, DATE_TAGGED, DATE_DIGITIZED, ORIGINAL_MEDIA_TYPE), physical-media IDs (MCDI, ISRC, BARCODE, CATALOG_NUMBER, LABEL_CODE, LCCN, ISBN) and multi-part tags (TOTAL_PARTS, PART_NUMBER, PART_OFFSET).
metadata_fields: PURCHASE_ITEM, PURCHASE_INFO, PURCHASE_OWNER, PURCHASE_PRICE, PURCHASE_CURRENCY, DATE_PURCHASED
ENCODED_BY, ENCODER, ENCODER_SETTINGS, DATE_ENCODED, DATE_TAGGED, DATE_DIGITIZED
MCDI (CD TOC), ISRC, BARCODE, CATALOG_NUMBER, LABEL_CODE, LCCN, ISBN
TOTAL_PARTS, PART_NUMBER, PART_OFFSET, COMMENT, URL, EMAIL
techniques: PURCHASE_OWNER and PURCHASE_ITEM are the Matroska equivalent of iTunes apID and purd and can link files to one buyer. Store them only as hashed keys
MCDI, ISRC, BARCODE and CATALOG_NUMBER identify the source disc; ENCODED_BY, URL and COMMENT often carry a group or site name
TOTAL_PARTS and PART_NUMBER group multi-part files
new_for_atlas: New tag names to extract.

title: Aegisub ASS writer: '; Script generated by Aegisub <version>' and the file paths in [Aegisub Project Garbage]
summary: On Save, Aegisub opens [Script Info] with '; Script generated by Aegisub <long version>' and '; http://www.aegisub.org/'. It then writes [Aegisub Project Garbage], right after Script Info and before the styles, holding Automation Scripts, Export Filters, Export Encoding, Last Style Storage, Audio File, Video File, Timecodes File, Keyframes File and Video AR Mode/Value, plus Video Zoom Percent, Scroll Position, Active Line and Video Position when UI state is saved. After the events comes [Aegisub Extradata] with lines 'Data: <id>,<key>,e<escaped>' or 'u<uuencoded>'. ExportFile leaves out both Project Garbage and Extradata.
metadata_fields: [Aegisub Project Garbage]: Audio File, Video File, Timecodes File, Keyframes File, Automation Scripts, Export Filters, Export Encoding, Last Style Storage, Video AR Mode/Value, Video Zoom Percent, Scroll Position, Active Line, Video Position
ass_parser.cpp also accepts 'Audio URI' and 'Aegisub Video Position' style keys
default new-file Script Info: Title 'Default Aegisub file', ScriptType v4.00+, YCbCr Matrix
techniques: Project Garbage is part of the header, so a loose .ass in a post, or MKV CodecPrivate if the muxer keeps extra header sections (not verified for mkvmerge), can carry 'Video File:' and 'Audio File:' entries. These name the subtitler's source video and audio, often a raw release name with its CRC, which makes them a strong signal for deobfuscation and for linking groups. Remove any local user-path parts before storing
The Aegisub version string, the Last Style Storage catalog name and the Automation Scripts list fingerprint a subbing team
Whether a file was saved (Project Garbage present) or exported (absent) is itself a workflow fingerprint
new_for_atlas: New. Atlas does not parse subtitle-track contents.

title: RFC 9639 FLAC: STREAMINFO audio MD5, the vendor string, CUESHEET and PICTURE
summary: STREAMINFO carries an 'MD5 checksum of the unencoded audio data': samples signed little-endian, interleaved, and sign-extended to whole bytes, with 0 meaning unknown. The VORBIS_COMMENT vendor string 'contains the name of the program that generated the file or stream'. CUESHEET holds a media catalog number (ASCII, padded to 128 bytes), a 12-character ISRC per track (12 NULs means none) and the CD-DA lead-in, and PICTURE holds the picture type, media type, description and dimensions. mutagen's flac.py (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/quodlibet/mutagen/main/mutagen/flac.py) parses these as StreamInfo.md5_signature, VCFLACDict, CueSheet and Picture.
metadata_fields: STREAMINFO: min/max block size, min/max frame size, sample rate, channels, bits per sample, total samples, MD5 of the audio
CUESHEET: media catalog number, lead-in samples, CD flag, and per track the offset, number, ISRC and indexes
PICTURE: type, media type, description, width, height, depth, colors, data
techniques: STREAMINFO MD5 together with total samples, sample rate and bit depth is a free audio-content key. It stays the same across re-encodes at other compression levels and across re-tagging, so it finds music alts: different FLAC bytes, same audio
The vendor string (libFLAC version) and the block layout fingerprint the encoder; the scene FLAC rules require the vendor string
CUESHEET MCN and ISRC identify the pressing
new_for_atlas: New. Atlas has no audio-format parsing.

title: mutagen mp3/_util.py: Xing/Info and LAME tag fields (music CRC, encoder delay and padding, preset) and VBRI
summary: XingHeader reads the 'Xing' or 'Info' (CBR) tag: frames, bytes, a 100-entry TOC, vbr_scale and the LAME version string. LAMEHeader reads vbr_method, lowpass, ReplayGain peak and gains, encoding flags, ATH type, bitrate, 12-bit encoder delay and padding, source rate, stereo mode, noise shaping, mp3_gain, surround, an 11-bit preset, a 32-bit music_length, music_crc ('CRC16 of the data specified by music_length') and header_crc. guess_settings maps these back to options such as '--preset standard' or '-V'. VBRIHeader parses the Fraunhofer tag.
metadata_fields: Xing/Info: frames, bytes, TOC, vbr_scale, lame_version string (e.g. 'LAME3.90 (alpha)')

LAME: vbr_method, lowpass_filter, track_peak, track/album gain + origin, encoding_flags, ath_type, bitrate, encoder_delay_start, encoder_padding_end, source_sample_frequency_enum, unwise_setting_used, stereo_mode, noise_shaping, mp3_gain, surround_info, preset_used, music_length, music_crc, header_crc
VBRI: bytes, frames, toc_scale_factor, toc_frames, TOC
techniques: music_crc with music_length is a hash of the audio frames written by the encoder. Equal values in files with different ID3 or APE tags identify the same encode, an MP3 twin that whole-file hashes miss
The LAME version, preset, lowpass and delay/padding fingerprint the ripper's settings, which scene MP3 groups keep consistent
An 'Info' tag means CBR and a 'Xing' tag means VBR or ABR
new_for_atlas: New.

title: EAC log signature (puddly/eac_logsigner, eac.py): how '==== Log checksum ... ====' is computed and checked
summary: EAC logs are UTF-16LE text whose first line is 'Exact Audio Copy V<x.y> [beta N] from <date>'. From V1.0 beta 1 they end with '==== Log checksum <64 hex> ===='. The checksum is Rijndael with a 256-bit block in CBC mode, a zero IV and a fixed public key (9378716c...efd9), run over the log text with CR, LF and BOMs removed, encoded UTF-16LE and zero-padded; the last cipher block is the signature.
metadata_fields: first line: Exact Audio Copy V<x.y> [beta N] from <date>
techniques: Check logs found in FLAC posts: a hand-edited log fails the checksum. Store the signature as an identity key for the log
The key is public, so a valid checksum only shows the log was not edited by hand. It does not prove the rip is genuine
new_for_atlas: New.

title: AniDB UDP API FILE command: look up a file by size + ed2k to get its anime, episode and release group
summary: 'FILE size={int8}&ed2k={str}&fmask={hex}&amask={hex}' (session key required) returns '220 FILE' with fid first and then the requested fields in mask order, or '320 NO SUCH FILE'. fmask covers aid, eid, gid, state, size, ed2k, md5, sha1, crc32, codecs, resolution, file type, dub and sub languages, length and the AniDB file name; amask covers the anime names, episode number and title, and the group name and short name. The state bits are FILE_CRCOK 1 ('matches official CRC'), FILE_CRCERR 2, ISV2 4, ISV3 8, ISV4 16, ISV5 32, UNC 64 and CEN 128.
metadata_fields: FILE by fid, by size+ed2k, or by anime + group + epno

fmask: aid, eid, gid, mylist id, other episodes, IsDeprecated, state, size, ed2k, md5, sha1, crc32, color depth, quality, source, audio codecs and bitrates, video codec, bitrate and resolution, file type, dub/sub language, length, description, aired date, anidb file name
amask: episode counts, year, type, related aids, names, epno, episode names, group name, group short name
state: CRCOK, CRCERR, V2-V5, uncensored, censored
techniques: For anime posts, compute the ed2k of each assembled file and query FILE with its size to get the group, anime and episode. This names obfuscated files exactly
The state bits give the version (v2-v5), censorship, and whether the file matches the official CRC (the [CRC32] commonly found in fansub file names)
Keep to the rate limits (one packet per 2 s short-term, per 4 s long-term; excess packets are dropped without notice) and cache the results
new_for_atlas: New external hash oracle for anime.

title: AniDB ed2k hash definition: MD4 over 9,728,000-byte chunks, with 'red' and 'blue' variants
summary: ed2k is computed by splitting the file into 9,728,000-byte chunks and taking the MD4 of each. A file of one chunk or less hashes to the MD4 of the whole file; otherwise the hash is the MD4 of the concatenated chunk MD4s. When the size is an exact multiple of 9,728,000 the two known methods differ (one appends the MD4 of empty data), and Avdump3 stores the second value as 'Alternative ed2k'.
metadata_fields: MD4 per chunk, then MD4 of the list of chunk hashes
an alternative value when the size is a multiple of the chunk size
techniques: Compute ed2k as a stream during assembly, alongside CRC32, MD5 and the OSO hash. Store both variants when the size is a multiple of 9,728,000
new_for_atlas: New hash for Atlas to compute.

title: AnimeTosho JSON feed: a torrent-NZB-AniDB bridge with per-file CRC32, MD5, SHA1, SHA256, ED2K and BitTorrent v2 hashes
summary: Each entry links a torrent (info_hash, info_hash_v2, magnet_uri, nyaa_id) to an AnimeTosho NZB (nzb_url) and to AniDB (anidb_aid, anidb_eid, anidb_fid). It carries total_size and num_files, and per file the filename, size, crc32, md5, sha1, sha256, ed2k, bt2, vidframe_timestamps and attachments (subtitle and font tracks with name, mime, codec, lang, default/forced flags and track number). The about page (https://animetosho.org/about/json) lists the RSS, ATOM and JSON feeds, a newznab/torznab api, and daily database exports at storage.animetosho.org/dbexport/.
metadata_fields: title, timestamp, status, is_dupe, deleted, nyaa_id, tosho_id, anidex_id
files[]: filename, size, crc32, md5, sha1, sha256, ed2k, bt2, is_archive, vidframe_timestamps, attachments[]{type, info{name, mime, codec, lang, default, enabled, forced, trackid, tracknum}}
techniques: Match Atlas's whole-file CRC32 (from yEnc or PAR2) or MD5 against AnimeTosho file hashes to name obfuscated anime posts and get AniDB ids, or use the daily exports to do this offline
Compare attachment lists (fonts, subtitle tracks) with MKV attachments to confirm alt versus twin
new_for_atlas: New external oracle.

title: 720p TV x264 Releasing Standards 2016 (scene rules): exact RAR volume sizes, naming, SFV/NFO, sample and MKV rules
summary: These rules have been mandatory since 2016-04-10. Releases must be RAR3 or RAR4 (RAR5 is not allowed), split into at most 101 volumes (.rar to .r99), with volume sizes in positive multiples of 50,000,000 bytes and at least 10 volumes before the next multiple is used. SFV and NFO are required, RAR, SFV and sample names must be unique and lower-case with the group tag, and compression, recovery records and encryption are banned; the archive must hold a single mkv. One 50-70 s sample goes in 'Sample/', cut from the final video. Other rules: x264 headers must stay intact, MKVToolnix is recommended, Matroska header compression is not allowed, and the rules list the permitted tags and directory formats.
metadata_fields: volume size (n x 50,000,000 bytes) and count (up to 101, .rar/.r00-.r99)
lower-case volume names with the group tag
SFV and NFO present; 'Sample' directory with a 50-70 s cut
x264 SEI intact; no MKV header compression
tags: PROPER, REPACK, INTERNAL, DIRFIX, NFOFIX, READNFO, RERIP, SAMPLEFIX, SOURCE.SAMPLE, and others
techniques: A scene-conformance score: volume sizes that are exact multiples of 50,000,000, .rNN naming, m0 storage, no recovery record, no encryption and one inner mkv strongly suggest an unmodified scene release. Inner size is roughly volumes x volume size, which can be checked against predb files and size
A sample that is a byte-exact cut of the main file (checkable through SRS) confirms the pair
Repacked uploads that break these rules (RAR5, 7z, recovery records, passwords) are re-wrapped alts, not twins of the scene release
new_for_atlas: New heuristics for classifying a post as an unmodified scene release.

title: Official.FLAC.Standard.Rules v3.0 (2016): proof JPG, compression level 8, vendor string required, empty PICTURE block
summary: Each release must contain an SFV, an NFO and a JPG proof, which rule 9.1 says must be a camera picture. CUE and LOG files are allowed for CD sources, and the valid file types are .cue .flac .jpg .log .m3u .nfo .sfv. Files must be encoded with --compression-level-8, should be encoded with --verify, and must not use ReplayGain; the vendor_string 'MUST be present indicating the correct lib FLAC version', the FLAC PICTURE block must be empty, and Vorbis fields must be unique, including TRACKNUMBER, ARTIST, TITLE, ALBUM, GENRE and DATE. File names must be lower-case and at most 128 characters, and REPACK/PROPER releases add -repack or -proper to every .flac.
metadata_fields: SFV, NFO, proof JPG, optional CUE/LOG/M3U
FLAC vendor string and compression level
techniques: Scene-FLAC test: a vendor string present, no embedded picture, lower-case track names, a proof JPG and SFV, and directory tags in the rule order
Proof JPGs carry camera EXIF (see the ExifTool finding), which links releases from one group's member. Use it as a hashed key only
new_for_atlas: New.

title: Real scene SFV headers: tool name, creation time, and per-file size and mtime comment lines (WIN-SFV32/QuickSFV)
summary: This SFV begins '; Generated by WIN-SFV32 v1.1a (QuickSFV v2.32 Compatibility Mode) on 2006-01-19 at 01:57:52' and '; http://www.QuickSFV.org'. A comment line gives each file's size, time and date (';       617971  00:19.50 2006-01-19 <file>') before the entry '<file> 54B6609E', and ';Q2-...' extension lines follow. Other SFVs in the same repository have headers from RekSFV v1.5.7 (with date and time), cSFV v1.40, Easy SFV Creator 2.7.0, WIN-SFV32 v1.0 with '(Compatible: Total Commander 7.01)', and the ioZS/ioFTPD zipscript; some have no header and lower-case CRCs. dariusiii/rarinfo SfvInfo.php keeps ';' lines as comments and matches entries with /^(.+?)\s+([[:xdigit:]]{2,8})$/.
metadata_fields: generation date and time in the header
per-file size and mtime in comment lines (WIN-SFV32/QuickSFV style)
techniques: Per-volume size and mtime lines plus the creation time are a packing-session fingerprint. They can be compared with RAR header mtimes and with the sizes of the posted files
The generator string and CRC case group a packer's output over time
Each volume CRC listed in the SFV can be matched with the whole-file CRC32 of each posted volume (yEnc crc32 or a CRC rebuilt from PAR2) to identify renamed scene volumes without opening them
new_for_atlas: New. Atlas does not parse SFV files.

title: TopClient and website-predb schemas: pre databases that keep full NFO/SFV/M3U/JPG copies and IRC announce provenance
summary: TopClient, a pre tool that saves NFO and SFV files from topsites, stores the full content and file name of each release's NFO, SFV, M3U, JPG and COVER. It also keeps Infos (Release_File count and Release_Size), ReleaseTime (name, time, section) and indexInCache (type, release, time, user, channel, bot, network), which records which IRC bot, channel and network announced each item. website-predb-master/table.sql (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/scriptzteam/SCENE-SCRiPTS/master/website-predb-master/table.sql) has releases(rlsname, grp, section, time, files TINYINT, size DECIMAL(7,2), genre), a matching spam table, and nukelog(rlsname, time, reason, network, status).
metadata_fields: NFO/SFV/M3U/JPG/COVER content and file names per release
announce provenance: bot, channel, network, user, time
predb: rlsname, grp, section, time, files, size (MB, 2 decimals), genre; nukelog reason and network
techniques: Index archived SFVs by volume CRC, so a post whose volumes are unchanged but renamed can be matched to a release through the whole-file CRC32 of each volume
Use files and size from predb (MB with 2 decimals) as tolerance windows when matching posts
Announce provenance (network and bot) gives a trust weight for pre data
new_for_atlas: New. A predb design that stores SFV and NFO content, which allows matching on volume CRCs.

title: pycdlib: ISO 9660 primary volume descriptor and UDF identifiers in disc-image posts
summary: The PVD is unpacked with '<B5sBB32s32sQLL32sHHHHHHLLLLLL34s128s128s128s128s37s37s37s17s17s17s17sBB512s653s' into the system identifier, volume identifier, space size, volume set identifier, publisher, data preparer and application identifiers, the copyright, abstract and bibliographic file identifiers, and the creation, modification, expiration and effective dates (17 bytes each). It also holds the file structure version and 512 bytes of application use. pycdlib/udf.py (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/clalancette/pycdlib/master/pycdlib/udf.py) shows that the UDF Primary Volume Descriptor carries vol_ident, vol_set_ident, recording_date, app_ident and impl_ident (EntityID '*<developer>'). It cites UDF 2.60 2.2.2.5: the first 16 characters of VolumeSetIdentifier should be unique, and the first 8 should be a time in ASCII hex. The domain identifier is '*OSTA UDF Compliant'.
