metadata_fields: ISO9660 PVD: system_identifier, volume_identifier, volume_set_identifier, publisher_identifier, preparer_identifier, application_identifier, copyright/abstract/bibliographic file ids, 4 volume dates, application_use
UDF: vol_ident, vol_set_ident (hex time + unique value), recording_date, app_ident, impl_ident ('*<tool>'), domain_ident '*OSTA UDF Compliant'
techniques: The UDF VolumeSetIdentifier is effectively a unique ID for each mastering run: the same value in two posts means the same image (twin), and the leading 8 hex digits give the mastering time
The application, preparer and implementation identifiers name the authoring tool, which fingerprints a group's ISO workflow
The PVD and UDF descriptors sit at fixed sectors near the start of the image (ISO 9660 at sector 16), so the first article or two of the ISO are enough
new_for_atlas: New. Atlas lists archive members but does not parse disc images.

title: FFmpeg movenc.c and L-SMASH: MP4 handler names, ©too and compressor-name strings that fingerprint the muxer
summary: FFmpeg writes hdlr descriptions VideoHandler, SoundHandler, SubtitleHandler, DataHandler, PictureHandler, HintHandler, TimeCodeHandler, ClosedCaptionHandler or 'GoPro MET'. When a 'handler_name' entry exists in the stream metadata it is copied instead, so handler names survive remuxes. ©too is set to LIBAVFORMAT_IDENT ('Lavf<version>'), or just 'Lavf' under bitexact, and the 32-byte compressorname comes from the stream's 'encoder' tag. L-SMASH (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/l-smash/l-smash/master/cli/muxer.c) writes 'L-SMASH Video Handler' and 'L-SMASH Audio Handler' and sets ©too to 'L-SMASH'.
metadata_fields: hdlr handler type and name string
visual sample entry compressorname (up to 31 characters)
techniques: Muxer fingerprint = handler-name set + ©too + compressorname + brands + box order. It separates ffmpeg, L-SMASH, mp4box and Apple-originated files even when the tags have been stripped
A handler name inherited from a source file (copied by FFmpeg) reveals the upstream muxer, for example a WEB-DL's original packager
new_for_atlas: New. Atlas parses MP4 tracks but not hdlr names, compressorname or brand-level fingerprints.

title: Gloe, Fischer, Kirchner: 'Forensic analysis of video file formats' (DFRWS EU 2014)
summary: The authors used custom parsers to extract the file-format structure of videos from 19 camera models, 14 phone models and 6 video-editing toolboxes, in AVI and MP4-like containers. They report 'considerable differences' in container choice, compression, acquisition parameters and internal file structure, enough to tell originals from post-processed files and to identify the device model or editing software.
techniques: Represent each MP4/AVI file by its container structure (box tree, order, field values) and cluster posts by producing software. This is an academic basis for the handler-name and ©too fingerprints
new_for_atlas: New. Only the abstract was available (no PDF link on the page).

title: x265 info SEI: 'x265 (build N) - <version>:<[OS][compiler][bits] bitdepth> ... options: ...'
summary: When bEmitInfoSEI is set, x265 writes a user-data-unregistered SEI containing 'x265 (build %d) - %s:%s - H.265/HEVC codec - Copyright 2013-2018 (c) Multicoreware, Inc - http://x265.org - options: %s'. The arguments are X265_BUILD, version_str, build_info_str and x265_param2string. In source/common/version.cpp (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/videolan/x265/master/source/common/version.cpp), build_info_str joins the OS ([Windows]/[Linux]/[Mac OS X]...), compiler ([GCC x.y.z]/[clang ...]/[MSVC ...]), bitness ([64 bit]), and asm, atomics, checked and bit-depth flags (8bit/10bit/12bit, +8bit/+10bit/+12bit).
metadata_fields: build_info_str: OS, compiler and version, bitness, bit depth
techniques: Parse the SEI from the first video NAL units, which are in the first article(s), the same way as for x264. The compiler/OS/build string identifies one encoding machine or build, a sharper group fingerprint than the options string alone
Matching option strings and frame counts across containers point to the same encode (an alt); a different build string with the same options suggests a different encoder
new_for_atlas: New for HEVC. The x264 SEI was covered earlier, but the x265 build-info fields were not.

title: Newznab API specification (nZEDb docs): standard newznab:attr names, including password and prematch semantics
summary: Section 4.1 lists attributes such as size and category (always present), files, poster (e.g. 'yenc@power-post'), group ('a.b.warez, a.b.teevee'), team, grabs, password ('0' no, '1' rar pass, '2' contains inner archive), comments, usenetdate, info (NFO URL), year and prematch ('0' no, '1' yes). For TV, movies, audio and anime it adds season, episode, tvdbid, rageid, anidbid, imdb, video, audio, resolution, framerate, language, subs and genre.
metadata_fields: size, category, files, poster, group, team, grabs, password (0/1/2), comments, usenetdate, info, year, prematch
season, episode, tvdbid, rageid, anidbid, imdb, video, audio, resolution, framerate, language, subs, genre
techniques: Expose the results of correlation through standard attributes: prematch for a predb-confirmed name, password=2 for a nested archive, and files and size checked against predb
new_for_atlas: Mostly nothing new, since Atlas is a newznab-tmux port. It confirms the password=2 'contains inner archive' meaning and the prematch flag.

title: RFC 2231: MIME parameter continuations and charset encoding (filename*0*=...) for attachment-style binaries
summary: Parameter values can be split into numbered sections name*0, name*1 and so on, with no gaps or leading zeros. A trailing '*' means the value is percent-encoded with charset and language (name*=charset'lang'value), and the two can be combined (title*0*=us-ascii'en'...; title*1*=...; title*2="..."). Older MIME binary posts carry their real file name in Content-Type name= or Content-Disposition filename= this way.
metadata_fields: charset and language in extended values
techniques: Join the sections in numeric order and percent-decode the '*' sections with the declared charset before applying filename or obfuscation regexes to MIME-attachment posts
This complements RFC 2047 encoded-words in Subject
new_for_atlas: New for MIME and base64 attachment posts. The earlier RFC 2045-2047 finding did not cover parameter continuations.

title: ExifTool EXIF tag table: camera identity and time fields in proof JPGs and cover images
summary: EXIF has these identity and time tags: Make 0x010f, Model 0x0110, Software 0x0131, Artist 0x013b, Copyright 0x8298, HostComputer 0x013c, DateTimeOriginal 0x9003 with OffsetTimeOriginal 0x9011 and SubSecTimeOriginal 0x9291, ImageUniqueID 0xa420, OwnerName 0xa430, SerialNumber (BodySerialNumber) 0xa431, LensMake 0xa433, LensModel 0xa434, LensSerialNumber 0xa435, GPSInfo 0x8825, and the embedded thumbnail at ThumbnailOffset 0x0201 / ThumbnailLength 0x0202.
metadata_fields: Make, Model, Software, Artist, Copyright, HostComputer
techniques: Scene FLAC rules require a camera proof JPG, so the body serial, lens serial, model and OwnerName repeat across one group's releases and can group them. Store these only as salted hashes and never expose them
Software and HostComputer on covers or screenshots fingerprint the editing tool
OffsetTimeOriginal gives the time zone of the photographer
new_for_atlas: New. Atlas does not read image metadata from proof, cover or screenshot files.
